item.title: Florence Pugh’s Best Red Carpet Moments Are Bold and Unexpected
item.description: We're taking a look back at the star's riskiest style moments over the years, from 'Don’t Worry Darling' to 'East of Eden'.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Twersky Winkler
item.content:encoded:
Florence Pugh’s rise in Hollywood happened quickly—like “blink and you’ll miss it” fast. All of a sudden, she was the hottest actor on the scene thanks to Midsommar, and she expertly followed the hit indie up with her Oscar-nominated performance in Little Women. Overnight, Pugh became the one to watch, both on the screen and on the red carpet. The actor quickly made it clear that she wasn’t willing to play by conventional style rules, often opting for unique silhouettes, bright colors, and otherworldly hairstyles to match. Because of this, some of her looks often cause debate, but they always start a conversation (people still talk about the sheer dress she wore to the Valentino couture show back in 2022).

If Pugh has proven anything, it’s that she’s always going to be unapologetically herself, and we wouldn’t want it any other way. Often working with stylist Rebecca Corbin-Murray, the actor loves to embody old Hollywood glamour and has often done so in frothy Valentino confections. Still, she also explores more modern looks through Rodarte, Miu Miu, and Harris Reed, among others.

Here, take a look back at Pugh’s best red carpet moments over the years.

2026: Governors Awards

Pugh delivered full mermaid glamour in a custom Valentino gown with a ruffled, floor-grazing train.

2026: In The Shadows Screening at BFI London Film Festival

Pugh wore a glistening lavender gown from Wiederhoeft’s spring 2027 runway to the premiere of In The Shadows—which stars her new boyfriend, Finn Cole.

2026: Jaguar Event in New York City

After a string of period-inspired ensembles to promote East of Eden, Pugh changed her aesthetic up to attend an event as Jaguar’s inaugural brand ambassador. For the occasion, she traded tight corsetry for a modern LBD by Patrick McDowell.

2026: East of Eden New York City Event

Pugh wore a sculptural ballgown—complete with an ornate bustle—from Erdem’s resort 2027 collection.

2026: East of Eden London Screening

The star served gothic glamour in a billowing black Rodarte gown.

2026: East of Eden Photocall

A ruffled Victorian collar with a touch of logomania—this archival Rodarte set delivered just the right amount of drama to match Pugh’s role in the 19th-century East of Eden series.

2026: East of Eden Screening in Beverly Hills

Pugh put a skin-baring twist on period dressing in this butter yellow Rodarte skirt set.

2026: Emmys

This Vivienne Westwood corset dress—with tulle overlay and a long train—proved to be the perfect punk pick for the 2026 Emmys.

2026: Spider-Man: Brand New Day UK Premiere

Pugh played with proportions in this Tamara Ralph couture gown, featuring an exaggerated off-the-shoulder silhouette and dangling fringe.

2026: Netflix Upfront Red Carpet

The actor leaned into Simone Rocha’s classic femininity in a floor-grazing white gown embellished with an oversized poppy motif.

2025: Coach Party

Pugh proved business casual can be party-appropriate when she wore a pinstripe pantsuit (exposed bra included) to a Coach party in London.

2025: Thunderbolts* New York Premiere

The actor embraced the cut-out look at the Thunderbolts* New York premiere in a daring Loewe look.

2025: Thunderbolts* L.A. Premiere

At the Thunderbolts* L.A. premiere, Pugh slipped into a ruffled McQueen look from the brand’s fall 2025 runway.

2025: Thunderbolts* London Premiere

The star slipped into a dramatic Elie Saab look at the Thunderbolts* London premiere which elevated her signature naked look in all the right ways.

2024: Academy Awards

Pugh’s 2024 Oscars dress, a custom stunner from Del Core, featured sculptural straps and sheer beadwork.

2024: Dune: Part Two NYC Premiere

Pugh looked like a sci-fi goddess in this Grecian Valentino stunner at the 2024 premiere of Dune in New York City.

2024: BAFTA Awards

For the 2024 BAFTA Awards in London, Pugh tapped one of the city’s boldest designers, Harris Reed, to create this silver and black gown.

2024: Dune: Part Two World Premiere

Pugh proved the power of a plunging neckline (and lots of the sequins) with this hooded Valentino look.

2024: Dune: Part Two Photo Call

The actor paired disco diva sandal heels with a one-shoulder Maticevski jumpsuit during a Dune photo call.

2024: Dune: Part Two Mexico City Premiere

Pugh tapped emerging London label Standing Ground for a Dune: Part Two event in Mexico City.

2024: Governors Awards

During the 2024 Governors Awards, Pugh glistened in pastel pink Rodarte.

2024: Golden Globe Awards

Pugh returned to familiar fashion territory (sheer Valentino) for the 2024 Golden Globe Awards.

2023: Business of Fashion 500 Gala

One has to imagine that when Pugh meets with Pierpaolo Piccioli to choose a gown for an event, she has three major requirements on her checklist: sheer fabric, lots of skin, and an extra piece that she can swing in to the air on the red carpet. Luckily for her, this Valentino fall 2023 dress hit all the marks.

2023: Elle Style Awards

Pugh looked ready to walk down the aisle in this sheer, white lace Alexander McQueen resort 2024 dress.

2023: Oppenheimer Premiere

If this Valentino fall 2023 haute couture dress looks familiar, it’s because Pugh wore a very similar one—also designed by Piccioli—to the BoF gala just two months after the Oppenheimer premiere.

2023: Met Gala

Pugh tapped Piccioli to design a Valentino dress for the actor to wear to the Met Gala. She even took the opportunity of her shaved head (which she buzzed for her upcoming film, We Live in Time), to top the look with a black, feathered headpiece.

2023: The Landmark at Tiffany & Co 5th Avenue Opening

Pugh channeled Michele Pfeiffer in Scarface in a mint green, off-the-shoulder Valentino dress.

2023: Academy Awards

A year after Kristen Stewart brought short shorts to the Oscars, Pugh followed suit, attending the awards in a pair of cropped bottoms with a voluminous topper from Valentino’s spring 2023 haute couture collection.

2023: Vanity Fair Oscar Party

When it came time for the after-party, Pugh traded in her shorts for pants and added a pink opera coat, also courtesy of Valentino.

2023: A Good Person Premiere

At the premiere of her film, A Good Person, she wore an outfit from Erdem’s pre-fall 2023 collection, featuring gray trousers and an embroidered, sleeveless top with dramatic gloves.

2023: BAFTA Film Awards

Pugh tapped her fellow Brit Harris Reed to design this bright orange, pleated Nina Ricci gown for the actor to wear to the 2023 BAFTAs.

2023: London Critics’ Circle Film Awards

The actor proved that peplums are making a comeback with the help of a bright red Robert Wun spring 2023 couture dress at the 2023 London Critics’ Circle Film Awards.

2022: The Fashion Awards

Pugh wore a bright red, backless Valentino gown to the British Fashion Council’s Fashion Awards, where she walked the red carpet with Pierpaolo Piccioli.

2022: British Independent Film Awards

The actor went full boudoir when she wore a Rodarte fall 2022 pale pink slip dress with a tulle overcoat to the 25th British Independent Film Awards in December 2022.

2022: Governors Awards

Pugh loves a sheer dress, so this Victoria Beckham spring 2023 number at the 2022 Governors Awards was an obvious choice.

2022: The Wonder Premiere

When in doubt, Pugh always turns to Valentino, which explains this pale peach dress with a ruched bodice and feathered hem at the premiere of The Wonder at the 66th BFI London Film Festival in October.

2022: Don’t Worry Darling Premiere

There was so much drama at the premiere of Don’t Worry Darling at the Venice Film Festival, one could have easily missed Pugh’s look. Luckily, the actor managed to stand out when she opted to wear an off-the-shoulder Valentino fall 2022 haute couture dress that demanded attention.

2022: BAFTA Awards

Pugh’s tailored black Carolina Herrera pre-fall 2022 jacket dress was made red-carpet-ready with the addition of the pink tulle bow on the back.

2021: Black Widow Premiere

This black silk Miu Miu set paired with purple dip-dyed hair made for the perfect premiere look for an action film like Black Widow.

2020: Academy Awards

Pugh celebrated her first-ever Oscar nomination in a teal, tiered Louis Vuitton dress with a belted waist and asymmetric hem.

2020: Vanity Fair Oscar Party

Following the 2020 Oscars, Pugh changed into a slinky, low-cut dress, also by Louis Vuitton.

2020: BAFTA Awards

This Dries van Noten look from his Christian Lacroix collaborative spring 2020 collection at that year’s BAFTAs was definitely a risk, but the simple styling helped Pugh pull it off.

2020: Critics' Choice Awards

Pugh turned up the glam factor at the 25th annual Critics' Choice Awards with the help of this silver paillette-adorned Prada dress.

2019: Little Women New York Premiere

For the big premiere of her breakout movie, Pugh opted for this off-the-shoulder Valentino fall 2019 haute couture mini dress with a side train.

2019: Governors Awards

Pugh wore this purple confection of a dress by one of her go-to fashion houses, Valentino, for the 11th annual Governors Awards.

2019: Cannes Film Festival

Pugh wore this low-cut Schiaparelli gown with floral embellishments to the premiere of Le Belle Epoque at the Cannes Film Festival in 2019.

2018: The Little Drummer Girl Premiere

The actor went casual for the premiere of The Little Drummer Girl, pairing a lace and floral Chloé resort 2019 dress with knee-high brown leather boots.

2018: BAFTA Awards

Pugh wore a sleeveless, embellished Miu Miu dress to the 2018 BAFTAs.

2018: London Film Critics Circle Awards

The actor went for a very romantic look for the London Film Critics Circle Awards in 2018, wearing a sheer, Sandra Mansour dress covered in script and finished with ruffled sleeves. She then paired the dress with velvet accessories and a bold red lip.

2017: British Independent Film Awards

A brunette Pugh wore an army green pleated Miu Miu dress to the British Independent Film Awards in 2017.

2015: BFI London Film Festival Awards

A 19-year-old Pugh wore a little black dress with an off-the-shoulder neckline and a fishtail braid to the BFI London Film Festival Awards in 2015.

item.title: Nicola Coughlan & Simone Ashley Snuck Away From Bridgerton For Swanky London
item.description: Nicola Coughlan & Simone Ashley snuck away from 'Bridgerton' to hangout with Selena Gomez.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
No, it wasn’t a Bridgerton promotional event. It was the premiere of Only Murders in London, the sixth season of Only Murders in the Building. And yet, two of the Ton’s most beloved leading ladies—Nicola Coughlan and Simone Ashley—reunited on the red carpet anyway. For the occasion, they ditched the period garb, but instead dressed entirely as themselves.

Staying true to her penchant for princess-gown drama, a 39-year-old Coughlan hit the red carpet in a look from Richard Quinn’s fall 2026 collection. The floor-trailing gown did have hints of historical codes, but they were reworked for modern times. Styled by Aimée Croysdill, her corseted bodice featured a subtle peplum silhouette and a plunging scoop neckline that revealed a structured white brasierre. With dark, dangling crystals lining the piece, it delivered the regal dressing that Coughlan is known for.

Next to her, Ashley struck a satisfying contrast with an opposite silhouette. The 31-year-old vintage-lover looked undeniably herself in a high-neck minidress, not from a recent runway, but instead pulled from Gucci’s early-aughts archives. Her ombré dress, designed by Tom Ford for spring 2003, had not even a whisper of Regency-era England. Instead, it was Japanese-inspired, complete with intricate embroideries of cherry blossoms and birds. Styled by Rebecca Corbin-Murray, it was an unmistakable ode to Y2K. She even wore the same metallic peep-toe pumps that first appeared on the runway.

While they’re best known for co-starring on the Netflix bodice ripper, the actors are reuniting for guest-starring stints alongside Selena Gomez and her friends on Only Murders in London. Set in the British capital, the newest season of the Emmy-winning mystery series finds Coughlan playing an imprisoned woman suspected of murdering a royal. The details of Ashley’s role have yet to be revealed, so we’ll have to wait until it premieres on December 8 to find out. We can only hope they’ll share a few scenes.

Bridgerton season 5 will premier next year. Filming for that wrapped in October. Clearly, spending so much time with a colleague makes for a certain red-carpet synchronicity—even when your outfits are polar opposites.

item.title: Inside III Points, America’s Wettest, Wildest, and Weirdest Music Festival
item.description: Where else would Lil' Kim and Sunn O))) share a bill?
item.dc:creator: Kyle Munzenrieder
item.content:encoded:
For better or worse, one of the best observations about the city of Miami came from “Mama” Elsa Patton, an alleged witch who appeared on an early season of The Real Housewives of Miami. “People love Miami, but they don’t love it because it’s a fun place,” she once said. “They love it because it’s a very odd place.” Unsaid, but implied, is that the reason it’s so fun is because it’s very odd. It is, after all, one of three points that make up the Bermuda Triangle. The III Points Music Festival seems to prove that thesis better than almost any of the city’s other annual events.

Held in the Wynwood neighborhood, the festival boasts an eclectic lineup almost unimaginable at any other major American music festival. This year it mixed ’90s rap icons (Lil’ Kim, Bone Thugs-n-Harmony), deep dance-floor legends (Honey Dijon, Underworld, Four Tet), buzzy indie bands (Chanel Beads, Connan Mockasin), and an expertly curated list of up-and-coming Gen Z-beloved genre-blending music weirdos (Nettspend, Jane Remover, horsegiirL, Bassvictim, et al.), with legendary Seattle drone band Sunn O))) thrown in for good measure.

It’s a bit of a choose-your-own-adventure lineup, in which you could spend your time moving from stage to stage, hitting up the legacy acts, sticking to the dance stages for a full-on outdoor rave experience, or scuttling around the smaller stages to check out all the bands that are sure to up your indie cred. The best course of action, of course, is to attempt to do all three over the two-day festival. This year, that meant listening to a leather Muir cap-clad Lil’ Kim spit classic lines like “Black Barbie dressed in BVLGARI / I’m tryin’ to leave in somebody’s Ferrari” at one stage, dancing to a remix of Trick Daddy and Trina’s “Nann” inside a giant metal cage contraption at the next, and watching the girls of MGNA Crrrta thrash around on stage with bubble guns to end the night.

This year’s edition was humid with a few disruptions from the rain, and yet, Miamians always know how to deliver a look, even when they’re not working with much fabric. Even drenched in rain and sweat, you can still tell the difference between a club-land baddie, an artsy cool kid, and a goth raver.

“The outfits at III Points always blow my mind. There were so many cool costumes, and horsegiirL fans always dress up,” said photographer Mark Hunter, AKA The Cobrasnake, who captured the photos here. “The crowd’s style is incredibly diverse, ranging from ravers to rockstars and everything in between. You can truly be whatever version of yourself at III Points. It's wet, wild, and Miami really brings the heat.”

item.title: November Horoscope: The 6 Zodiac Signs Getting a Fresh Start With the Gemini Full Moon
item.description: On November 24, prepare for a subconscious and emotional exploration that'll clear away the cobwebs in your life.
item.dc:creator: Cole Prots
item.content:encoded:
Another lunar cycle peaks with the glorious moon glowing overhead. The Gemini full moon on November 24 is called the “beaver full moon” because, like beavers, we are building our safe havens for the cold season. The last full moon of autumn comes in swinging, stimulating your mind, opening your eyes, and jolting your nervous system. Fear not, friend; sometimes a good ol’ spiritual shake-up is just what you need to clear away stale energy and ignite growth.

While the moon draws us inward to our subconscious and emotional core, this full moon weaves a thread between the head and the heart. Gemini tends to be one of the less touchy-feely types of the zodiac, so expect some mental gymnastics as you navigate newfound awareness and acceptance of the world around you. The beauty of the yearly Gemini full moon is that it offers perspective. How does each piece of the puzzle play an important role in the picture you are trying to build? Things might start to click around the full moon, giving you a stronger understanding of the fragmented visions with which you’ve been wrestling. Because Sagittarius season is just starting, you must strike a balance between reaching for broader horizons and appreciating where you are in the present moment—that’s crucial to making the most of this full moon.

That said, the full moon might feel like the world around you goes from zero to 100 in the blink of an eye. What’s been lurking in the shadows of your subconscious might pour out all at once; a leaky faucet could suddenly become a burst pipe. This kind of rush can show up internally and externally. A new idea or a refreshed perspective could feel like it needs tending with adolescent-like impulsivity. Or some new bit (or likely many bits) of information has you feeling like you’re at system overload—inundated with stimuli and unsure of which thing to tackle first. Regardless of the information revealing itself, what does it show about where you are, where you’d like to go, and what you need to work with regularly to get there?

The full moon is also heavily influenced by Uranus and Pluto. These two powerhouses have been in close aspect all year; much of the overwhelming information and shifts in social dynamics are largely because of them. Ideas, conversations, and routine workings that would normally hide in the shadows have been exposed, and this full moon is another checkpoint where they could become even more obvious. However, with support from Neptune and Saturn to the sun, awareness of what might be seeping through the cracks could come sooner than the full moon’s peak. Catch it quickly: like a tea kettle that is about to overflow, pay attention to what in your mind and heart has been heating up and might boil over before you know it.

As downloads come to you, take time to chew on them so you can understand what they mean for the larger story of your life. Focus on what they reveal about communication, information processing, getting lost in the weeds, or fixating solely on the destination. While it may be a lot to digest, this full moon promises insights that will help you find your way out of the dense thicket and carve a clearer path forward.

The full moon culminates the intentions set six months ago during the Gemini new moon. So while you reflect, consider what’s come to fruition over that time. As with all full moons, this increased awareness makes it a beautiful time to cleanse your mental and material spaces. The Gemini full moon is lively, so focus on rituals and routines that ease your mind. Let the rising-sign horoscopes below guide your reflection, and happy full moon!

Aries

Has daily life become too mundane? Are you going through the motions or making intentional choices? Boredom and burnout are likely your biggest hurdles right now. It seems contradictory, but any Gemini transit has a bit of that duality. What in your everyday life is causing your mind to race, either toward solutions or escape paths? The Gemini full moon is a perfect moment to work in your mental spaces and better understand what controls your attention. Who knows, maybe you’ll find a greater appreciation for something you often take for granted.

Taurus

How has your inner dialogue established the precedents for how you see yourself? What about the things you value says something about who you are? The Gemini full moon will likely take on a dual material-and-mental quality for you, and ideally, it will help you better understand your resources as a reflection of your self-worth. Are material things weighing heavily on your sense of self? Take time to reflect on all the pieces of you and the inner narratives that construct your self-portrait.

Gemini

What is the person looking back at you in the mirror telling you about what you’ve overcome, especially in the past six months? How does your personal growth show up in your self-talk, the parts of yourself you fixate on, and the decisions you make? During this full moon, you have an amazing opportunity to reconnect with yourself. Take the time to explore the nuances of how you speak to yourself: are you combing through the weeds of your mind with a fine-tooth comb, or glazing over the narratives like a student rushing through last night’s reading? The Gemini full moon offers you the chance to shine a light on the parts of yourself that are easy to celebrate, and to appreciate the parts you’ve been conditioned to reject.

Cancer

If you were to storyboard your dreams, what would you tell the main character to do? How would you advise them to keep the faith and carry on? Take your time with this full moon; a lot of energizing vibes are at play, but the slower you move, the clearer the picture will become. While the destination may be hazy, you can still use your past experiences to navigate the unknown right now. Focus your gaze on what is directly in front of you, and once you’ve got a clear vision of that, shift your attention. One step at a time, and a little faith in the unknown will go a long way.

Leo

Have the webs of your social circle woven into a snare that traps you, or a beautiful masterpiece that captures the beauty of the dewy sunrise? Who is the master of whispers in your life? Lately, your relationship with relationships has shifted, and this full moon is illuminating the bigger picture of what belonging truly means to you. Perhaps you’re evolving beyond surface-level interactions, or realizing that the smaller relations building your personal world aren’t in sync. The Gemini full moon gives you a chance to see the bigger picture of what you want from connection, while also pushing past the hazy convenience of proximity.

Virgo

How have your goals changed, and how has your understanding of what is worth working with day in and day out evolved? Have you been putting too much attention on things that don’t serve your ultimate destination? Now is the time to strike a balance between your inner and outer worlds, and something outside of you will likely spark to remind you to listen to your intuition. A professional opportunity may ask you to rise to the challenge, or a missed connection could remind you of a subconscious pull to shift your focus. The Gemini full moon offers you a chance to refresh your approach, let goals you don’t want on your CV fade, and allows you to start chipping away at something that satisfies both your internal and external sense of fulfillment.

Libra

What are you realizing you didn’t know? Has a belief system or notion you’ve held as true been challenged recently? An a ha, lightbulb-over-the-head, spiritual awakening moment is happening in your life right now. It could be something from your everyday life that you typically gloss over but it gives you a double-take, or it could be a metaphorical boulder you smack into on your journey through life. What does this new piece of information, or desire to expand your perspective, mean for your personal philosophy on life? The Gemini full moon is a chance to broaden your horizons, so avoid assuming you know the answers, and give yourself the chance to step outside your known limits.

Scorpio

What idea, notion, or inner conversation are you struggling to release? Is something from your past—perhaps a skeleton in the closet or a grudge for which you never sought closure—starting to spill over? This baggage feels heavy right now, and you may be inclined to rip off the Band-Aid to get it over with. Think about what you can say or do to build a more trusting, intimate relationship with yourself and those around you. If you are going to make a change, change the way you share what is going on behind the scenes.

Sagittarius

Who inspires you and who irritates you? Imagine you were locked in an elevator with everyone in your life; go through them, one at a time—who would make you think “It could be worse” and who would make you think “Oh, this is the worst”? Right now, there is a push to pack your bags, change your name, leave a cryptic message to only those who need to know. However, this urge likely comes from a part of you that wants to gloss over the fact that, with a little effort, you could change the whole dynamic. This is where the small details matter, because small interactions reinforce the bigger boundaries and expectations. The Gemini full moon will bring relationships to a peak, so trust yourself to recognize which ones honor you and which you can lay to rest.

Capricorn

The Gemini full moon spotlights your health, work, and routines, but it might feel like the spotlight is jumping from one thing to the next without rhyme or reason. What feels static in your daily life? Has an activity or part of your routine made you feel extra frustration or even boredom? During this full moon, a “screen time” audit for every facet of your day will likely do you good. When you break it down and crunch the numbers, what is occupying your time, and does it align with the fantastic vision you have of yourself? Take this moment to start adjusting how you move and what you prioritize.

Aquarius

What is piquing your interest and stirring a burst of inspiration right now? Is there someone or something that has your heart pitter-pattering, making you excited to step out of your comfort zone? You dance between the revolutionary and the refined, willing and able to explore the unknown while also appreciating the tried-and-true. The Gemini full moon is a chance to reconnect with the dimly lit sparks of joy in your life; find new ways to fan that flame. Raise the vibration through activity—song, dance, sport, sex, you name it. As long as it’s pleasure-based, you’ll find a way to keep hope alive and stay connected to happiness.

Pisces

How often do you move through your home? While it might look appealing at first glance, have you properly dusted off the most sacred space in your life? Right now, you are likely feeling a mix of anxiety and fatigue. Focusing on the big picture may have caused you to lose sight of the nervous-system regulation you need right now. That said, consider how you use your time to rest and recharge. During the Gemini full moon, you might find yourself focusing on your inner world—use your emotional body to inspire a rational approach to bettering yourself. It wouldn’t hurt to look at the four walls where you rest your head every night and give them a little more TLC.

item.title: Olivia Dean's Holiday Dress Code Is Merry & Bright
item.description: The singer kicked off the festive season in a bold Burberry look reminiscent of a colorful Christmas ornament.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
While some stars prefer to ease into the holiday season with après-worthy furs and slinky velvet separates, Olivia Dean is going all in on glitz. Yesterday, the neo-soul singer and ascending fashion It girl toasted to Burberry’s extravagant new Christmas tree dressed like a very own opulent ornaments.

For the unveiling of the British brand’s intricately decorated tree at the Victoria & Albert Museum in London, the 27-year-old songwriter and Burberry ambassador wore a festive ensemble fresh from the 2027 runway. Her chocolate brown coat gave the classic check trench an eveningwear spin, while her glossy nude slingbacks added modern polish. But the main event was her subtly reflective slip dress. Adorned with 3D floral appliqués, it caused the exquisite tree behind her to shine even brighter.

Created in collaboration with chief creative officer Daniel Lee and British artist Ann Carrington in celebration of Burberry’s 170th anniversary, the tree is in and of itself a piece of art. The 16-foot installation is decorated entirely with scrap metal—like cookie tin lids, trinket dishes, and silver trays—which have been transformed into bright steel bows and ribbons. Of all last night’s attendees—including Helena Bonham Carter and Tish Weinstock—Dean’s look was decidedly the most on-theme. We’d expect nothing less from the singer and her stylist Simone Beyene, who have crafted a specific fun-filled aesthetic in recent years.

It’s a particularly celebratory time of year for the superstar, who received six Grammy nominations earlier this month. After winning Best New Artist at the 2026 Grammys, her sophomore album The Art of Loving is now up for Album of the Year, while her hit “Man I Need” is in the running for Song of the Year. Final round voting takes place from December 10 to January 7, so breaking out a bold look here and there only serves as another reminder to voters of her star power. ’Tis the season for more-is-more dressing, especially when there’s a Grammys race involved.

item.title: Art Basel Miami Beach 2026: All the Must-See Exhibitions, Events & Activations
item.description: Blue-chip galleries, black-card holders, and lots and lots of colorful art.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Munzenrieder
item.content:encoded:
Billions of dollars’ worth of art, millions of glasses of champagne, and thousands of events: It’s time for Art Basel Miami Beach once again. The world’s blue-chip art galleries and black-card holders descend on the neon-tinged town for the annual bacchanal. With a seemingly limitless number of late-night parties, tony brunches, brand activations, and art exhibitions, there are more missions and sidequests available to fairgoers than in all of Miami Beach’s video-game doppelgänger Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. So here’s a guide to ensure you don’t miss out on any of the good stuff (for maximum efficiency, just be sure to consult the weather app, Waze, and your bank account, too).

Art Basel Miami Beach

The Miami Beach Convention Center; visiting information here.

Entering the Miami Beach Convention Center for Art Basel 2026 might feel different compared to past years. In an effort to make the venue appear less like a labyrinth, the fair has rejiggered its physical configuration: while the overall floor plan will shrink by about 12 percent, individual booths will be given more room to breathe. Notably, the mega-galleries that were grouped together in the center of the fair will now be scattered throughout the layout, hopefully leading to more discovery. Here, booths you can certainly mark on your map.

Travesía Cuatro—Traveling & Inhabiting the Moon

With space tourism on the verge of becoming a reality, Madrid’s Travesía Cuatro presents a selection of works exploring the moon as both a destination and a symbolic fantasyscape. Works include Álvaro Urbano’s imagined lunar plants, moon landscapes by Friedrich Kunath and Eleonore Koch, and pieces by Jorge Eielson, the Peruvian conceptual artist who once dreamed of working with NASA to send both his sculptures and his own ashes to space.

Mariposa—Peter Berlin’s Double Exposures

Peter Berlin is like the artistic godfather of the modern thirst trap. Mariposa, making its ABMB debut, will present handpainted photographs and silver gelatin prints from the artist, which haven’t been displayed publicly for 40 years. Photographing himself using double exposure, the gallery notes that the works create “a psychological theater of narcissism, fantasy, and self-invention.”

Lehmann Maupin

Celebrating its 30th anniversary, Manhattan gallery Lehmann Maupin is taking a victory lap by displaying several of its artists who have major current or upcoming museum placements. Hernan Bas is the subject of a retrospective at Miami’s Rubell Museum, Do Ho Suh will have a solo exhibition at the Guggenheim next year, and Alex Prager will present at Crystal Bridges in 2027.

Spinello Projects—I Could See the Water at the Edge of All Things

The Miami-based gallery’s booths are always a must-see. This year, Spinello presents five local artists whose works are tied together by the same shade of dark blue. Naturally, the booth walls will be painted in the matching hue.

DC Moore Gallery—Joyce Kozloff’s Patterns of Desire: Pornament is Crime (1987–89)

In the Kabinett section, DC Moore will present a selection of Kozloff’s rarely seen watercolor paintings, which juxtapose the aesthetics of historic hand-drawn pornography against classic ornamental motifs.

Zero 10

The section of the fair dedicated to digital art returns this year with its biggest selection yet. Artists include Jon Rafman, Refik Anadol, and Sarah Meyohas. Within, The Institute for Studies on Latin American Art will present ARTE Y CIBERNÉTICA, a survey of early Latin American digital art.

The Best of the Rest

Design Miami

Convention Center Drive & 19th Street, Miami Beach; visiting information here.

After a stint across the bay, Design Miami returns to Miami Beach (and is just walking distance from ABMB) for its 22nd edition.

NADA

1400 North Miami Avenue, Miami; visiting information here.

With 130 participating galleries, the New Art Dealers Alliance takes over Miami’s Ice Palace Studios.

Untitled Art, Miami Beach

Ocean Drive and 12th Street, Miami Beach; visiting information here.

Set in a tent directly on South Beach, Untitled is a small but mighty fair full of young galleries.

Museum and Institution Shows

Carroll Dunham

ICA Miami, 61 NE 41st Street, Miami, 33137

The simply named show will be the first museum survey of Carroll Dunham’s works for the first time in 25 years.

Basquiat: Figures, Signs, Symbols

Perez Art Museum of Miami, 1103 Biscayne Blvd, Miami, 33132; visiting information here.

Featuring ten major works culled from the Kenneth C. Griffin Collection, this show also marks the largest-ever exhibition of Jean-Michel Basquiat works in Florida.

Hernan Bas: A gray foundation paired with rich walnut wood and vibrant pops of color

The Rubbell Museum, 1100 NW 23 ST, Miami, 33127; visiting information here. Opening December 1 and running through fall 2027.

Fresh off of a major show in Venice earlier this year, Hernan Bas returns to his hometown. The show will feature works from the museum’s collection spanning the artist’s career.

Two Exhibitions From Josh Aronson:

Welcome to Wonder

Vizcaya Museum & Gardens, 3251 S Miami Ave, Miami, 33129; visiting information here.

A Sudden Leap

Museum of Contemporary Art, 770 NE 125th Street, North Miami, 33161; visiting information here.

Photographer Josh Aronson, best known for his ongoing Florida Boys series, has two shows at museums in different corners of town that find their own ways to commune with nature. A Sudden Leap is a sail-shaped installation at MOCA North Miami’s pond, while Welcome to Wonder places Aronson’s work throughout the trees of Vizcaya’s walking paths (a nice escape from the rest of the Miami madness, even if you’re not familiar with his work).

Geoffrey Holder: Black Magic

Museum of Contemporary Art, 770 NE 125th Street, North Miami, 33161; visiting information here.

Geoffrey Holder, who died in 2014, was a true renaissance man. He was a principal dancer at the Metropolitan Opera Ballet, played a James Bond villain, won Tony Awards for both directing and designing costumes for The Wiz, and even voiced the sun in Bear in the Big Blue House. Amid all that, he also honed his talents as a visual artist. Black Magic marks the first museum survey of his work, featuring paintings, drawings, collages, and sculptures.

Art Everywhere Else

During Miami Art Week, you’ll literally see art everywhere: in private homes, on the street, perhaps even in the drugstore on the corner. Here, some of the can’t-miss selections from outside the museum and gallery walls.

The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach Presents The Perfect Trade-Off

1 Lincoln Road, Miami Beach, 33139

Conceptual artist Rachel Lee Hovnanian, noted for her provocations about beauty and perfection, takes on artificial intelligence and digital alienation for this exhibition presented throughout the beachfront and public areas of The Ritz-Carlton, South Beach. Two works will debut at the hotel: the installation Dinner for Ten invites viewers to join a dinner party with nine other guests (depicted on screens) who can’t look up from their phones, while Poor Teddy in Memoriam is a giant sculpture depicting a discarded teddy bear (perhaps abandoned in favor of an iPad?). The previously displayed FMLMBD (F**k My Life My Battery’s Dead) will also offer visitors a chance to charge their phones.

Armani/Casa Presents Graeme Black’s Interwoven

3820 NE 2nd Ave., Miami, 33137. Running December 2nd through the 13th.

Artist Graeme Black’s previous career was in fashion design; in fact, he spent 7 years working under Giorgio Armani. His show at Armani/Casa’s Design District outpost is something of a homecoming, featuring one painting on loan from Mr. Armani’s personal collection. A tapestry made in collaboration with Emma Jo Webster, among other works, will be displayed alongside a curation of iconic Armani/Casa pieces.

Out of This World—A Field of Conditions by Objects of Common Interest

The Design District, Miami.

This year, the Miami Design District Annual Design Commission has enlisted Objects of Common Interest—the studio cofounded by Eleni Petaloti and Leonidas Trampoukis—to install works throughout the shopping and culture hub. Many of the sculptural pieces respond to either the viewer or their surroundings, releasing puffs of vapor, rotating on touch, or, in the case of a marble-and-resin pyramid structure, emitting a sound that you can only hear when standing close to it.

LVMH The Studio Miami

140 NE 39th Street, 3rd Floor, Miami, 33137; visitor information here. Running December 2nd through 6th, open to the public daily 11 AM to 4 PM.

For the sixth year, LVMH The Studio returns to the Design District with open-to-the-public gallery viewing hours and special programming throughout the week. Featured artists this year include Rodrigo Méndez, Jay Chung, Kid Kardiac, and Rachel K. Artisans from Louis Vuitton, Tiffany & Co., and Tag Heuer will also be leading live, on-site demonstrations.

item.title: Can Dyson’s New Hair Tool Remove the Stress of At-Home Blowouts?
item.description: Four W editors take on the Dyson Airsmooth to see just how sleek their hairstyling routines can get.
item.dc:creator: Che Baez
item.content:encoded:
There’s nothing quite like a good hair day, but getting to that point can sometimes feel like a slog. Blow-drying, brushing, stretching, and smoothing are all moves that require an arsenal of tools, and a whole lot of patience. For those with curls or particularly stubborn strands, finding hair tools that won’t give you anxiety is an uphill battle.

After wishing for a beauty miracle, the Dyson Airsmooth has entered the ring. Designed to dry, smooth, and shape the hair all at once, the hot-air brush combines Dyson’s signature airflow tech with a dual-bristle system to prevent snagging and breakage. But does it live up to the hype across different hair types and textures? We asked four editors to put the Dyson Airsmooth through its paces. Below, they share their honest opinions.

Maxine Wally, Senior Digital Editor

Tell me about your hair type, routine, and biggest styling frustrations.

I have thick, dark-brown strands, which get very frizzy very easily. I apply Shu Uemura Essence Absolue Hair Oil or Roz’s Santa Lucia Styling Oil daily to weigh my hair down. But in general, I follow a less-is-more routine because I am completely inept when it comes to doing hair. I have a handful of go-to styles I keep in rotation, (most of which are plays on a slick-back bun) and I typically air-dry after shampooing and conditioning once or twice a week.

What was your first impression of the Dyson Airsmooth?

Okay, this is serious—I’m telling you, I’m really bad at doing hair. It’s like when aspiring doctors in medical school are informed they’ve “got no brains in their fingers,” and they should drop out. I do not have the skills to do hair. At least, that’s what I thought, until I tried this product. It is so incredibly easy to use, even for someone as hair-challenged as myself. With this tool, I could do my hair in the most wispy, whimsical, voluminous manner. I recently got a haircut with lots of long layers and I felt the results I got from the Dyson Airsmooth accentuated those layers in a pretty way.

Did the Dyson Airsmooth solve your hair dilemma?

Now that you mention it, yes, it did solve a dilemma I’ve always had—that I don’t feel confident with a hair tool in my hand. To be honest, I don’t use tools at all, a combination of general disinterest and overall anxiety. But this product made everything so seamless. First of all, it’s a two-in-one, so it dries your hair while styling it. Secondly, it removes frizz, a major plus. And it gives your ends a lovely curl or flip that’s on-trend for fall.

Would you use this product again?

I will definitely be using this styling tool in the future. The look is a little polished for every day, but for a night out or a special occasion I know where to go for a silky, shiny mane that won’t take hours (or specialized skills) to attain.

Dyson Airsmooth Styling Brush

Tori López, Fashion Market Editor

Tell me about your hair type, routine, and biggest styling frustrations.

While I love my natural curl pattern, I still struggle with daily maintenance. Often, I find myself opting for a slick-back look or blowout to alleviate stress in my morning routine. I use the Dyson Airwrap for my blowouts: it’s my holy-grail hair tool, hands down. With the Airsmooth, my goal was to see if I could achieve a similar bouncy blowout in the same amount or less time than my Dyson Airwrap.

What was your first impression of the Dyson Airsmooth?

The blowout was quick! The head of the Airsmooth doesn’t come off, so there is no way to give your hair a rough blow-dry. I thought that might add time to the whole process, but it didn’t. You’re able to get close to the scalp because of the bristles, so I was able to smooth out any curls at the roots. I will say, I had a bit of trouble in the beginning—my hair got caught in the brush—but after trying a few different techniques I was able to avoid any painful tugs.

Did the Dyson Airsmooth solve a hair problem of yours?

In terms of time, using the Airsmooth was actually faster than the Airwrap, which is great for a lady like me who is always running ten minutes behind. But the blowout was not as bouncy—it was more sleek than I prefer, since the round brush is larger in size than the head of the Airwrap.

Will you use this product again?

While I prefer to use my Airwrap on a daily basis, the Airsmooth has now become my new international travel buddy. It is one of two Dyson tools (second to the Supersonic Travel hair dryer) that has universal voltage, so I can finally put my hair gel to rest and rock a blowout worldwide.

Carolyn Twersky-Winkler, Staff Writer

Tell me about your hair type, routine, and biggest styling frustrations.

I have curly waves, which I place in category 2B. I usually blow my hair out (with a Dyson) once or twice a week, and then ride that out for days. When I feel like my hair needs a break, I do let it air-dry. My biggest styling frustration is frizz and breakage, two things I’m prone to because of the texture of my hair. I therefore prefer tools and products that are simultaneously smoothing and gentle on my strands. My perfect hair day features a silky blowout with a flirty flip at the end, and I was hoping I could achieve that quickly with the Dyson Airsmooth.

What was your first impression of the product?

I was initially dubious about the Airsmooth. I am a fan of Dyson’s hair tools—I use my Airwrap multiple times a week—but blow-dry brushes specifically give me pause. I have tried a handful over the years, and have never been superimpressed by them. Before using the Dyson Airsmooth, I let my hair dry to about 80 percent. One of my issues with styling brushes in the past is that I feel they’re not designed to reach the roots, where my hair will still feel damp even after styling. In my experience, styling brushes place more of an emphasis on styling than drying. I will say, though, the teardrop shape of the Dyson did make reaching my roots a bit easier. But I still didn’t feel like I had as much control as when I use a regular dryer.

How did your hair look and feel afterward?

I liked that the Dyson Airsmooth was fairly gentle on my hair. I didn’t feel like it was tugging at or breaking strands, which I appreciated. It also did leave my hair smooth, and I didn’t feel like I needed an excess amount of styling cream to tame the frizz once done. Still, my hair felt kind of flat once finished. I wasn’t able to achieve the volume I get from blow-drying, and while I focused on my ends to achieve that flippy finish I like, I had a hard time.

Would you use the Airsmooth again?

I think I will grab the Airsmooth if I’m in a rush and just want to dry my hair quickly, but for the most part, I’m going to stick with my Airwrap (which, by the way, does have a blow-dry brush attachment). I would recommend the Airsmooth to anyone who isn’t particularly fussy about their hair—someone who just wants a smooth, dry coif but doesn’t mind the style too much.

Che Baez, Visuals Editor

What does your dream hair day look like?

My dream hair day is: no frizz. Full stop. I have curly 3A-3C hair, so even though it’s healthy and strong, it can get frizzy easily if the right combination of products and styling aren’t used.

What was your first impression of the Dyson Airsmooth?

My first impression of the Dyson Airsmooth was how light it was. The reason I typically air-dry my hair is because I despise raising heavy tools above my shoulders while styling. My second impression was: the bristles are so interesting! I immediately noted that this would not pull my hair as much as typical tools. The bristles on most blow-dry brushes scare the living crap out of me, as someone with long hair that is kinkier at the root.

How did your hair look and feel afterward?

The tool was incredibly easy to use. I’ve used various blow-dry brushes in the past, and I found they left my hair tangled if I wasn’t holding them at a specific angle. I was pleasantly surprised that I garnered a great result after first use, when typically it would take me years to be able to master using a blow-drying tool.

My hair looked and felt shiny and voluminous after blowdrying my curls from wet. I used a heat protectant on each section, and it took me about 35 minutes to dry my entire head of hair. I also loved how my hair looked even when I wasn’t trying to get it pin-straight—I loved the volume and soft-feel. For those who want to stretch their hair before doing a silk press or getting their hair braided, this might be the ticket to a quick blow-dry. I was also surprised at the high heat temperature.

Would you use the Dyson Airsmooth again?

I love this tool. It is easy to use, easy to store, and I don’t have anxiety when I want to blow out my hair. I’m so excited to continue to use it throughout fall/winter and achieve a salon-level blowout with lots of volume.

item.title: Irina Shayk Wears Furry Party Pants for an Errand Run
item.description: For a wellness-filled day in Beverly Hills, the supermodel eschewed casual off-duty denim for a pair of high-octane leather pants.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Most people’s favorite pants are stretchy slacks or nondescript denim. But not Irina Shayk. The legendary supermodel’s go-to bottoms are edgy, gothic, and texturally distinct. Sure, they may seem uncomfortable to some, but on a casual outing in Los Angeles yesterday, Shayk demonstrated how wearable her go-to leather trousers really are.

On her way to a spa appointment in Beverly Hills, the 40-year-old star rewore a recognizable low-waisted design from Junya Watanabe. The avant-garde slacks feature faux crocodile leather, metallic hardware zippers, and jet-black fur lining. While she kept the dark intensity going with hardware-studded boots, up top, she went all in on off-duty dressing, wearing a white tank with bra straps peeking through. To finish, she had a sweater slung over one shoulder and a colossal canvas tote on the other that was big enough for a week’s worth of groceries. Strolling through the palm tree-lined sidewalks, she showed that her party pants were indeed also perfect for wellness activities.

As fashion fans will recall, the star first wore these trousers a year ago, when she suited up in a bondage-inspired leather look to attend a launch party for photographer Steven Klein’s book Steven Klein: Vogue in New York City. But while that outing was fitting for a gritty downtown warehouse party, her West Coast rewear proves her one-of-a-kind pants are also somehow Erewhon appropriate.

We’d expect nothing less from the seasoned runway star, who has had a busy few weeks of back-to-back fashion statements. After walking the Victoria’s Secret runway, she went unexpectedly minimal in an angelic Issey Miyake breastplate at the WSJ Innovator Awards before referencing the ’90s in a simple Dolce & Gabbana LBD at the LACMA Art+Film Awards. Still, subversive dressing is ultimately what Shayk does best, so she will always find a way to work a provocative statement piece into an everyday outing. Prebiotic soda and all.

item.title: How Netflix's 'The Body' Fashion Brings Rebellious Y2K Girlhood to Life
item.description: Costume designer Mirren Gordon-Crozier shares an exclusive look at the show's It-girl aesthetic, from rosary-draped Balenciagas to Galliano-era Dior.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
The Body is more than just an ode to Y2K fashion. For those who grew up Catholic, queer, and quietly rebelling against school dress codes, it’s a visceral time capsule. The psycho-thriller Netflix series follows the Lions, the reigning dance team at St. Mark’s Catholic High School in 2004. Despite the strict, God-fearing setting, the Lions are culty, provocatively glamorous, and constantly up to no good. They’re led by co-captains—and secret lovers—Anya (Kristina Bogic) and Elise (Sara Boustany).

Then comes Lisbeth (Geena Meszaros), a new-to-town, socially awkward outsider who wants nothing more than to be on the team. After a satanic ritual at a Halloween party goes awry, she blackmails her way in, and things take a haunting turn from there. Throughout its eight-episode run, The Body charts the complicated intimacy of teen-girl friendship, the weight of religious guilt, and how much better a secret is kept in a pre-iPhone age. A big part of this worldbuilding, of course, comes down to the clothes.

“I kind of approached it like a period film,” says costume designer Mirren Gordon-Crozier, noting that she mostly restricted her vintage sourcing to pieces from 2000 to 2004. For inspiration, she looked to paparazzi shots of Paris Hilton and Britney Spears and analyzed early-aughts tabloid media. “It was the rise of the It girl, reality TV, and public personas,” she says of this time in pop culture history. She combed through vintage shops in Toronto, where the series was shot, and stayed up until the early hours finding designer bags on eBay. She also created an inner world for each character, down to picturing which posters would be plastered on their bedroom walls.

Here, Gordon-Crozier walks us through her process for dressing The Body’s Anya, Elise, and Lisbeth, how the Lions’ uniforms came to life, and the details on all those enviable 2000s It bags.

“Anya is trying to hide her sexual desires from her disapproving mother,” Gordon-Crozier says of the popular team captain. “So we went extra floral and uber feminine with her.” She wears a lot of Blumarine, ballet-inspired pieces, and pastel palettes. As for her celeb style inspiration? That would be The O.C.’s Mischa Barton.

“Elise is a little bit darker. She’s sort of inspired by Devon Aoki, Comme des Garçons, and Marithé + François Girbaud,” says Gordon-Crozier. “She wears asymmetrical silhouettes, more complicated designs, and lots of texture.”

Most impressive, perhaps, is Elise’s expansive outerwear collection. “She’s just a coat girl, that’s her thing,” says Gordon-Crozier of the biting dance captain, noting her particularly striking vintage animal-print jacket. “If you were going to get metaphorical with it, you could say it’s like the tiger that she wears on her body.”

“Lisbeth is the one that evolves the most,” Gordon-Crozier says, adding that her early outfits reflect her conservative upbringing in the Pentecostal church. “I wanted to have her covered up in the beginning. She has a long denim skirt; she has one pair of Walmart sneakers that we beat up. She’s definitely a little inspired by Chloë Sevigny in Gummo. We had the idea to bleach her eyebrows, and she has her cat T-shirt, which is similar to the one Sevigny wore. It’s a little nod.”

Once Lisbeth manipulates her way onto the team, she starts to “single-white-female” Anya, says Gordon-Crozier. “She sort of wants to wear Anya’s skin. She starts wearing her clothes, borrowing her bags, emulating her style, and forgetting about her mother at home.”

“[For the Halloween party], it was scripted that [Anya] would be ‘slutty God.’ I was like, ‘Okay, well, she doesn’t have any money. How’s she going to get this costume?’ So the idea is that she pulls the sheet off her bed, and then she takes a cross off her wall and hangs it around her neck.”

“We made all the school uniforms, and every girl has a different skirt length. Lisbeth’s was longer, and the Lions had shorter skirts because they would roll them up at the top,” she says. “The main thing for us was the bags, because even though the girls had these uniforms, and they weren’t really allowed to wear makeup, we wanted to show that they cared about how they looked.”

“I was literally up until 2 a.m. every night on deep, deep holes on the internet. We would find bags in bad shape, and I had an ager and dyer who would clean them, paint them, and re-weave the leather, because we didn’t have a big budget,” she says. Her favorites are the John Galliano-era Dior purses, but they also had bags from Coach, Longchamp, Louis Vuitton, Von Dutch, and, of course, Balenciaga. “I borrowed a Givenchy bag from someone in my office. I brought in one of my Balenciaga City bags. We were begging, borrowing, and stealing to get all of them,” she laughs.

“I tried not to repeat bags too much with Anya...I thought she would have one for every day. I decided to add rosaries to her Balenciagas as a little personal touch.”

The Lions’ stage costumes, too, were rooted in 2000s-era It girldom. “I saw a photo of Chloë Sevigny in a dance leotard, and I basically copied the shape of it,” she says. “I think the girls had a love-hate relationship with the bodysuits. But it was a true uniform, in the sense it brought them together.”

“I researched images of debutantes in that era,” she says of coming up with the dresses for the ball in the finale. “The idea of the debutante is so bizarre. It’s like purity, white gloves, and teenage boys in tuxedos handing off their dates. Everyone had white dresses with touches of black. I wanted it to be very uniform in that sense, because I think they all talk.”

“Anya’s was a copy of a Stella McCartney-era Chloé dress. It was seafoam green, but I really liked the black detail on it, so we made that in white and changed it up a little bit.”

“For Elise, I saw a photo of Devon Aoki on the red carpet in this white braided top, so we remade that with a puffy skirt on the bottom.”

“[Showrunner Quinn Shephard] and [executive producer Gina Gammell] had such a clear vision of what they wanted. They wanted this to be a special fashion TV show. The set designer is amazing, the music is amazing, and all these girls are unknown,” she says. “A lot of them have worked before, but not to this capacity. They all really bonded, like real Lions.”

item.title: Rihanna Brings Back a Surprising 2010s Style on Date With A$AP Rocky
item.description: The Fenty Beauty founder referenced one of last decade's biggest trends on a stylish outing in Los Angeles this week.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Rihanna is no stranger to a good fashion reference. But while her sartorial callbacks tend to pull from the 2000s or the 1990s, yesterday, she brought things up a decade by putting a modern spin on a 2010s staple: the millennial green jacket.

While on a rare date night with A$AP Rocky in Los Angeles, RiRi wrapped herself in a plush Celine parka with unmistakably nostalgic details. Defined by its big, utilitarian pockets and olive hue, the green cargo jacket style is a relic of the last decade—beloved by 2010s It girls everywhere, from Alexa Chung to Candice Swanepoel. It has been subtly making its return, however, in recent seasons, with Prada and Victoria Beckham introducing modish reimaginings. Rihanna’s Celine version, which seemingly came from her stylist Jahleel Weaver, features some contemporary touches. With a two-tone palette and a removable shearling lining, the loose-fitting men’s jacket is relaxed, slouchy, and perfectly fitting for a coordinated date night with A$AP Rocky.

For his part, the rapper kept things decidedly modern and minimal (for him) in a dark-wash denim jacket, tailored trousers, and dapper penny loafers. Walking arm-in-arm with her partner, Rihanna amped up the throwback aesthetics by finishing her 2010s silhouette with pink-tinted Y2K sunglasses and strappy heels. Together, with their elevated accessories and utilitarian jackets, they were once again subtly in sync instead of overtly matchy.

It’s been a while since Rihanna and A$AP Rocky have had a proper date night. He’s been in the midst of his Don’t Be Dumb tour, while she’s been busy promoting Fenty Beauty launches and helping her 1-year-old daughter Rocki make her Dior-model debut. Still, when they do find time to go out together, the pair always appear sartorially aligned. With Rocky currently on a break between the European and Oceanic legs of his tour, what better time for them to show off their affinity for autumnal accessorizing? His concert shows officially pick back up in Australia on December 5, so perhaps there are a few more couple outings—and surprising 2010s references—to come.

item.title: 16 Advent Calendars That Are Actually Worth the Price
item.description: The best cult-favorite products, coveted formulations, and unexpected treasures (not hair ties and keychains!).
item.dc:creator: Maryam Lieberman
item.content:encoded:
A holiday gift that unfolds day by day bears an incredible allure. Why settle for one moment of delight when you can have 25? For the beauty devotee, a luxury advent calendar transforms the Christmas countdown into a daily ritual of discovery, with a new indulgence waiting behind every door. Think: exquisitely considered edits of cult favorites, coveted formulations, and unexpected treasures (real treasures, not hair ties and keychains). A veritable cabinet of curiosities for the discerning beauty enthusiast is an outstanding gift idea. After all, anticipation is part of the pleasure. These are the most desirable advent calendars actually worth their salt in 2026.

Dior Beauty Le 30 Montaigne Advent Calendar

This is divinity done the French way. Dior creates an advent calendar, and naturally, it’s anything but ordinary—featuring an edit of the house’s most coveted beauty icons, from its prestige skincare and coveted Lip Oils to signature fragrances. Here’s a serious lineup of beauty heavy hitters, wrapped in the unmistakable world of Dior.

Sisley Advent Calendar by Marie-Victoire de Bascher

Please meet one of our favorite advent calendars of the year. The presentation here has a distinctly Parisian sensibility—but what really caught our attention is the swoon-worthy contents. Twenty-five products (including Sisleÿa face cream, the mascara we keep coming back to, neck cream, and Velvet Body Cream, among plenty of others) make this product hard to beat, especially when it comes to the generous sizes and quality.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian The Countdown Calendar

Who says the fun has to stop on Christmas Day? Maison Francis Kurkdjian takes things through to New Year’s Eve with a countdown that is anything but traditional. And the aromatic contents are out of this world: Baccarat Rouge 540 Extrait and its scented body oil, Grand Soir, plus Oud Satin Mood sparkling oil, a miniature Aqua Universalis, and an assortment of beautifully sized candles and fragrance vials are included.

Augustinus Bader The 12 Days of Bader

A dozen days will give you a very good reason to get serious about skincare. This edit brings together some of Augustinus Bader’s best-known formulas, from The Rich Cream and The Cream to The Eye Patches, The Elixir, and The Hand Cream. This is a particularly thoughtful gift for someone who knows their way around a skincare shelf and is always game to discover what else deserves a place on it.

Dolce & Gabbana Beauty Advent Calendar

A little theatricality never hurts at Christmastime, especially when the presentation is super glam. This one brings together Dolce & Gabbana makeup and fragrances in lavish gold package, with each little reveal feeling like its own occasion.

Acqua di Parma Advent Calendar

Beautifully presented, the Italian fragrance house consistently makes the most impeccable scents that are timeless and unforgettable. So, of course, this one’s a total win in terms of gift-giving.

The Jewelry Box Guerlain x Germanier Advent Calendar

Guerlain has made an advent calendar with more glamour than your average countdown. The beauty brand dressed up 25 of its beauty icons—from Shalimar to a limited-edition Rouge G lipstick and Abeille Royale serum—in a jewel-box-inspired creation designed in collaboration with couturier Kévin Germanier. We love that the embellished box becomes a chic jewelry keeper after all the little gifts have been revealed.

111Skin 11 Days Of Radiance Advent Calendar

This is not your average beauty countdown. The collection here is firmly in the serious-skincare category, and 111Skin’s advent calendar is a rather clever way to get acquainted with the line—or simply to reaffirm your affection for the fabulous products.

Baobab Collection Advent Calendar Voyage Extraordinaire

Here are twenty-four winter-inspired scents that are beautifully composed, while the glass vessels are objets d’art in their own right, gorgeous enough to keep long after the candles have burned down. We think this advent calendar makes the countdown every bit as lovely as the holiday itself.

Byredo Advent Calendar

This one’s worth its weight, and we mean that literally. If Santa shimmied down the chimney with the Byredo advent calendar in his velvet bag, we’d be absolutely thrilled. This heavy set is filled with fragrance, makeup, body care, home, and accessories in both travel and full sizes. You’ll receive glass bottles of Bal d’Afrique, Blanche, and Mojave Ghost, along with the classic Bibliothèque, Tree House, and Summer Rain candle range. A present like this portends good things to come in the New Year.

Penhaligon's The Advent Calendar

For your recipient’s home, body, and mood (yes, all three are intertwined!), these stunningly curated candles, scents, and creams are a fabulous way to bring some elevated English moments to the holidays.

Charlotte Tilbury Hollywood Beauty Wonderland Advent Calendar

If it’s 15 dazzling beauty surprises you seek in an advent calendar, then look no further: Charlotte Tilbury’s Hollywood Beauty Wonderland has everything you need. There are four full-size products here, plus two accessories for the first time in the CT advent calendar’s robust history.

Diptyque Advent Calendar

A clever twist this year at Diptyque borrows from the traditional wood-turner’s toolbox in a design created with artist Jean-Simon Roch. Inside, 25 little discoveries range from its beloved candles and fragrances to body care and home objects. There’s a nice balance of familiar favorites and things you may not have tried before, which is really the fun of it.

24 Days Of MAC Icons Advent Calendar

Twenty-four days of MAC favorites, covering just about every makeup mood imaginable. From lips and eyes to complexion essentials, it’s a well-rounded edit of the products that have made MAC a makeup-bag mainstay.

Typology Paris Advent Calendar 2026

Dare we say—this is one of the more worthwhile beauty calendars this year? Typology does brow and lash products particularly well, but there’s plenty more to get stuck into, from face essentials to some genuinely good serums.

Clarins 24-Day Beauty Advent Calendar Gift Set

Clarins has nailed the beauty game for decades, and its products continue to impress. The label’s advent calendar has 24 advanced, fast-acting offerings for the beauty obsessive in your life. Another bonus point—there are several full-size items, including the beloved Total Eye lift, the Multiactive Glow Serum and the Lip Comfort Oil, which are genuine beauty must-haves.

item.title: Hailey Bieber Celebrates Her Birthday In A Sexy Roberto Cavalli Cutout Top
item.description: For her 30th, the Rhode founder broke her vintage-pull tradition in favor of a fresh-off-the-runway statement.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Now that she’s 30, Hailey Bieber is changing things up—starting with her birthday outfit. While it’s become something of a tradition for the Rhode founder to wear a piece of runway history to ring in a new year, to enter her third decade, she kept things au courant with an outfit fresh from the spring 2027 season.

On Sunday, the Sagittarius superstar posted a celebratory mirror selfie. Her sexy ensemble featured an emerald green cardigan with whisper-thin lace-up details and zebra-print low-waisted trousers. To the untrained eye, it could have been mistaken for a deep-cut design from iconic 2000s archives. But nay. Bieber’s more-is-more getup was, in fact, recently debuted on Roberto Cavalli’s Milan Fashion Week runway.

To be fair, Cavalli’s latest collection was heavily aughts-derived, with creative director Fausto Puglisi citing 2001-era Sex and the City as a major creative inspiration and thus reviving the brand’s most nostalgic house codes. As such, the catwalk was full of bedazzled denim, gauzy sheer slips, and—a Hailey Bieber favorite—animal print galore.

Still, it’s a notable shift for the fashion-history-loving It girl, whose birthday ensembles over the past few years have reliably included some enviable decades-old element. For her 29th, she opted for a leather top from Donatella Versace’s fall 2002 collection. The year before that, she went back a decade further with a jacket from Tom Ford’s Gucci.

But after pulling off one of her most impressive ’90s pulls ever in a CBK-approved Yohji Yamamoto look last week, she took a more modern sartorial approach for weekend festivities. Following her viral Dealbook Summit interview in New York City, the beauty mogul ostensibly celebrated her birthday in a more laid-back Los Angeles. Naturally, she did work in one vintage pull, with longtime pal Camila Morrone posting a picture of Bieber in a sheer spring 1997 Dolce & Gabbana cardigan for a day by the beach.

But her birthday evening—involving an intimate fireworks viewing with husband Justin and a rose-colored cocktail in hand—did not entail a vintage pull. After all, some traditions are meant to be broken.

item.title: Kim Kardashian Ties Herself Up in Vintage Dior Pants to Support Lewis Hamilton
item.description: Tie her up. Tie her down. Just make sure she's tied in vintage Dior.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Leave it to Kim Kardashian to turn a WAG outing into an opportunity to wear Y2K Dior. Over the weekend, the Skims founder cheered on her boyfriend Lewis Hamilton at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Showing her support for the famed Ferrari driver, Kardashian adhered to the race car’s signature black-and-red palette—with an archival twist, of course.

For Friday’s qualifying session on the Las Vegas Strip Circuit, Kardashian laced up in a pair of latex pants from Dior’s fall 2003 runway by John Galliano. Studded with gold grommets and bondage lacing along the front of the leg, the cutout-filled piece is an on-theme choice for the vintage-loving star. Styled by Law Roach, she paired the pants with a matching cropped jacket and a waist-cinching black trench. For a final hit of archival glamour, she accessorized with gladiator heels from Roberto Cavalli’s spring 2005 collection.

It wasn’t the only show-stopping look of the weekend, however. The following day, she doubled down on the red-and-black palette in two complementary monochrome leather looks. First, a custom Chrome Hearts crimson set, complete with a zip-up jacket and bedazzled pants. Next, all-black separates with intricate ruching and an even tighter silhouette.

Kardashian is becoming something of an F1 race weekend regular, this being her third. She made her debut at the buzzy event during the Monaco Grand Prix with sister Khloé in June, before hitting the Singapore Grand Prix in October. While those outings saw her wearing slinky, skin-tight dresses and bedazzled Gucci thongs, her most recent appearance was the most moto-core yet.

On the race track, it was a tough weekend for Hamilton, who was involved in a crash with teammate Charles Leclerc and received a 10-second penalty. Still, it was a successful networking-forward few days for Kardashian, who was spotted spending time with All’s Fair co-star Teyana Taylor, as well as meeting members of the all-female F1 Academy. Videos show Hamilton introducing her to Susie Wolff, a former driver and the managing director of F1 Academy, whom she later gushed over on Instagram. Perhaps she has Academy members in mind for her next Skims campaign? Talk about winning WAG behavior.

item.title: Sienna Spiro Rings in the Holidays With Bloomingdale's and Ralph Lauren
item.description: The Best New Artist Grammy nominee brought her hits to Lexington Avenue for the unveiling of the iconic New York retailer’s festive new windows.
item.dc:creator: W Staff
item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, Sienna Spiro helped Bloomingdale’s flip the switch on the holiday season. The 21-year-old British singer took over Lexington Avenue outside the department store’s 59th Street flagship, performing against a backdrop created in partnership with Ralph Lauren. For the occasion, Spiro wore a glossy red mackintosh coat pulled from the Ralph Lauren archives, styled with black leather driving gloves and towering Christian Louboutin heels—a suitably cinematic and festive look for Gotham. The appearance capped a whirlwind week for Spiro, who had just been named a 2027 Grammy nominee for Best New Artist.

After her set, Bloomingdale’s CEO Olivier Bron and Ralph Lauren chief branding and innovation officer David Lauren led the countdown to the reveal. This year’s windows lean fully into the house’s holiday mythology: tartan, velvet, polished wood, and warmly lit vignettes that conjure the sort of snow-dusted country-house fantasy Ralph Lauren has long made its own. For the first time, the brand also transformed the flagship’s facade with a massive illuminated log cabin installation. Among those who turned out for the festivities were François Arnaud, Karl-Anthony Towns, Brittany Snow, Lux Pascal, Nicky Hilton, Ben Ahlers, and Team USA Olympic stars Maia and Alex Shibutani.

The collaboration anchors Bloomingdale’s broader “A Treasured Holiday” campaign, which extends well beyond the windows. Inside, shoppers can visit a Ralph Lauren Holiday Shop stocked with Purple Label, Ralph Lauren Collection, and luxury gifts, alongside more than 50 seasonal activations ranging from an UGG takeover at Forty Carrots and a Barbour tea shop to Hermès beauty, Santaland, and designer pop-ups.

For one night, though, the spectacle belonged to Spiro—and to that unmistakable moment when New York officially starts to look like Christmas.
