item.title: Dakota Johnson & Machine Gun Kelly Coordinate with Statement Bags
item.description: On a dinner outing in Los Angeles, the rumored couple *almost* achieved aesthetic cohesion.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Rumored couple Dakota Johnson and Machine Gun Kelly are not exactly known to match. She leans more red-carpet royalty, while he reliably serves mallpunk. But there appears to be one area where their styles unexpectedly align: the statement bag.

Last night, the pair were spotted leaving dinner in Los Angeles in looks that let their patterned purses take center stage. Johnson embraced her love of leopard print with a structured XL tote, seemingly from Dolce & Gabbana, which she paired with a black leather trench and green scarf. Next to her, MGK donned a Louis Vuitton Speedy festooned with zebra-like monogramming. Ever the beanie enthusiast, he finished with a black-and-white hat by streetwear brand Reach and a faded C2H4 bomber.

As they parted ways, their respective loud bags clashed to almost poetic extents. It’s the closest thing we’ve seen to outfit coordination from these two, whose alleged relationship has been the subject of non-stop speculation ever since they “hit it off” at Taylor Swift’s wedding in July.

As the extremely online may recall, the last time the pair were spotted out together, they appeared dressed for opposite events. When attending a screening of Johnson’s film Flesh Impact last week, Johnson donned a Valentino evening gown, while MGK wore distressed jeans and a shrunken white T-shirt. Johnson did, notably, break out one of her many animal-print jackets for the date. Perhaps she influenced her rumored beau to embrace big, bold patterned purses? A couple that shares accessories—now that just might be true love.

item.title: Chase Infiniti and Alysa Liu Have a Night at the Museum With Louis Vuitton
item.description: Plus, more of the season's best ads.
item.dc:creator: W Staff
item.content:encoded:
Fashion loves to press fast forward. A brand’s mind is always on the next big thing, the newest trend, the upcoming season. That’s just the nature of the industry. But sometimes, it can feel excessive, like when cruise collection campaigns get released simultaneously with holiday campaigns while there’s still a pumpkin on your front step. Soon enough, the spring campaigns will be rolling out in full force, but for now, we have intermediaries like GucciCore and Loewe’s spring/summer pre-collection to warm us up. But check back here often for the latest campaigns from your favorite fashion brands.

Louis Vuitton

Louis Vuitton has returned to the Frick Museum—the site of the brand’s cruise 2027 show last May—for the collection’s campaign. Chase Infiniti and Alysa Liu star in the Ethan James Green images, which depict a journey through the artworks of the New York City institution.

Louis Vuitton

Set within the Frick’s historic galleries, the campaign unfolds through a narrative of discovery via art and imagination.

Louis Vuitton

“The Cruise collections have always been about movement, emotion, and the encounter between silhouettes and place,” said Louis Vuitton artistic director Nicolas Ghesquière. “For the cruise 2027 campaign, I wanted to extend that dialogue through a tale of two cities—between Paris and New York, expressing legacy and modernity. The campaign reflects the layered identities, contradictions, and cultural energy at the heart of the collection, where each look becomes part of a conversation between history, colorful expression, and imagination.”

Givenchy

Paris’s famed Jardin du Luxembourg serves as the backdrop for Givenchy's spring/summer campaign. Models pose amid the greenery. Floppy, flowered heels bloom from the grass, and the curves of trees contrast the sharp tailoring of a jacket.

Givenchy

In some photos, the more industrial parts of the garden are on display. A rust-covered ladder acts as a perch, and a similarly treated door provides contrast to the modernity of the Shark Boot. Primary colors pop against the bright green of the leaves and the muted ecru of the buildings. There is a clarity to the images alive in Sarah Burton’s designs.

Celine

Michael Rider’s spring 2027 collection for Celine was created on intuition. The accompanying campaign lives in a similar space of instinct. Shot by Zoë Ghertner, the images take the collection away for the weekend.

Celine

The spontaneous styling of the show is once again on display. You see it in the capris rolled up so they avoid the water or in the jacket casually draped over the shoulders.

Celine

What has become Rider’s signature—the red sweater of his men’s debut—reappears as well, climbing out of a pair of pants, stretching past wrists and hands, and clinging on as it falls past shoulder blades. 

Loewe

Diego Calva, Kristine Frøseth, and more stars met up in Madrid for the Loewe spring 2027 pre-collection campaign, bringing the brand back to its roots in the city it calls home.

Loewe

Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez’s wardrobe is invigorated by the restless energy of Madrid. Bright colors are mirrored by the surroundings as models are photographed in fruit-stuffed marketplaces and the doorways of tiled tapas bars.

Loewe

There is a confidence to the images, partly provided by the assurance exuded by the models, who stare down Talia Chetrit’s camera. The campaign stars were no doubt bolstered by their armor of technical suiting, knitwear, and leatherwork.

Gucci

After a runway show that took over Times Square this past May, Gucci is sticking to a New York state of mind, photographing the GucciCore campaign in the city that never sleeps.

Gucci

The plurality of both GucciCore and New York are at play in the Peter Funch-shot images. Models walk the city streets—on their way to work, a dinner, or nowhere in particular. Despite the number of people who crowd the block, the Gucci-adorned have no problem standing out, thanks to Demna’s designs.

item.title: For Mariko Mori, Science and Spirituality Are Interconnected
item.description: The artist's first major retrospective in Japan in 25 years reminds us why Mori is one of contemporary art's most intriguing creative forces.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Sporn
item.content:encoded:
Mariko Mori’s boundary-pushing art practice is defined by juxtaposition. In her photography, sculptures, videos, and installations, she examines all things ancient and futuristic, the scientific and spiritual, technology and nature. “However, my intention is not to emphasize these oppositions, but to explore the possibility that they are fundamentally interconnected,” the artist, who splits her time between New York, Tokyo, and Miyako Island (about 180 miles southwest of Okinawa Main Island), tells W. Mori notes her upbringing was similarly marked by dualistic thinking: “Growing up in Japan, I was surrounded by a culture where ancient spiritual traditions coexist with an extraordinary enthusiasm for technological innovation. The worlds of anime, science fiction, Buddhist philosophy, and Shinto beliefs were all part of the cultural landscape that shaped my imagination.”

These sources of inspiration have fueled Mori’s practice for more than three decades, rendering her work as awe-inspiring and relevant now as when it was first created. This fall, the Mori Art Museum—founded by the artist’s uncle in 2003—celebrates her multifaceted oeuvre with Mariko Mori: All That Shines, the artist’s first major retrospective in Japan since 2002 (open through March 28, 2027). The exhibition is a highlight of Art Week Tokyo, an annual citywide platform encompassing museum and gallery presentations, performances, talks, and more. Conceived in collaboration with The Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation, the show presents some 40 career-defining works, from early photographic experiments in self-portraiture to the iconic Wave UFO (1999-2002), and a new video incorporating AI. Organized chronologically, the show is curated by Alexandra Munroe, senior curator at large of global arts at the Guggenheim Museum and Foundation; and Mami Kataoka, director of the Mori Art Museum.

Mori calls the homecoming “deeply meaningful and emotional. Although I have spent much of my life living and working internationally, Japan remains at the heart of my cultural and spiritual identity,” she says, noting how she was “struck by the philosophical continuity” of the works upon seeing them together for the first time. “This exhibition has allowed me to see my artistic journey not as a series of separate chapters, but as one continuous exploration.”

Many of the questions Mori’s work examines stem from her father’s passing during her early 20s. “His death made me confront the fragility of human existence for the first time,” she says. “I began to wonder whether consciousness truly disappears when our physical body dies, or whether we might be part of something much greater.” Mori studied Buddhism and astrophysics to better understand humans’ place in the universe, and has continuously collaborated with scientists and engineers, as well as architects, programmers, and craftspeople, in her practice. Mori also found herself drawn to sacred sites and ancient ruins, such as Giza, Angkor Wat, and Machu Picchu. “I came to understand that our physical existence is never separate from the universe. From a scientific perspective, the elements that make up our bodies were formed within stars and released into the universe when those stars died,” says Mori, who believes science and spirituality are not opposing fields but rather “different ways of approaching the same mysteries of existence.”

With the issue of existence at her practice’s core, Mori describes her work’s evolution as shifting “from the individual to the collective.” Early works, such as her “Cyborg” series (1994-95), in which Mori photographed herself in everyday urban settings, critique contemporary society and gender roles. In Play With Me (1994), for example, Mori, donning a metallic anime-robot-like costume, stands outside a gaming store, blurring the boundaries between real and fictional characters (while challenging the traditionally submissive role of a Japanese woman). In another series, titled “Esoteric Cosmos” (1996-98), Mori uses advanced digital imaging to create mystical scenes in which she, embodying deities, is superimposed onto barren landscapes, dotted with cartoon-like lotus blossoms and aliens. The series also features orb-like forms, which are echoed in 3-D as the exhibition progresses. A four-channel video installation produced between 1995 and 2006 depicts performances in which Mori lies in a transparent capsule situated in different public spaces, inciting an array of reactions from onlookers.

Mori’s biomorphic capsules peak with her largest installation, Wave UFO, which was the first artwork to ever use brainwave biofeedback. Three people can simultaneously lie down inside the pod, where headsets use electrodes to measure the electrical activity in their brains. Their electrical brain rhythms are then converted into colors and shapes, and, after a few minutes, the participants can watch an accompanying Mori-made video of the abstracted imagery. “What interests me is not simply creating a spectacular visual environment, but offering an experience that may lead to an inner transformation,” the artist adds.

Technology “has always been a medium through which I explore much older and more fundamental questions about existence, consciousness, and spirituality,” Mori says. “In that sense, my work is not so much about the future as it is about exploring what is timeless and universal.” In the case of Wave UFO, the work reflects the concept that all existence is interconnected, which the artist argues is especially urgent now that “we are living in a time of profound division, marked by conflict, environmental crises, and increasing social fragmentation.”

All That Shines spotlights the Faou Foundation, established by Mori in 2010 to engage local communities by permanently installing artworks that encourage connection between nature and humanity. So far, Mori has realized sculptures on Miyako Island and Rio de Janeiro. On view in the exhibition, Peace Crystal (2016-24)—an over-five-foot-tall diamond-shape sculpture of transparent crystal glass—is planned for installation in Ethiopia.

Iridescent materials and crystals have become a signature of Mori’s. For the artist, “light symbolizes the continuity of existence, as well as love, compassion, and the possibility of transcendence.” She adds, “If there is one thought I would like to share through All That Shines, it is that each of us carries a light within. And perhaps, by recognizing that light in ourselves and in others, we can begin to understand that we are all part of one greater existence.”

item.title: Net-A-Porter Hosts a Star-Studded Friendsgiving on the Upper East Side
item.description: Plus more of the best parties, galas, and events of the year.
item.dc:creator: W Staff
item.content:encoded:
Fall is already in full swing, and brands are breaking out the champagne and hors d’oeuvres, fueled by new collaborations and launches, plus the simple desire to throw a great bash. Fetes are taking place all over the world in honor of the season of renewal (along with every other reason imaginable). With the holidays—and galas galore—on the horizon, we’re calling a spade a spade: it’s all just an excuse to have a wonderful time while often donating to a good cause. While you might not be invited to the biggest parties in town in person, you can still enjoy them vicariously. Keep checking back here as we cover the best and brightest events of the year—and their A-list attendees.

Leave it to Net-A-Porter and diamond jewelry designer Jessica McCormack to host Friendsgiving inside an art gallery. On November 17, friends of the brands gathered at Salon 94 on the Upper East Side for an intimate, candle-lit dinner ringing in the holidays.

Guests included All’s Fair co-stars Sarah Paulson and Naomi Watts, who coordinated with the modern setting in contrasting black-and-white looks.

Also in attendance was supermodel Christy Turlington. Naturally, she exuded effortless ’90s elegance in a Toteme belted satin blouse and St. Agni wool pants.

The Mark Hotel is ready for the holidays, thanks in large part to Burberry. The British brand is taking over The Mark this Christmas, transforming the iconic New York hotel into a red-checked wonderland through the New Year. On Monday, November 16, friends of the label gathered in the cozy, tree-filled hotel restaurant to kick off the holiday season and toast the collab.

Star of Burberry’s holiday campaign, Gabrielle Union, was in attendance, as was Teyana Taylor. The two actors found a cozy red velvet booth in which to catch up and compare their respective Burberry fur coats.

The Burberry-adorned guests enjoyed drinks and bites before they were treated to a performance from Moses Martin’s band, People I’ve Met. The son of Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin recently made his modeling debut in Burberry’s “Escape to the Countryside” campaign. On Monday, the musician returned to his comfort zone on stage, where he was cheered on by his big sister, Apple.

Moses and Apple Martin at the Burberry party at The Mark Hotel.

Guests gathered at Palma in the West Village on Monday, November 16, for a Friendsgiving. This wasn’t a BYOB or potluck-style event, however, but an elegant affair hosted by Pamela Anderson and Pandora.

“I love any excuse to bring people around a table and make collective decisions to be good people, in deep gratitude to nature, and not forget history so we can make better decisions in the future,” Anderson told W over email ahead of the event. The actor-turned-gardener-and-cookbook-author achieved her goal with the candlelit dinner, which saw vegan dishes from Anderson’s cookbook, I Love You—including pumpkin risotto and veggie pot pies—on the menu.

“I've learned that the best part of bringing people together is actually getting to enjoy their company,” Anderson said. The convivial event allowed for just that. Ahead of dinner, guests mingled throughout the restaurant, sipping on drinks, including Anderson’s favorite rhubarb raspberry lemonade. Bethann Hardison, Ella Emhoff, and more explored Pandora’s new collection and customized engraved necklaces to take home.

On November 12, the New York City arts organization Performa descended upon the former City Cinemas East 86th Street theater and transformed it into a home for Double Feature, a benefit hosted by Chloe Wise and Miles Greenberg. Although Performa typically hosts an annual Biennial to spotlight its favorite artists and new commissions, this was a fresh way to experience Performa’s offerings outside of its usual schedule. For the event, Greenberg and Wise gathered with friends like Richie Shazam, pictured here, Pauline Chalamet, Blake Abbie, and more.

Guests were treated to the U.S. premiere of Chloe Wise’s PsyFi*—a 30-minute, three-channel film installation which Wise brought to life on Thursday night. Laszlo Horvath, Cam Arnold, and more performers sang and danced in the style of PsyFi*. Plus, chef Ashley Rath served a food installation inspired by Chloe Wise’s works at the party. Above, Michael Buscemi (brother of Steve) and JT pose for a photo.

Raul Lopez at the Performa party.

Tiffany & Co. kicked off the holiday season with an event hosted by its newest house ambassador, Amanda Seyfried, held at the Fifth Avenue flagship, The Landmark.

To celebrate her new position, the You Can See Everything actor was given the honor of lighting up the Bird on a Rock installation while guests watched in wonder, phones held high.

Seyfried was joined by fellow house ambassador Mikey Madison, along with Louisa Jacobson, Jordyn Woods, Danny Ramirez, and more friends of Tiffany. Of course, all were bedecked in Tiffany jewels, with the Bird on a Rock flying across many earlobes, ring fingers, and décolletés that evening.

On November 10, Loro Piana celebrated the 11th edition of the Loro Piana Cashmere of the Year Award, which honors herders who produce the finest cashmere fiber.

Bruce Springsteen, Jeremy Strong, Huma Abedin, and more guests were welcomed to the Brant Foundation in New York. Upon arrival, they were invited to explore "Master of Cashmere: The Quest for Fiber Excellence", an installation spotlighting the House’s longstanding relationship with cashmere and its responsible approach.

After guests seated for dinner, it was time to hand out the prizes, which went to three pairs of cashmere herders from Inner Mongolia. Each winner received a financial reward per kilo of fiber produced, along with an intricately crafted silver comb symbolizing the cashmere gathering process.

Bvlgari brought a dose of Roman glamour to Palm Beach with a gala celebrating the arrival of its Eclettica High Jewelry collection. Held at a historic 1920s waterfront estate designed by Addison Mizner, the evening drew Venus Williams, Chanel Iman, Becca Bloom, and Jewel, who performed an intimate set following a presentation of the collection. Guests later gathered for dinner beneath the tennis pavilion before dancing under the estate’s portico.

The Palm Beach celebration also marked a new chapter for Bvlgari in South Florida. Eclettica, which debuted earlier this year, features some of the house’s most ambitious high-jewelry creations to date, including 15 transformable pieces. The gala coincided with the opening of Bvlgari’s new Palm Beach boutique, extending the Roman jeweler’s presence in the region just as its latest collection arrived in town.

On November 5, Adria Arjona received the 2026 Women in Film Max Mara Face of the Future Award, which recognizes an actress who is committed to community-building. Dressed in a slinky black Max Mara dress featuring a keyhole neck cutout, the Onslaught actor celebrated with a party held in her honor at Chateau Marmont the night before the WIF gala.

Naturally, Arjona’s longtime partner, Jason Momoa, was by her side.

Arjona also posed with pal Shay Mitchell and mingled over cocktails with other A-list guests, including Brittany Snow, Jessica Alba, Zoey Deutch, and Victoria Justice.

Mariah Carey celebrated the release of her Gucci holiday campaign on Monday night at an exclusive cocktail reception at the House’s Fifth Avenue flagship in New York. 

Guests were invited to enjoy champagne and spiked hot apple cider in the store’s newly opened Gucci Apartmento, a private space on the third floor designed for a more exclusive shopping experience.

Dressed in a black maxidress and fur coat, Carey enjoyed a performance of her hit song, “All I Want for Christmas Is You,” performed by an a capella choir. She then closed out the night in the role of Santa Claus, handing out Gucci-branded chocolate for guests to take home.

Pomellato celebrated 20 years in New York with an intimate party on Wednesday, October 20, held at a Sutton Tower private residence. There, actor Michelle Monaghan, entrepreneur Olivia Palermo, and Olympian Lindsey Vonn gathered among other guests for cocktails and conversation.

The occasion also marked the North American debut of Pomellato’s newest High Jewelry collection, Pomellato Stile Libero, and the exclusive Americas launch of Moneta Orientale, the house’s latest in a series of archival reinterpretations. Guests were welcomed to admire these new creations, and were given their own Pomellato jewels to wear for the evening as well.

Nordstrom’s celebration of its 125th anniversary continued on October 22nd with help from Sacai designer Chitose Abe. The Japanese designer not only released a special capsule collection for the department store, but flew in to New York to host a celebratory dinner alongside Yumi Shin, Nordstrom’s executive vice president of global brand partnerships. Held in an intimate space inside the WSA building, Ghetto Gastro provided an appropriately culture-bridging menu with a main dish of honey miso sablefish.

Rapper JT, back stateside after making several front-row appearances during Paris Fashion Week, arrived in head-to-toe Sacai.

Ferragamo brought Florence, Italy to Beverly Hills on October 22, with the reopening of its Rodeo Drive flagship during the day, followed by a fabulous dinner in the private room at the Polo Lounge in the evening. The newly reimagined store is an exceptional sight, bearing a rich, assured palette across menswear and womenswear.

Leonardo Ferragamo and creative director Maximilian Davis hosted the intimate dinner on Thursday night, which was attended by stars like Andrew Garfield, Tracee Ellis Ross, Vittoria Ceretti, Gemma Chan (shown here with Leonardo Ferragamo), Tinashe, and Carolyn Murphy. James Ferragamo, men’s and women’s leather product director for the brand, was on hand for the party, along with many other members of the Ferragamo family.

A short film created by actor Martina Ferragamo lent a personal note to the evening. What emerged was a portrait of a family deeply connected to its roots, with Maximilian Davis now bringing his own innovative vision to the house as creative director. There was no need to choose between heritage and reinvention. Over dinner, the two felt entirely at home together.

Carolyn Murphy at the Ferragamo dinner in L.A.

Gabrielle Union

Kathryn Newton, Tinashe, and Karla Souza caught up before sitting to dinner.

Vittoria Ceretti

The natural beauty of Southern California was on display on September 23 as Tiffany & Co. invited guests to celebrate the grand opening of its South Coast Plaza store in Costa Mesa.

Zoey Deutch, Charles Melton, Laura Harrier, and more stars wore Tiffany jewels as they enjoyed canapés, champagne, and cocktails. Guests had the opportunity to explore the store, which was transformed for the occasion into a floral landscape inspired by the wild poppies of the California coast.

After some mingling, it was time for a multicourse dinner featuring the flavors of the region, curated by Daniel Boulud. The evening concluded with a performance by Ashe, a fitting end to a memorable night.

On June 17, Burberry celebrated its A Good Sport campaign with not just a World Cup watch party but a full takeover of New York’s iconic Corner Bistro. Through June 28, the low-key neighborhood haunt will be decked out in the British heritage brand’s signature checks in honor of the World Cup.

Guests, including actor Adam DiMarco, arrived early to watch the England vs. Croatia match and were treated to the restaurant’s famous burgers and fries, as well as pints of Guinness served in glasses featuring the Burberry knight.

Industry star Myha’la made the Burberry watch party a date night with her husband Armando Rivera.

Spring Street in New York City’s SoHo was the place to be on Tuesday, May 26—specifically, the four-story Longchamp store on Spring Street, where crowds of people gathered to watch Zoey Deutch (pictured here), Emma Roberts, Joan Smalls, Maggie Gyllenhaal, and more head to the French label’s latest big party. The cause for celebration? Twenty years of collaboration between Longchamp and the American designer Jeremy Scott, plus the launch of the new limited-edition “Greetings From New York” Le Pliage bag.

Roberts, shown here, wound her way up the steps to the rooftop, where more drinks were served and all the different Jeremy Scott Pliage styles were on display.

For Gyllenhaal, the evening was something of a reunion between her and Sophie Delafontaine, Longchamp’s creative director. “I looked at her face and I was like, ‘We have met before,’” the actress told W at the party. “Sophie was like, ‘Yes we have, we met at this store,’ maybe even the opening of this store.” That was back in 2006, when the Jeremy Scott collabs first began—it was also “the year my daughter was born,” Gyllenhaal noted.

Scott and Delafontaine at the event.

Musician Chloe Flower made an appearance, wearing Longchamp’s kimono jacket with trumpet sleeves.

Lola Leon at the Longchamp x Jeremy Scott party.

Amanda Lepore, Joan Smalls, and CT Hedden at the Longchamp x Jeremy Scott party.

On May 19, guests gathered at Fendi’s Madison Avenue flagship in New York City to celebrate the Baguette 26424 Re-Edition. The name references the first model code assigned to the bag, which quickly became a signature silhouette of the house upon its 1997 release. The crowd featured friends of Fendi, including Blake Lively, Olivia Wilde, Ayra Starr, Delilah Belle Hamlin, Ella Hunt, Steph Hui, Deacon Phillippe, Lux Pascal, Esther McGregor, and Ivy Getty.

At the event, guests were treated to a preview of the new bags, available this July in 20 designs inspired by the Fendi archive, and first seen on the runway of Maria Grazia Chiuri’s fall 2026 debut collection.

The immersive evening also featured a look at the Baguette Lab, which, for a limited time, will provide complimentary restoration services for clients’ own vintage Baguettes.

Fine jewelry brand Brent Neale gathered some of New York’s most influential names on Tuesday, May 19, to celebrate the opening of its New York City salon. Hosted at the Astor Trust Building on Fifth Avenue, the 7,000-square-foot space was transformed into a new kind of jewelry showroom.

Guests including Blake Lively and Kate Mara were invited to browse an immersive display of the brand’s signature collections, one-of-a-kind creations, as well as the newest collection, Tides. They sipped cocktails and took in the glittering gems while enjoying the new, more personalized jewelry experience Brent Neale will soon launch to all clients.

On Saturday, May 16, Dia Beacon brought together a notable crowd of more than 600 members of the art, film, and fashion communities (including Paloma Elsesser, pictured here) to celebrate the Dia Art Foundation’s Spring Benefit. The gala—which started with a morning reception at Dia’s Gerhard Richter gallery before moving on to a lovely family-style spring lunch—paid tribute to artists John Chamberlain, Tehching Hsieh, Lee Ufan, Agnes Martin, Hélio Oiticica, Kishio Suga, and Jack Whitten, each of whom has had recent or upcoming exhibitions at the museum.

After lunch, guests were invited to wander the galleries and explore Dia’s grounds. Those in attendance included artists, philanthropists, gallerists, collectors, and other creatives including Alicia Keys, Steve McQueen, Derek Blasberg, Lauren Santo Domingo, Carrie Mae Weems, Laurie Simmons, Diamond Stingily, and many more.

The benefit also marked Dia Beacon’s new partnership with Chanel. Co-chairs included house designer Matthieu Blazy, Dia’s Board chair Nathalie de Gunzburg, and artists Joan Jonas and Lisa Yuskavage. Proceeds from the gala will support the museum’s ongoing programming, including installations, publications, and public educational initiatives.

On May 14 in New York City, Troye Sivan made his way to the Meatpacking District for a carnival-themed party thrown by Coach to celebrate its new collaboration with the Los Angeles-based creative collective Brain Dead. Sivan snapped photos in the cavernous space on West 14th Street, which had been filled with fairground treats and games like cotton candy stands, balloon popping, and even a cyclone-style amusement park ride installed inside.

Launching globally on May 29, the collection features lots of playful touches, like the cartoon sketched onto the leather bag gymnast Suni Lee is pictured holding, with creative director Stuart Vevers, above. (Vevers’s children were also in attendance for the party; the VIP tots spent the evening running from popcorn stand to merch booth to miniature golf.) Inspirations for the capsule include Tokyo street style, collectible souvenir culture, and merch the designers dreamed up that would be sold at this fictional amusement park.

A surprise runway show took place midway through the night, putting all the wares from the collection on display.

Vevers took a bow with Brain Dead cofounder and creative director Kyle Ng while guests like Lourdes Leon, Aquaria, and Ella Emhoff cheered them on.

Gold House hosted its fifth annual Gold Gala at the Music Center in downtown Los Angeles on Saturday, May 9. The event brought together over 650 of the most influential Asian-Pacific and multicultural leaders across industries, all dressed in “heritage-inspired black tie” from AAPI designers.

Bowen Yang opened the show with a monologue before an array of awards were handed out to actors Charles Melton and Simu Liu and Olympic freestyle skier Eileen Gu, among others. Hayley Kiyoko performed her song, “Girls Like Girls,” while H.E.R. and Liza Soberano shared an exclusive first look at their upcoming film, Forgotten Island.

Guests took in the show while enjoying a three-course dinner from chef Justin Pichetrungsi and drinks provided by Hennessy. When the programming came to an end, attendees let loose at the Billboard x Gold House Founders Party. There, RuPaul’s Drag Race stars Nymphia Wind and Plastique Tiara performed before Mortal Kombat II star Joe Taslim took the stage for a DJ set.

It was not your average book club on April 28, when friends of Valentino gathered together at the Marciano Art Foundation in Los Angeles. This was a high-fashion evening, though the reason for the event was a book. The night was dedicated to the launch of Specula Mundi by Mark Borthwick, the new haute couture tome with a visual narrative that reinterprets the collection of the same name by Alessandro Michele.

Patricia Arquette, Maude Apatow, Sombr, and more stars were in attendance, dressed in their Valentino best. Those who missed the presentation of the collection in Paris last January were transported there thanks to a Kaiserpanorama installation on-site.

The hottest accessory of the evening was, of course, Specula Mundi, produced in a limited edition of 1,500 numbered copies. A close runner-up was the new Valentino Garavani Devain bag, held by Arquette and Apatow, among others.

Teyana Taylor pregamed the Met Gala at the event, showing up in a romantic black dress.

Tate McRae attended in an animal print jacket from Valentino’s pre-fall 2026 collection and a Devain bag.

On April 28, the arts nonprofit Creative Time invited New York's art and fashion worlds into the Russian Tea Room for its 2026 gala. Over borscht and vodka, guests celebrated the organization's new Executive Director, Jean Cooney, and honored artists Guadalupe Maravilla, Molly Gochman, and philanthropist Michelle Coffey. Co-chaired by stylist Kate Young, designer Waris Ahluwalia, and Nordstrom, the night was unexpectedly full of Russian bears. Waiters dressed as polar bears toted bottles of vodka while guests—from artists Kara Walker and Chloe Wise to designers Daniella Kallmeyer, Wes Gordon, and Henry Zankov—mingled around a giant bear-shaped ice sculpture. The night ended late, with dancing to sets by Leigh Lezark of The Misshapes and Jean d'Armes.

Gala season in New York City is officially in full swing. Apex for Youth—an organization that mentors and supports underserved Asian and immigrant youth in NYC—hosted its annual fete on April 16 at Cipriani South Street. The event drew over 600 guests and raised nearly $3.7 million for the nonprofit, which offers health-focused programming, education, and community engagement via volunteers. Olympic champion Eileen Gu, shown here with Michael Chung, attended the event, along with actress Lana Condor, who received honors.

“The Inspiration Awards Gala is one of the few moments where you can see the full ecosystem of Apex in one room—our youth, mentors, supporters, and partners,” executive director of Apex for Youth Jiyoon Chung told W. “It’s powerful because the impact is tangible. You’re not just hearing about change—you’re witnessing the relationships and community that make it possible.” That sentiment proved true when Avantika Vandanapu, pictured here, presented Condor her award onstage.

Of course, the dinnertime auction is as key for a gala as the starry guest list. During the evening, guests like Kim Shui—photographed here with Chloe Misseldine and Isiah Magsino—Sandy Liang, Dao-Yi Chow, and many other New York City insiders helped raise nearly $4 million for Apex for Youth.

Next up on April 15 was The Bronx Museum of the Arts, which held its annual gala at Tribeca Rooftop this year. Artist Awol Erizku, cultural patron Lois Plehn, and designer and artist Colm Dillane (aka KidSuper)—pictured here with The Bronx Museum’s director and chief curator, Shamim M. Momin—received honors during the stylish party, which included dinner and a live auction.

Joey Bada$$ and Ferg, shown here, were also in attendance for the soirée—the museum’s most important yearly fund-raiser, which also served as a welcome party for Momin, who threw her first Bronx Museum gala that evening.

Tyrell Hampton at The Bronx Museum’s gala.

Alex Consani may be known as a downtown fashion darling, but on Friday, April 10, the model traveled to Times Square for a party celebrating the acclaimed artist Tomokazu Matsuyama’s latest work. Along with Lulu Tenney, Hank Willis Thomas, and many more art-world stars, Consani feted Matsuyama’s new piece, Morning Again, with a soirée that began at the Times Square EDITION and ended on the Red Steps—where Consani joined Matsuyama to watch the project illuminate Times Square.

Commissioned by the Times Square Arts Midnight Moment program, Morning Again will screen nightly from April 1-30 from 11:57 PM to midnight, on nearly 100 electronic billboards in Times Square.

In the piece, the Japanese–born, New York–based artist Matsuyama—pictured here with Hank Willis Thomas—traces four symbolic currents that move through New York City: flows of hope, rhythm, self-expression, and transformation.

On the afternoon of Wednesday, March 26, Movado toasted its latest chapter at New York’s King restaurant, where brand president Margot Grinberg hosted a seated lunch along with ambassador Julianne Moore. The gathering marked the debut of three new women’s watch collections—Museum Bangle, Heritage 1917, and Museum Velura—as well as the official launch of Curve, Movado’s newest high-fashion jewelry collection. All were showcased alongside archival designs.

“I’ve always admired Movado for its clean, modern aesthetic and its ability to create pieces that feel both timeless and deeply personal,” said Moore. “These new collections are beautifully crafted and thoughtfully designed—a true reflection of the brand’s artistry and its commitment to celebrating women.”

On Thursday, March 19, guests gathered for an intimate dinner at The Odeon hosted by Loewe and Bergdorf Goodman. The party celebrated Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez’s first collection as Loewe’s new creative directors as well as the house’s takeover of Bergdorf’s famed windows.

American Love Story star Grace Gummer and Mark Ronson joined the exclusive group, carrying his-and-hers Amazona bags.

True Whitaker also joined the event, whose guests included Britt Lower, Michael Stipe, Jayme Lawson, Sandra Bernhard, Morgan Spector, Lucas Hedges, Isaac Powell, Talia Ryder, Tramell Tillman, and more.

Along with the collection launch, McCollough and Hernandez collaborated with Bergdorf Goodman on exclusive custom windows and an interior installation in the brand’s women’s store, bringing their spring 2026 collection to life.

On March 18 in Manhattan’s Union Square neighborhood, Dua Lipa descended upon the new Nespresso flagship boutique on 5th Avenue. Wearing a white minidress and a stunning Serpenti necklace, the singer toasted her status as the coffee brand’s latest global ambassador. Guests sipped on espresso martinis (like DJ Mia Moretti, above) and plucked tuna crispy rice bites from geometric blocks held by the waitstaff. As the sun set outside, the crowd trooped downstairs for more dancing.

Dua Lipa at the Nespresso party.

Meanwhile, farther uptown at The Pool/The Grill, art-world luminaries gathered to celebrate the 16th annual Art Production Fund gala. The event—which supports the organization’s work of commissioning and producing public art projects—raised a record-breaking $1 million. More than 300 guests including Chloe Wise and Brooke Wise, along with gallerista Hannah Traore (shown above) attended, decked out in fashion that reflected the theme of the night: après ski at the “APF Chalet.”

Legendary artists like Marilyn Minter and Sanford Biggers showed up for APF, whose executive director, Casey Fremont, can be seen here with the duo.

Spring brings countless galas to New York City, but we’re pretty sure there’s only one where you’ll find the city’s premiere “experimental clown” performing as one of artist Paul McCarthy’s famed butt plugs and donors will get called “pay pigs.” Welcome to Performance Space New York’s annual spring gala, where this year, the best way to do some good was to be very, very bad.

Playwright Jordan Tannahill, fresh off his off-Broadway success Prince Faggot, stepped into the role of creative director and reimagined a kink-friendly gala with a “Haute Fetish” dress code that that meant black leather was more common than black tie. This year’s gala honored fashion’s Michèle Lamy, artist McCarthy, and writer Samuel R. Delany, all creatives who no one has ever accused of being prudes. Naturally, Tannahill called in former dominatrix Julia Fox and her BFF, the photographer and model Richie Shazam, to cohost. Dressed as a gala table to open the night, Fox reminded the crowd this was a kink-friendly event. She pulled up comedian Julio Torres onstage to interrogate him about his favorite kink. “A memorable, entertaining night supporting the arts,” he demurred.

French singer Yseult, long-known for making a statement on the Cannes red carpet, made her United States performance debut with her new single “Freak” accompanied by a BDSM performance by Mistress Nina, Dahlia Damoiselle, and Tristan Allen.

Moses Sumney performed a multisong tribute to Lamy, including his first performance of his song “Rank & File” in years.

Performance artist and clown Alex Tatarsky’s tribute to Paul McCarthy was undoubtedly one of the evening’s most delightfully weird moments.

Right as the elevator doors were about to close and take us to the fifth floor of the WSA building for Free Arts NYC’s 26th Annual Gala, none other than Rosie Perez slipped in. There’s no better omen for a good night in the city than starting it with an accidental run-in with one of its cultural icons. Once inside, we were greeted with a glass of red wine and gallery walls full of 70 works on paper by a who’s-who of art-world notables, including Tschabalala Self, KAWS, Will Cotton, and Marilyn Minter. They would all be auctioned off that night through an online portal to benefit the nonprofit. Even New York’s new first lady, Rama Duwaji, donated a sketch.

Founded in 1997, Free Arts NYC provides kids from underserved communities with both daylong creative workshops for younger artists and more in-depth mentorship and scholarship programs for teenage artists.

This year’s edition honored three women from three different generations: artists Katherine Bradford and Sasha Gordon, and Jody Quon, creative director of New York magazine. Yet the three didn’t just show up to collect their adoration on gala night. Earlier in the year, the trio stopped by to both offer advice and create alongside Free Arts students. The results—“exquisite corpse”-style drawings—were also on display.

“Free Arts is planting seeds of curiosity that will undeniably make this world more beautiful,” Quon said upon accepting her award. “We are not just investing in children’s art. We are investing in the next generation of thinkers, makers, leaders, and dreamers.”

Stylist and editor Alastair Mckimm and photographer Carin Backoff represented the fashion world.

This was the rare gala for an arts foundation in which the act of creation literally took center stage. Artist Adam Dressner had set up an easel to paint live portraits of guests during both the cocktail hour and after party. At dinner, guests were provided with colored pencils and encouraged to draw on the table by Free Arts founder Liz Hopfan. Paper had been placed over some windows, with crayons provided to encourage guests to leave a doodle. “A sketch is a funny thing,” she told the crowd. “We tend to think of it as lesser, the thing before the thing. But a sketch is where we are all most honestly ourselves. It's a color test, a first instinct, a page that was never meant to be seen. This is where Free Arts lives, too.”

Nike

On February 15, Nike closed out All-Star Weekend in Los Angeles with All-Time High, a star-studded after party at the members-only Bird Streets Club on Sunset Boulevard. The event wrapped up the weekend and celebrated the intersection of sports and entertainment, bringing together figures across industries like Teyana Taylor, Travis Scott, Damson Idris, Takashi Murakami, Steve Lacy, Ego Nwodim, and more.

Nike

Zack Bia was on deck, DJing for the crowd, followed by a lineup that included Chase B, Coco & Breezy, and Hank Korsan.

Nike

The event space had a sprawling setup, where guests could move between three different floors, each with their own unique feel. The layout lent itself to the eclectic crowd that had gathered there, which also included musician Shaboozey.

Bulgari

Eternal beauty was the theme of the night at the Bulgari event held at the luxury jewelry brand’s Rodeo Drive flagship on January 15. VIP clients, celebrities, and creatives came together to celebrate Bulgari Eternal, a new collection breathing new life into archival designs.

Bulgari

Maude Apatow, Phoebe Dynevor, and Ryan Destiny were in attendance on Thursday night, enjoying the conversation and immersive experiences on offer. Apatow and Destiny, specifically, acted as models for the evening, wearing the new collection while enjoying rooftop cocktails and the celebratory atmosphere.

Bulgari

The mood was set by Kaytranada and Kim Gordon, who both delivered DJ sets for the guests, keeping the energy high throughout the evening. It was a true L.A. party, celebrating glitz, glamour, and, of course, Bulgari.

item.title: Jennifer Lopez’s Take on the Embroidered Coat Trend Is the Most Opulent Yet
item.description: At the premiere of her new concert film, the ever-extravagant superstar went full diva in a colorful, crystal-embellished robe.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Jennifer Lopez has never met an extravagant style moment she didn’t like, so leave it to her to put an over-the-stop spin on this season’s biggest coat trend.

Last night, the superstar looked downright decadent at the Los Angeles premiere of The JLO Show: Live in Las Vegas, a concert film capturing her 12-show residency in Las Vegas earlier this year. True to form, she brought high-octane glam to the red carpet, wearing a look from Dolce & Gabbana’s Alta Moda collection. Her sheer Chantilly lace gown was a statement in itself, but it was the satin shawl she wore overtop that truly stole the show. Adorned with bright silk flowers, crystals, and trailing fringe, the shearling number made the entire ensemble theatrical and impossible to miss.

Lopez is but the latest A-lister to wear a such a regal formal coat. The style, comprising a fur-trimmed collar, silk fabrication, and all-over intricate embroidery, has taken off among It girls in recent months. One of the most prominent iterations comes from designer Conner Ives, who has dressed Kendall Jenner and Hailey Bieber in his demi-couture robes. Most recently, at The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping premiere, Jennifer Lawrence gave the aesthetic a queenly finish, wearing a floor-grazing Dior design by Jonathan Anderson with nothing underneath.

Lopez herself has also had an affinity for the style, wearing a different Dolce & Gabbana Alta Moda design—also lined with trailing fringe and adorned in colorful flowers—to the L.A. Opera 2026 Opening Night Gala last month. But while that version was giving vintage après-ski, her latest look is more snow-queen appropriate. Naturally, while walking the carpet at her film premiere, she amped up the opulence with yellow diamonds from the Italian brand’s Alta Gioielleria 2026 collection.

Known for her more-is-more taste, the 57-year-old singer has been unsurprisingly going all out on her film press tour—sporting everything from pantless Marc Jacobs looks to head-to-toe red-wine dressing. All things considered, it was only a matter of time until she reimagined the fashion-girl robe with her over-the-top glamour.
