item.title: 60 Luxury Holiday Gifts for Your Chicest Loved Ones
item.description: From Louis Vuitton's impeccable beauty line to Gucci's sleek leather turtleneck and everything in between.
item.dc:creator: Maryam Lieberman
item.content:encoded:
Most gift guides promise something for everyone. But this one is for the people who have everything—your friends, family, and loved ones with impeccable taste, the ones you’d happily give the moon (if only the moon met their standards. But some Louis Vuitton will do, of course). We’ve done the hunting, from small luxuries that punch above their price point to showstoppers worth gushing over. Below, peruse our compilation of recent and forever favorites that will make even the most discerning recipient light up.

Chanel Sublimage L'Extrait de Crème L'Érin de Voyage Cream

This is the beauty gift for the person who truly has everything, except perhaps a good reason to get out of bed and do their skincare routine. Chanel’s Sublimage L’Extrait de Crème is obviously some serious skin indulgence, but we must say the real pièce de résistance is the lacquered case. It’s so beautiful, you’ll keep it long after the product is done.

Tiffany HardWear Necklace in Gold With Pearls and Turquoise

It bears repeating that a little old-school glamour still goes a long, long way. Inspired by a design from Tiffany & Co.’s 1962 archives, this 18-karat yellow gold necklace with Akoya pearls and turquoise has that rare, untouchable chicness that’s never dated. Wear it long or doubled up (our preference). This is a piece for a lifetime.

Gucci Horsebit Python Bag

Consider this your permission to put something spectacular under your own tree. A little reward for all those hours of hard work, this silver python Horsebit is equal parts sexy, statement-making, and endlessly tempting for evening.

Louis Vuitton Diago High Vase by Patricia Urquiola

Make your home gift memorable—why settle for the obligatory silver frame or crystal piece? The Louis Vuitton Diago High Vase, designed by Patricia Urquiola in lilac or seafoam green glass with LV perforated leather detailing, is a far more striking proposition. It’s sculptural, unexpected, and compelling with flowers inside (or not!).

Cartier Panthère de Cartier necklace

Because she has super-sharp taste and her entrances are studied by everyone in the room, this Cartier necklace is pure provocation, and perfect for her. Fashioned in 18-karat gold with onyx accents and emerald eyes, this long necklace features a chic panther medallion with tassels.

Hermès Faubourg Cuff Bracelet

This one is clearly for someone with a strong point of view on dressing, with just the right amount of fashionable edge. We love this chic, substantial accent that works as well with a crisp white shirt as it does with a black evening gown.

La Beauté Louis Vuitton Scott Lipstick Case

Smaller in scale but singular in presence, this season’s most coveted Louis Vuitton beauty-centric launch turns up the volume on glam traveling. The monogrammed piece is a gorgeous, timeless color and defines what luxe leather collectables are all about.

Dior J'Adior Pump

These beauties are stylish, pared-back, and impossible to overdo. Dior’s four-inch pumps are a fabulous gift to elevate her jeans-and-black-turtleneck look—or give her Little Black Dress effortless élan.

Guerlain Météorites Prestige Edition Jewel Case

Because subtlety is overrated, especially when it comes to holiday gift-giving. Guerlain’s glow-inducing pearls of multicolor makeup arrive in a jewel-worthy case, complete with its own kabuki brush. This product is entirely too gorgeous to hide in a makeup bag.

Chanel Cruise 2026/27 Earrings

A little irreverence goes a long way, particularly when Chanel is involved. These gold-tone metal-and-resin earrings from the house’s cruise 2026/2027 collection are both playful and polished.

Cartier Love Unlimited Flexible Diamond Bracelet

We all know the Love bracelet needs no introduction. But this pink-gold version, set with diamonds and designed with a flexible construction, offers a more unexpected take on a familiar icon. Wear it solo, without another bracelet in sight (a little Parisian insouciance, if you will).

Fendi Croissant Bag

The effortless edge here is undeniable—the distressed tasseled leather gives this piece a lived-in, rock-and-roll feel from day one. Pair with your jeans and thigh-high boots and you’ve got a look you will reach for season after season.

Dior Medium Initials Hobo Bag

Meet the everyday bag finally done right in a beautiful leather. Jonathan Anderson’s Dior proves elegant and easy can be the same thing.

Gucci Flora Gorgeous Gift Set

Gucci’s recent fragrance game has been especially strong, and this whimsical jasmine-and-gardenia blend is no exception. Effortlessly feminine, the set includes an eau de parfum, body lotion, and travel-size spray.

Loewe Medium Sally Flamenco Clutch

The Flamenco bag is a stunner, with luminous shades and a shape that will outlast every trend. Give it to the woman who lives for color, or the one who’s worn nothing but black for years. Both will fall in love with the accessory instantly.

La Beauté Louis Vuitton Lip Pencils and Case

Never lose track of your lip pencils while traveling again. This gorgeously, timeless case houses ten beautiful colors, from perfectly curated nudes to classic reds and everything in between.

Chanel Cruise 2026/27 Clutch With Leather Strap

We love this piece for a multitude of reasons: it’s a little Aspen, a little Gstaad, and entirely Chanel. The neutral palette has an après-ski nonchalance, but there’s nothing ordinary about it. The zip closure keeps essentials tucked away, while the silhouette does the fashion talking. It’s practical, yes, but that’s hardly the first thing you’ll notice about this bag.

Pat McGrath Labs The Complete Lip Artistry Vault

For the lipstick devotee, here are 12 (yes, 12!) perfected shades from Pat McGrath Labs. This gift is like a years-long celebratory wardrobe for the lips, with liners to match.

Estée Lauder Estée Treasures Perfume Compact

The most memorable beauty gifts are the ones that blur the line between vanity and collecting. Inspired by Estée Lauder’s 1965 holiday collection, this turquoise compact—with its mother-of-pearl and tortoiseshell hues—has the appeal of a vintage jewel. Inside, the solid scent of Beautiful Magnolia lends a soft, feminine finish that is impossible not to love.

Ferragamo Hug Handbag

This is one of Ferragamo’s most refined seasons yet—and the mini Hug handbag is another fabulous example of creative director Maximilian Davis’s chic vision. This piece is plush, luxe, and totally covetable.

Bottega Venetta Intrecciato Credit Card Case

We can’t stay away from a little everyday luxury in the prettiest shade of pink. Bottega’s buttery-soft leather is in a class of its own, and the signature Intrecciato weave makes this far more than just a cardholder. It is a work of art!

La Mer The Calming Hydration Collection

A La Mer devotee is not easily tempted elsewhere, and this set only reinforces that sense of loyalty. Packed with the brand’s complexion essentials, it’s a welcome excuse to replenish their favorites. And for what it’s worth, it’s a very satisfying gift to unwrap.

Augustinus Bader The Supreme Collection

Someone has clearly been very good this year. With eleven full-size Augustinus Bader formulas for face, body, and hair, this will be a Christmas morning to make even Santa reconsider his own skincare routine.

HigherDose Full Spectrum Infrared Sauna

The best part? You don’t have to go anywhere. This at-home sauna is your own private indulgence, whenever you want it. No booking, no crowds, just you, the heat, and a door that transports you to glowing skin, detoxification, muscle recovery, better sleep, and less anxiety (seriously).

Bulgari Tubogas Necklace

Some gifts are destined to elicit an audible reaction, like this one—a nod to the Bulgari archives, a little modernist bravado, and coming in an utterly covetable shade of blue. This 18-karat yellow gold Tubogas necklace, set with a central blue topaz and pavé diamonds, epitomizes enduring style. It needs no occasion, of course, but Christmas makes for a very good excuse.

Giorgio Facchini Onyx Sculptural Ring in 18k Gold

For the fashion iconoclast who loves a statement and wears it with confidence, this Giorgio Fachini ring is impossible not to love. Eighteen-karat yellow gold is capped with a disc-shaped onyx that will stun from the moment it’s on the hand.

Christofle Tray x Sisley

This is beyond good taste on every level: Sisley for the skin, Christofle for the home. Two icons of French luxury come together in a set that pairs Sisley’s exacting approach to skincare with a beautifully etched Christofle tray designed by Christine d’Ornano.

La Beauté Louis Vuitton Beauty Makeup Duo Gift Set

This is a gift duo that balances thoughtful formulation with understated polish. The LV Ombrés 150 Beige Memento refillable eyeshadow compact pairs squalane and camellia seed oils with a texture designed to help keep creasing in check, while the LV Rouge 105 Nude Nécessaire lipstick brings a complementary wash of color that you simply can’t get wrong (because who doesn’t love a good nude lip?).

Ferragamo Adjustable Gancini Belt

The unexpected fashion pick of the person who already owns all the basics. In animal print, the Ferragamo Gancini belt polishes a white shirt and jeans and can cinch beautifully on a dress if you’re feeling daring.

Hermès Barénia Perfume Gift Set

No one can touch an iconic French scent, and Hermès is always a sure winner in the fragrance game. Barenia is fast becoming a modern classic, with sensual notes of chypre, oakwood, and patchouli. The set comes with a full-size bottle and travel spray, so you are never without the aromatic mood.

Gucci Soft Nappa Turtleneck

Gucci is testing everyone’s spending willpower this season. This one’s for the woman who has every It bag and shoe on the planet. Gucci’s buttery-soft nappa leather turtleneck is pure fashion attitude—sleek and subversive.

Louis Vuitton Multipass Mini Bag

Meet the bag to carry on repeat from fall through the New Year. We assure you it will be worn straight out of the gift box and never make it the closet, because that’s what happened to us.

Celluma Mystique LED Mask

When it comes to red light masks, Celluma is in a league of its own, bringing decades of photobiomodulation research to its newest product, which delivers precisely calibrated wavelengths and has energy output designed to deliver red-light therapy where it counts. A standout gift for the skincare devotee who wants the best, with the added appeal of red-light benefits for the scalp (!).

La Double J Mahjong Game

Mahjong shows no sign of losing its hand, and while there are plenty of luxe sets on the market, La DoubleJ’s is an especially fun choice. The color schemes are bold, the design has that unmistakable Italian flair, and it brings colorful joy to the game wherever you are playing.

Missoni Giacomo Face Towels

A gift for a new home, a guest bathroom in need of personality, or anyone whose getting-ready space deserves as much attention as the rest of the house. Missoni’s signature fiammato (zigzag) print brings an unexpected jolt of pattern and color.

Tata Harper Winter Nourishment Ritual

Here’s something for the clean-beauty devotee with high standards. This set brings together four of Tata Harper’s formulas for exfoliation, hydration, replenishment, and barrier support. Organically sourced ingredients and sustainable packaging round out the offering, housed in a verdant box that makes a beautiful first impression.

FoundRae Love Link Double Candle Holder

For someone who knows that the objects on a table are part of the pleasure of gathering around it. FoundRae’s sculptural brass double candle holder brings a touch of gold and a strong design to a dinner table or coffee table.

Hermès Succulent Sultan Beach Rackets

For the beach-house hosts who have received their share of wine and flowers, a pair of artfully designed beach rackets is a welcome change of pace. A little unexpected, genuinely fun, and likely to see far more use than another hostess bouquet.

Maison Francis Kurkdjian Paris Baccarat Rouge 540 Body Oil and Perfume Set

A fragrance gift that always lands, this for the woman with timeless taste. Baccarat Rouge 540 is an iconic scent for a reason (it is, notably, Rihanna’s favorite), and pairing it with body oil makes an already exceptional fragrance gift that much better.

Bulgari Omnia Crystalline Kit

Here’s a beautiful and pleasing scent for all to love. This is a delightful pear and lotus incantation that comes with a full-size bottle and a cute travel size option.

Le Labo Discovery Set

For the fragrance obsessive and the perpetually undecided, this set is an excuse to experiment. Seventeen 1.5ml samples, plus a 50ml bottle, cover plenty of olfactory ground, from the heady Jasmine 17 and understated Lavande 31 to the cult-favorite Santal 33.

Hourglass The Bestsellers Set

Some gifts are a gamble, but this is a guaranteed home run, especially if your recipient is on the more youthful side. Hourglass has packed four of its greatest hits into one very luxe package: a full-size Phantom Volumizing Glossy Balm in Slip, Unlocked Instant Extensions Mascara in Ultra Black, Ambient Lighting Edit Unlocked in Hope, and a limited-edition Ambient Lighting Edit Brush II in Love. It all comes tucked inside a vegan leather makeup pouch.

Anyon Atelier Brass Match Strikers

In this clever home gift, the brass has just enough polish to work in both modern and traditional interiors. Plus, there’s something satisfying about giving a gift that won’t be relegated to the back of a cupboard. Anyon Atelier’s match holder comes in a small and large option, and unlike the candle it accompanies, this product has staying power.

Bonjout Beauty L'Édition Bonjout Gift Set

Some skincare gifts are best judged a few weeks after Christmas, when your loved one starts noticing the difference in their complexion. Bonjout’s pairing of face cream and balm is an invitation to discover a new favorite, and the sort of introduction to a brand that can turn a first-time user into a serious loyalist. Trust us, this French label is worth checking out.

Knesko Skin Gold Repair and Rose Quartz Sculpting Set

The Knesko Sculpting Set pairs its beloved glow-giving face oil with a heart-shaped rose quartz gua sha for facial sculpting and lymphatic drainage. It’s perfect for pre-party prep or an evening ritual to boost circulation and de-puffing.

Liis Forest Sounds Eau de Parfum

Whoever gets this gift will fall in love with this fabulous and unique fragrance that has a limited-edition bottle designed by painter Abel Macias. Forest Sounds feels destined for cult-classic status especially for those who find gourmands a little too dessert menu and florals a little too basic. This yuzu green masterpiece has a transportive depth that hits just right.

Diptyque Holiday Lantern for Classic Candle

Give the candle lover something to watch while they enjoy the flaming aroma: Diptyque’s’s pine tree lantern dotted with golden stars turns the flame skyward, throwing dazzling moving shadows around the room.

Byredo Trois Encens Incense

For the person whose home should smell as considered as their personal style, this set pairs three of Byredo’s signature fragrances with an engraved wooden incense holder. A welcome departure from the predictable candle, it offers a different way to scent a room.

Dries Van Noten Lipstick Duo Set

Because it’s so pretty in presentation and on the lips, it’s a lovely gift. Dries Van Noten offers two fine lipsticks and a sheer balm in this set.

Dyson CameraJet Electric Toothbrush

A toothbrush may not strike everyone as a sexy holiday gift, but there might be someone in your life who takes their oral hygiene very seriously. If so, Dyson’s new CameraJet is an elevated option, all the way. Using a microscopic camera and AI to identify gaps between teeth, it combines brushing and precision-flossing in one rather ingenious kit.

T3 Aire 360 Ceramic Air Styler

If they’re the type to cancel plans for a proper hair night, the T3 Aire 360 is a gift that understands their need for perfection. The new Rouge edition combines a compact, dual-voltage design with ceramic attachments for bouncy curls or a voluminous blowout.

Biologique Recherche The Vivant Set

Good skin is a gift that keeps on giving. Biologique Recherche brings together its iconic Masque Vivant and blemish-control serum here—two serious players in the complexion department, and a proper skincare splurge.

Santa Maria Novella The Melograno Body Selection

If they can happily lose an hour (or two) in a bath, Santa Maria Novella’s Melograno bath salts are a healing indulgence with panache. There is something gratifying about gifting a pleasure that rarely makes it onto anyone’s to-buy list, particularly when it comes from one of Florence’s most storied apothecaries.

Gucci Herbarium Tray Set

Because one catchall is never enough, these botanical-print porcelain beauties bring a little Gucci glamour to every room. You can use this to coral rings, bedside odds and ends, or whatever deserves a prettier landing spot.

iS Clinical Hydrate + Renew Essentials

For the peel devotee who takes their skincare seriously, this is a high-mark skincare set from iS Clinical that’ll provide a skin-renewing and rejuvenating regimen all winter long.

Victoria Beckham Beauty Eye Wardrobe Collection

Here’s a makeup gift that punches well above its price tag. Beckham’s Bordeaux collection makes a case for the burgundy palette on everyone, whether they’re blonde, brunette, blue-eyed or brown-eyed. The set includes a refillable eye compact that works all year, black mascara, and the new Bordeaux Pavé kajal liner flecked with gold and ruby.

Tory Burch Sublime Shimmer Oil

There’s no shortage of shimmer oils, but after testing so many, this one gets the balance just right: a beautiful, subtle gleam without veering into disco-ball territory. The Sublime scent is another selling point—the title says it all. Adding a little shimmer to our holiday outfits? Don’t mind if we do.

Evolvetogether Hand Care Set

This is hand wash for people who notice all the details while inspecting your powder room. Housed inside plant-derived, sustainable packaging, this set comes with a nourishing hand cream that earns its place in your purse, too.

Seed to Skin The Tuscan Escape Ritual

If you’re seeking an elevated gesture to gift that isn’t too loud, we recommend this little slice of Tuscan escape, minus the ten-hour flight and airfare. Seed to Skin, the spa-world insider favorite, brings its particular brand of indulgence home with the Borgo Air Candle and Cloud Nectar bath treatment.

Little Joe Woman Walker Bag

They’ll use it for every holiday, guaranteed. The deep tan iteration of this bag is especially beautiful for leisurely getaways, and it’s a favorite among the jet-set crowd for good reason. It’s the sort of bag you’ll spot everywhere, from beach escapes to hotel restaurants.

item.title: Rihanna’s Daughter Rocki Trades Her Dior Diaper for a Moto Jacket
item.description: The one-year-old made her fashion campaign debut in the house's new ads alongside mom.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Twersky Winkler
item.content:encoded:
The fashion calendar can be a confounding thing. Just when the weather warms up and the public starts shedding layers, unearthing long-abandoned sundresses—brands begin releasing their fall collections. Now, autumn has arrived—and the fall 2026 campaigns that have rolled out all summer are providing tons of fashion and accessories inspiration for cooler temps. You might have spent May-through-August observing the laissez-faire French attitudes of Celine’s offerings to come, or daydreaming about the drama of Balenciaga’s Celine Song-directed world. Remember those pieces that called out to you months ago? Feel free to peruse the looks that will be everywhere for the coming season, and check back here often once you’re mentally ready to dive into some seriously chic fall fashion.

Dior

Rocki Irish Mayers is barely one year old, and already she is a star. The youngest child and only daughter of Rihanna and A$AP Rocky made her debut on W’s Pop Issue cover earlier this year in a Dior haute couture diaper. Now, she’s front and center with her mother in the latest Lady Dior campaign.

Dior

Rihanna is joined by her child in matching leather jackets with the pink, feminine Lady Dior by their sides. The images display Rihanna’s multidimensionality. She is a mother, an artist, a muse, and so much more.

Saint Laurent

Is there anything more quintessentially Saint Laurent than a sharp suit? In 1966, Yves Saint Laurent introduced Le Smoking to the world and challenged the rules by which women got dressed. Decades later, it remains a sartorial emblem of independence and modernity.

Saint Laurent

In honor of Le Smoking’s 60th anniversary, Saint Laurent is bringing the production of Le Smoking back to its atelier next year. There, Le Smoking will once again be made according to the traditions of French tailoring for both women and men.

Saint Laurent

The anniversary also called for a campaign, shot by Mark Kean, and starring a cast of familiar personalities. Anok Yai, Connor Storrie, Rosé, Zoë Kravitz, Anja Rubik, Kate Moss, Charli xcx, and more don Le Smoking. Together, they prove Le Smoking isn’t simply a part of Saint Laurent history. It is also the brand’s present and future.

Balenciaga

It’s Le City bag’s 25th anniversary, and Balenciaga has invited Damien Hirst to join the celebration. The artist produced a limited-edition series of bags featuring a multitude of Hirst’s most popular motifs decorating the classic accessory.

Balenciaga

The campaign takes the Damienciaga bags (as they’re called) around the world. Friends of the house tote the accessory in various cities, like L.A., Paris, and Shanghai. In Los Angeles, Nicole Richie returns as the ultimate Le City champion—a Y2K icon with a Y2K icon—alongside Rachel Sennott.

Balenciaga

“My Balenciaga bags have been with me through every era of my life,” Richie said. “They’ve only gotten better with age, and you know what? So have I!”

Self-Portrait

Self-Portrait’s ongoing collaboration with Jisoo continues. The brand has released “Portraits of a Woman in Motion,” a series of videos capturing the singer against different fast-paced backdrops. Despite the chaos around her, Jisoo remains calm, serene, and unmistakably stylish.

Moncler

When reinterpreting outerwear icons, it makes sense to look to cultural icons as well. It is fitting, then, that Moncler tapped Cher, Jennie, and Grace Jones as the faces of its latest Moncler Re/Icons collection.

Moncler

Inspired by archival photographs of alpine pioneer Lionel Terray, the campaign honors the three women as pioneers in their own right. They are captured in bold portraits wearing updated versions of Moncler’s most famous pieces.

Moncler

“Pioneering spirit is just going forward and being tough,” says Cher, pictured in the campaign wearing the Re/Icons Verone jacket in black. The piece is accessorized by a yellow scarf, a reference to a Bob Mackie scarf dress she once wore on The Cher Show.

Gucci

After a runway show that took over Times Square this past May, Gucci is sticking to a New York state of mind, photographing the GucciCore campaign in the city that never sleeps.

Gucci

The plurality of both GucciCore and New York are at play in the Peter Funch-shot images. Models walk the city streets, on their way to work, a dinner, or nowhere in particular. Despite the number of people who crowd the block, the Gucci-adorned have no problem standing out, thanks to Demna’s designs.

Dr. Martens

Shoe brand Dr. Martens wants to know, “What makes your sole bounce?” The question is posed on every Dr. Martens heel loop. With its new initiative, “With Bouncing Soles,” the footwear label hopes to answer it. The program is designed to connect product, craft, culture, and community through one shared story.

Dr. Martens

Dr. Martens tapped a cast of globally recognized creative voices, cultural pioneers, and community changemakers for the autumn 2026 campaign coinciding with the launch of “With Bouncing Soles.” Chloë Sevigny is one of those cultural pioneers—the actor and style icon stars in the images wearing both the 1460 boot and the 8065 Mary Jane in a new, cherry-red finish.

Dr. Martens

“I’ve always been drawn to pieces that become more personal the longer you live in them, and Dr. Martens has always represented that for me,” Sevigny said in a statement. “I love that the campaign starts with such a simple question: What makes your sole bounce? For me, it’s staying curious—taking on new roles, finding inspiration in unexpected places, and always being open to what’s next.”

Burberry

In honor of 170 years of Burberry outerwear, the brand tapped 170 individuals across London, New York, Seoul, and Shanghai to bring their own perspectives to ten staples of the label.

Burberry

The worlds of art, literature, sports, music, and, of course, fashion are represented in the casting, with each individual shot on the city street they call home. “For 170 years, our outerwear has adapted to the weather and the way we dress,” says Burberry chief creative officer Daniel Lee. “Each portrait is different, but together they capture individuality and self-expression.”

Burberry

Knicks player OG Anunoby is, naturally, shot in New York City wearing a subtly checked Highlands Puffer jacket. London native Lila Moss throws a trench over a metallic mini in the U.K. capital. The cast is rounded out by Pat Cleveland, Connie Fleming, and Gabé Doppelt. All of the Burberry classics are on display, exhibiting the versatility and longevity of the brand’s outerwear.

Maison Margiela

Rebecca Hall is preparing for her next role. In the trailer for Anonymity, Maison Margiela’s fall campaign film, she plays an actress forced to confront her own identity. But the face she sees before her is covered, adorned with an artisanal mask from the French fashion house.

Maison Margiela

The retro-style trailer, which features looks from Margiela’s fall/winter 2026 collection, raises the stakes and asks the questions: Who are you? Who is real? And how can we truly know ourselves? Hall tries to answer these and more as she’s constantly confronted with faceless figures, all adorned extravagantly but remaining anonymous.

Chanel

Matthieu Blazy is throwing a party, and everyone’s invited. The reason for the fete? Chanel’s fall/winter 2026 collection, inspired by the caterpillar-to-butterfly transition.

Chanel

Awar Odhiang, Bhavitha Mandava, Noor Khan, and more models gather in Coco Chanel’s apartment. It’s a full house at 31 Rue Cambon in Paris, but the more, the merrier. It just means there’s a bigger audience to admire the clothing.

Chanel

Tweeds shimmer with lurex, and beading adds dimension to a jacket. There is an extravagance to the pieces, but also a wearability. A bubblegum-pink suede bomber is precious while simultaneously practical. A gathered black dress rids the need for accessories thanks to a flower blooming on the back.

Fendi

Fendi’s latest campaign for its iconic Peekaboo bag centers around the connection between the brand and the world of cinema. The newest expression of the accessory, designed by Maria Grazia Chiuri, is showcased on the arms of Monica Bellucci and Yara Shahidi in the Laura Sciacovelli-shot images.

Fendi

The campaign unfolds on a film set as Sciacovelli’s lens reveals the bones of the movie-making process, blurring the lines between performance and reality. Each woman’s bag boasts their initials, turning the accessory into a personal totem, the perfect accompaniment to a life that’s lived both on and off set.

Givenchy

Sarah Burton invited Givenchy’s extended “family” to star in the brand’s winter 2026 campaign. Eva Herzigova, Kaia Gerber, and the French writer and former lawyer Constance Debré represent the array of identities, ages, and sense of femininity that inspires Burton and illuminates the new world of Givenchy.

Givenchy

The models pose for Juergen Teller’s camera, showing off Burton’s latest designs before a landscape of steely granite in Croatia. The images are unflinching as each woman impresses an unsparing sense of her selfhood upon the imagery.

Givenchy

“There’s a directness about the women in the campaign which speaks to their personality and strength,” Burton said in a statement. “I wanted it to be purely about that—everything I design at Givenchy centers on seeing and celebrating the reality and the brilliance of all kinds of women.”

Roger Vivier

Jaya Harper is following in her mom’s footsteps. The 21-year-old daughter of Laura Dern is the face of Roger Vivier’s new campaign, supporting the brand for which her mom has also been an ambassador.

Roger Vivier

This isn’t the first time Harper has been in a Roger Vivier campaign, but in the past, Dern was by her side. When it comes to the autumn/winter 2026/2027 collection, however, Harper has been paired with actress Zoé Adjani and Léonie Cassel, daughter of Monica Bellucci and Vincent Cassel.

Roger Vivier

The images are captured inside Maison Vivier in Paris. The three women laze on the stone steps and chat on a luxe carpet. They wear the Talon Chic, the iconic heel introduced in 1959 and reinterpreted for the new season by Roger Vivier’s creative director, Gherardo Felloni.

Burberry

FKA Twigs was the voice of Burberry’s winter 2026 runway show soundtrack. Now, she’s the face of the collection’s campaign. The singer stars alongside Romeo Beckham in images set throughout London.

Burberry

“FKA twigs and Romeo Beckham represent the energy that makes London unique,” says Daniel Lee, Burberry’s chief creative officer. “It’s a place where anything feels possible, and it felt right to return to our home city this season.”

GapStudio

For fall 2026, GapStudio and Zac Posen are looking to the pieces that have long defined both the brand and classic American style. The new, 20-piece wardrobe collection, designed by Posen, reconsiders familiar forms through sculptural silhouettes and shifts in scale, bringing new perspective to enduring wardrobe archetypes.

GapStudio

Of course, denim acts as the foundation of the collection. Khaki, utilitywear, shirting, T-shirts, and workwear round out the offerings. They are shown off in the campaign, which stars Esther McGregor and Alton Mason. Depicted in a stripped-back setting, the imagery pulls the focus to the clothing, both its details and attitude.

Tom Ford

The Tom Ford autumn/winter 2026 campaign presents a study in characters. Individuals of every age and walk of life are depicted in glaring light against a clinical, white background. There is no hiding.

Tom Ford

“I wanted the images to be pure and direct, stark but trembling with human substance, therefore it’s just the camera and the subject, no theatrics or props needed,” creative director Haider Ackermann said. “What these personas wear is who they are. There is a sense of presence and awareness in such characters, caught either alone or in groups, highlighting the respective individualities. What they have in common is the fact that they all flirted with debauchery, but now they stand straight. They are here, unfiltered and defiant. Come closer, and see.”

Celine

Celine winter 2026 is for the routine. It’s for the woman on the go, who sometimes needs a moment to herself. This is made clear in the collection’s campaign, which shows both sides of a day: when you spend the morning running through the city streets and the afternoon trying to recover from all the action.

Celine

A black turtleneck and a pair of jeans are accessorized with a simple belt, while an all-black ensemble is topped with a geometric hat. These are clothes for real women to wear, and to do so every day.

Gucci

Allow Kate Moss to serenade you in the new Gucci Primavera campaign. Well, technically, she’s giving her best lip-sync. But that doesn’t make the Johan Renck-directed video any less alluring. Moss shimmies in a sparkling black dress with a high neck and open back as she mouths the words to Chris Isaak’s “Wicked Game.” Around her, Gucci-clad strangers awaken, pair off, and fall in love on the dance floor as Moss stands in the center, leading it all from the mic.

Gucci

In addition to the video, there’s a campaign photographed by Michal Chelbin. featuring Tom Brady, Alex Consani, Shawn Mendes, and Rico Nasty posing for portraits in the spirit of modern Renaissance imagery.

Gucci

The models represent the cross-section of individuals who personify creative director Demna’s vision for Gucci. They don clothes from the designer’s debut show for the house, displaying a new vocabulary of silhouettes and textures that embody the contemporary expression of Gucci’s identity.

Giorgio Armani

Giorgio Armani is using its fall/winter 2026/2027 campaign to declare its identity and reaffirm the strength and relevance of the Armani codes. It’s an appropriate time to do so, since the images feature the first collection designed under Silvana Armani and Leo Dell’Orco, ushering in a new era for the brand.

Giorgio Armani

The campaign, shot by Oliver Hadlee Pearch, is set against a neutral background, evoking a timelessness seen within the clothing. Christy Turlington’s presence has the same effect. She walked Armani shows in the ’90s, and here she is, decades later, still embodying the essence of the brand.

Giorgio Armani

Turlington’s effortlessness and authenticity are felt within the photographs as she stares down the camera with a look of confidence, grace, and sincerity. Dressed in Armani, she conveys the power of a distinct and recognizable identity.

7 For All Mankind

7 For All Mankind’s fall/winter 2026 campaign captures Chloë Sevigny in motion. The actor is photographed by Marili Andre as she shifts from faux interiors to artificial city streets. Everything is blurry—her hair as she tosses it around, the lights that surround her—representing fleeting moments that make one feel spontaneous and alive.

7 For All Mankind

Titled “In the City, Off Duty,” the campaign celebrates an instinctive approach to dressing. It’s all about feeling like yourself in your clothing—confidence without too much effort.

Loewe

Loewe is reaching new heights, literally. The brand’s fall/winter 2026 campaign was shot on top of the highest mountain in the Alps, Mont Blanc. There, Julia Garner—alongside Lil Yachty and artist Cosima von Bonin—braved the unpredictable elements to show off Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez’s latest designs.

Loewe

The collection’s bold colors are especially striking against the stark white surroundings. Bright yellow knits and shocking orange pants feel even more graphic amid the windswept expanse.

Loewe

Athletic poses emphasize the sportswear codes in the collection. Garner lunges across the frame while Lil Yachty adopts a strong stance with his Storm boots firmly planted in the snow.

Alaïa

Teyana Taylor was an obvious choice for the Alaïa summer/fall 2026 campaign. Her background in dance and movement lends itself perfectly to the brand’s designs. Second-skin, knit dresses stretch and expand as Taylor moves across David Sims’s frame in pared back, powerful images.

Alaïa

“As someone who’s loved Alaïa for a long time, being part of this campaign felt really special,” Taylor said. “The collection pulled me in right away. It’s bold, it’s feminine, but there’s a strength to it that I connect with. I’ve always loved fashion that lets a woman own who she is without having to say too much.”

Saint Laurent

Saint Laurent is easing the yearning for Heated Rivalry season two: Connor Storrie has temporarily given up his hockey pads for suits fas the star of Saint Laurent’s fall/winter 2026 campaign. Photographer Talia Chetrit captured Storrie in a sleek modern home that’s decidedly not the cottage.

Saint Laurent

Saint Laurent

Rosé stars alongside Storrie in the campaign, with Liu Wen rounding out the trio. The three flaunt their looks in the minimalist environment that spotlights the rich colors and fabrics of Anthony Vaccarello’s latest designs.

Proenza Schouler

Designer Rachel Scott’s first Proenza Schouler campaign is marked by a consideration of color, precision, and craft. It’s a presentation of the new Proenza woman, one shaped by thought, intuition, and contradiction.

Proenza Schouler

While, at first glance, Scott’s woman is put-together and precise, the campaign rejects the idea that perfection equals constraint. There remains a mysterious and capricious nature, illustrated in the lightly rumpled dresses and slightly irregular draping. These choices suggest a woman in motion, with a purpose.

Gap

Gap tapped two rising talents to star in its fall 2026 campaign. Malcolm Todd represents the world of music, while Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette provided the Hollywood perspective in another fun-filled ad for the brand.

Gap

In the campaign, titled “Denim on Your Own,” Todd and Navarrette dance around set to Todd’s cover of Robyn’s song “Dancing on My Own.” They roll around the floor and mimic each other’s moves in an ever-changing array of Gap denim.

Gap

“I’ve always been drawn to making things my own—whether that’s through music, style, or the way I express myself,” Todd said in a press release. “Being able to reinterpret an iconic song like ‘Dancing on My Own’ and bring my own perspective to it was such a special experience.” For her part, Navarrette added, “From the moment we started filming the Gap campaign, it felt like we were able to bring our own energy and personalities to the campaign. There was so much freedom to move, experiment and express ourselves.”

Guess

Irish television personality and model Maura Higgins is trading in Traitors for roadsters, posing alongside a vintage car for Guess’s latest campaign. The sleek ride is the perfect accompaniment for the Guess Allegra bag, which emphasizes form, feel, and function with sculpted lines and a striking presence.

Guess

Higgins, who rose to fame on Love Island UK, shows off two of the accessory’s colorways in the pared-back shoot. The bag’s “form” comes through in its dramatic winged silhouette and precise pleating; its “feel” in the soft faux suede; and its “function” in a versatile design that Higgins demonstrates can be worn with ease.

Ferragamo

Shoes are the true stars of Ferragamo’s fall 2026 campaign. A set of surreal yet still glamorous images portrays Ferragamo’s historic language and showcases footwear as a timeless object of dreamlike desire.

Ferragamo

Anok Yai sits on a throne of heels, a 1994 Willie Cole sculpture that plays perfectly into the campaign’s theme. “Willie takes everyday objects—objects that you feel connected to, that you can relate to—and distorts them,” says Ferragamo creative director Maximilian Davis. “The chair feels very surreal, but immediate—and, with my recent collections referencing Surrealism and Dadaism, the collaboration felt right.”

Ferragamo

Elsewhere, Vittoria Ceretti is surrounded by the accessory. It is a modern image that pays homage to Ferragamo’s past, specifically the 1950s, when Salvatore Ferragamo was an innovator in the space.

Ferragamo

“So many things make a Ferragamo shoe an object of desire: the construction; the wearability; the innovation of the design,” says Davis. “And since I’ve been at the house, it’s been about refining the details to make them feel more sharp, more graphic; to take those core codes of craft and construction and translate them for today.”

Versace

The Dario Vitale era of Versace has officially ended. Versace Obsessed, Chapter II is the final campaign to feature Vitale’s designs. Photographed by Steven Meisel, the images are laid out in a series of cinematic vignettes, capturing the strength of Versace’s legacy and its ability to bridge the past, present, and future.

Versace

Models dressed in the fall/winter 2026 collection are shot from above. Around them lay artifacts from Versace’s past, specifically archival images from the ’90s and ’00s, also shot by Meisel.

McQueen

Tension is building within the McQueen fall 2026 campaign. There’s a psychological conflict between interiority and exteriority here, alluding to the meticulously crafted facade we all work so hard to maintain—and the visceral, emotional reality that lies beneath.

McQueen

Photographer Glen Luchford captures this dichotomy in the images. He depicts the slow slip of the fourth wall and the deep impulses that emerge through the confronting gaze of Karen Elson, Paloma Elsesser, Jacqui Hooper, and Ju Xiao Wen.

McQueen

The clothes, meanwhile, bear their own kind of material tension: when precision tailoring meets the fluidity of silk georgette. The ads are an exploration of depth, darkness, and beauty, constructed by creative director Seán McGirr and cast in a noir light.

Jimmy Choo

The Jimmy Choo autumn 2026 campaign is all about the joy of dressing up. Model Africa Garcia is captured inside Palazzo Gallarati Scotti as she explores the brand’s latest offerings. Each shoe and bag unleashes a new side of Garcia, from a businesswoman in full control to a more demure ingenue.

Jimmy Choo

From painstaking embellishment to pure form, the expansion of the collection is on full display. Femininity is at the core of every design, but how it manifests varies by shoe.

Miu Miu

Femininity is flipped on its head in Miu Miu’s fall 2026 campaign. Clothing is armor as much as it is adornment. Distressed leather and wool cling to the body while babydoll dresses provide a soft contrast, especially when paired with studded leather bags.

Miu Miu

Hailey Bieber and Xiao Wen Ju are captured by Zoë Ghertner in what looks to be an abandoned parking lot at night. Street lights shine behind the models, reflecting off nylon pants and coats. There is a sense that these women should not be here, but they claim ownership of the space in their assurance of expression and dress.

Chloé

Chloé’s winter 2026 campaign presents a whimsical, otherworldly landscape where color remains beautifully saturated and hair perfectly crimped. Inez Van Lamsweerde and Vinoodh Matadin shot the images, which present creative director Chemena Kamali’s latest collection in a folkloric setting, among cliffs blooming with flowers.

Chloé

“For this campaign, I wanted to express devotion through women, the vastness of open landscapes, and craftsmanship,” Kamali said. “Nature brings us back to instinct, freedom, and connection. In that openness, femininity unfolds with untamed strength and togetherness.“

Prada

Routine life is what’s on display in Prada’s fall 2026 campaign. A film by director Barry Jenkins embraces the little moments throughout a single day—those instants when you can stop and admire the way the sun shines through the window or take a second with yourself in the mirror. It’s all about the extraordinary within the ordinary.

Prada

Actors Hunter Schafer, Troye Sivan, Chen Haoyu, and Kelvin Harrison Jr. star in Jenkins’s short film and the accompanying images. They perform along with the clothing, which is a character in itself. Bags are an extension of the body, and coats an expression of mood. Even the most mundane acts can be made significant when handled with purpose and care. Watch the full video below.

Prada

Loro Piana

Houston (or more specifically, John and Dominique de Menil, who helped shape the cultural landscape of the Texas city) was the inspiration for Loro Piana’s fall 2026 campaign. “Working on this campaign for Loro Piana within the extraordinary de Menil landscape was truly inspiring,” says photographer Mario Sorrenti. “The synergy between the collection’s refined elegance and the timeless, art-filled environments created by John and Dominique de Menil was profound. It allowed us to capture a natural, unforced beauty, a quiet dialogue between the clothing and these spaces, that felt both intimate and expansive.”

Loro Piana

The story begins at the de Menils’s former residence, where interiors by couturier Charles James provide a rich backdrop for Loro Piana’s new range of garments. From there, a trip to the Menil Collection, designed in 1987 by Renzo Piano. The campaign explores the various galleries of the building, where art, architecture, and community intersect.

Loro Piana

And finally, a stop at the Rothko Chapel, which houses fourteen canvases by Mark Rothko, creating an immersive expanse within which to indulge. Here, the collection does not compete with the art for attention, but moves in dialogue with it, complementing each other in both color and form.

Burberry

Apple Martin is not the only model in her family. Her younger brother and fellow offspring of Gwyneth Paltrow and Chris Martin, Moses Martin, has officially entered the world of fashion with a starring role in Burberry’s latest campaign.

Burberry

The 20-year-old is part of creative director Daniel Lee’s “Escape to the Countryside” campaign, which sees friends embarking on a summer road trip. “A road trip is a very British thing to do,” Lee says. “Getting into your car, heading out to the countryside, and seeing where the day takes you. That idea of exploration has always been part of Burberry. Listening to music on a long drive becomes part of the memories you make along the way.”

Burberry

The images, shot by Chris Rhodes, follow the group on a beautiful summer day as they swap the city for the winding roads and rolling hills of the countryside. They make stops along the journey, taking in the sights in their autumn 2026 duds, and end their trip at a classic English manor, Deene Park in Northamptonshire.

Tiffany & Co.

Tiffany & Co.’s latest campaign is all about love in its many forms. Not only romantic love, but also those deep personal relationships between family, chosen communities, and with oneself. At the center of this love is Tiffany’s new Sixteen Stone solitaire diamond ring.

Tiffany & Co.

In the short film “Love & Celebration,” Academy Award-winning actor Mikey Madison turns the age-old refrain, “he loves me, he loves me not,” into a ritual of quiet affirmation. With the ring—inspired by Jean Schlumberger’s 1959 design—on her finger, she concludes, “I love me.”

Fendi

In season three, episode 17 of Sex and the City, Carrie Bradshaw takes a wrong turn during a shopping trip in SoHo and finds herself at the whim of a mugger. While pointing a gun at her, he demands she hand over her bag. “It’s a Baguette,” she corrects as she reluctantly gives him her purple paillette-covered purse. It was a scene that would start a movement and launch the Fendi Baguette into It bag status. Over a quarter of a century, the Baguette is still as popular as ever, and Sarah Jessica Parker is still a fan.

Fendi

It’s not surprising, then, that Maria Grazia Chiuri featured Baguettes in her inaugural collection for Fendi and tapped Parker to lead the accessory’s latest campaign, “It’s Not a Bag, it’s a Baguette.”

Fendi

Parker is joined by Sophie Thatcher, Jessica Alba, Emma D’Arcy, Iris Law and more stars in the images, shot by Bibi Borthwick. Each photo showcases a different iteration of the Baguette, demonstrating the purse’s immense variety. A corresponding video set to Addison Rae’s “Fame Is a Gun” drives this point home as each campaign star declares their connection to the Baguette, stating, “It’s history,” “It’s controlled chaos,” and “It’s my attitude.”

Coach

Coach is introducing its latest project, &Coach, a content series co-created with Gen Z communities, creators, and cultural voices. In its first iteration, &Coach introduces a new model for luxury storytelling. The American brand tapped Charli XCX, Malala Yousafzai, PinkPantheress, and more unique voices to share their perspective through social-first content.

Coach

Of course, across every story, there’s a Coach bag—a companion to amplify your confidence. The bag joins Pink on stage, or completes Charli’s outfit as she’s getting ready. It’s a conduit for community as much as an accessory.

Loewe

Loewe is celebrating its 180th anniversary with a campaign honoring almost two centuries of leather craftsmanship—and a playful spirit. Brand ambassador Julia Garner stars alongside Sissy Spacek and artist Kara Walker in the Talia Chetrit-shot images, showcasing an array of iconic Loewe handbags from across the decades.

Loewe

From the Flamenco clutch (launched in the ’80s) to the Puzzle bag of 2015, the campaign highlights the enduring impact of these accessories. Also on display is the Amazona 180, which was introduced in 1975 and recently reimagined by creative directors Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez for their debut collection at the house. The selection proves Loewe’s affinity for the past, as well as its ability to adapt to the present and lead the future.

Balenciaga

Celine Song lent her directorial talent to Balenciaga for A New York Minute, the brand’s theatrical fall 2026 campaign, starring Love Story actor Sarah Pidgeon.

Balenciaga

The campaign, which takes the form of three one-minute films, finds Pidgeon during a day in Manhattan as the actor engages in mundane tasks. She retrieves her dry cleaning, crosses a busy street, and takes a cab home. These are simple actions every New Yorker makes daily, but zoom out, and you will find it’s all movie magic.

Balenciaga

Song’s videos act as an exploration of movie-making and city life. Of course, they’re also a meditation on Pierpaolo Piccioli’s latest offerings for the brand. Each scene finds Pidgeon in a different Balenciaga look, always with one of the brand’s classic bags in hand. It proves that Piccioli’s Balenciaga can be utilized in everyday life, but there is an added sense of drama to this wardrobe, even if you might not notice it at first.

Celine

Celine invites you to a day at the beach in celebration of its fall 2026 campaign. The sun hides behind clouds, but the warmth comes from those around you. A group lounges on the sand and rocks and blocks each other from the whipping wind. They layer up in tailored coats with oversize shoulders and collegiate sweatshirts, protecting their belongings in patterned totes.

Celine

Accessories are key. Beaded necklaces layer atop a short-sleeve knit and sunglasses cover almost every set of eyes. Color comes in the form of nautical stripes and green accents on a silk scarf. Red flannel provides a sense of nonchalance, as does the wind-blown hair and the up-close nature of Zoë Ghertner’s imagery.

Burberry

Burberry is getting in the football spirit ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup this summer. The brand has released its autumn 2026 campaign, “A Good Sport,” celebrating the energy of the sport’s fandom.

Burberry

Jason Sudeikis, who has become especially familiar with footy thanks to his work on Ted Lasso, stars in the campaign alongside actors Jodie Turner-Smith, Lucy Punch, and Stephen Graham. Also featured are Romeo Beckham, models Rosie Huntington-Whiteley and Neelam Gill, as well as football stars Eberechi Eze, Leah Williamson, Naomi Girma, and Son Heung-min. 

Burberry

“Burberry has connected football fans across generations for decades,” says the brand’s chief creative officer, Daniel Lee. “It’s only right that we celebrate that this summer....There’s a certain attitude to being a good sport that is very British and very Burberry.”

item.title: Joseph Zada on 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' & What's Next
item.description: The 'Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' star discusses playing young Haymitch, studying Woody Harrelson, and channeling James Dean.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Twersky Winkler, and ,Austin Sandhaus
item.content:encoded:
Joseph Zada would describe himself as a bit of a rebel. “More so than other people,” he clarifies. When asked for examples of his defiance, however, he gets coy, or more accurately, a little cheeky: “If I told you, I’d probably be in trouble.”

As he says this, his lips lift into a smirk, and his eyebrows rise slightly, giving his sharp blue eyes more room to draw you in. All he’s missing is a bomber jacket and a cigarette dangling from his mouth to become a modern James Dean. It’s an apt comparison, considering he just stepped into a role once played by the late heartthrob in Netflix’s new East of Eden adaptation.

Zada is making a habit of taking on roles originated by greats. This month, he stars as Haymitch Abernathy in the Hunger Games prequel Sunrise on the Reaping, playing the younger version of Woody Harrelson’s character.

When talking to Zada, it’s easy to see why director Francis Lawrence chose him to lead the prequel, based on Suzanne Collins’s fifth book in the popular series. Zada is suave, but in a way that feels natural, not manipulative or artificial. His golden curls fall haphazardly across his forehead as he gets wrapped up in a point he’s trying to make with that mesmerizing Australian lilt, but he always concludes his thought with a smile and a direct look into your eyes.

That charm is just as perceptible in Zada’s portrayal of a 16-year-old Haymitch. Fans first met the character through Harrelson, who played him in the original four films as a browbeaten, cynical middle-aged man more interested in getting drunk on the Capitol’s dime than supporting Jennifer Lawrence’s Katniss or Josh Hutcherson’s Peeta. But the Haymitch of Sunrise is worlds away from Harrelson’s depressed and snarky alcoholic. Zada’s Haymitch is in love (and sober), and throughout the film we see him gradually unravel from a youthful mama’s boy making do in the neglected District 12 to the jaded, lonely mentor of those original films.

Sunrise takes place 24 years before we meet Katniss Everdeen, during the 50th Hunger Games, or the second Quarter Quell, when the Capitol chooses twice the usual number of tributes. When Haymitch gets plucked as one of District 12’s unfortunates, he must leave behind his family and girlfriend, Lenore Dove (Whitney Peak), to face certain death alongside 47 other innocent kids.

Zada himself is just a kid in many ways. The 21-year-old Sydney native is endearingly earnest, which is striking given his recent successes. Aussies will know the actor from the drama series Invisible Boys, in which he played an aspiring musician who is outed as gay. YA fans caught him in season one of Prime’s We Were Liars (he just finished filming season two). But Zada really broke into the mainstream this fall, when he starred in the final two episodes of Zoe Kazan’s East of Eden. Sunrise hits theaters on November 20, and the franchise has a history of turning young actors into stars, including Lawrence, Rachel Zegler, and Tom Blyth. If all goes to plan, it will do the same for Zada, whose career has been in the works since he was a young boy.

“From the time I was five years old, my mom was like, ‘He’s going to be an actor,’” Zada recalls. His mother, film producer Jessica Brentnall, took the prediction seriously. “I wasn’t allowed to play rugby,” he says. “You can’t have a broken nose as a movie star.”

She knew that fact all too well. Zada’s father, Jeremy Cumpston, is a director and actor, and his older brother started performing at a young age. Today, several of the five Cumpston siblings have IMDb pages. (Zada, who was born Joseph Cumpston, adopted his grandmother’s surname professionally when he was 18. The name traces back to his great-grandfather, an Afghan cameleer, and Zada has said he felt a “spiritual connection” to the family history it carries.)

When he was 15, Zada decided to pursue acting himself. “It’s the most random story ever,” he says of meeting his first agent, Mags Stewart. He agreed to star in his then-girlfriend’s short film for a school project. When she presented it over Zoom, Stewart walked by her daughter’s laptop and caught a glimpse of Zada’s performance. In that moment, she decided, “I want to be that kid’s agent.”

Zada’s career has been filled with these sorts of kismet moments. He says his audition for We Were Liars was the last one the casting team watched. From there, his costar, Mamie Gummer, helped push his tape through to Kazan for East of Eden. He auditioned for Sunrise just days after wrapping the Steinbeck adaptation. “The role came at the perfect point,” Zada says of Haymitch. “I never would have been as ready as right after East of Eden when I worked with Florence [Pugh].”

Sunrise is Zada’s first movie, and it proved to be a baptism by fire. He joined a beloved series whose director and crew had worked together for more than a decade, with a legacy to uphold and a set to lead. “There was a lot of pressure,” Zada admits. In many ways, though, that pressure put him right in his character’s headspace.

“Haymitch is someone who gets thrust into a position where people look towards him, though he doesn’t know what to do,” Zada says. “He has to stand up and take charge.”

Once the initial jitters wore off, Zada naturally took a leadership role on set. “I have three younger siblings, so I’m very good at hanging out with younger kids, taking care of them, and being a leader,” he says. “That was the core of the character, uplifting younger actors and these younger characters.”

With just a handful of projects under his belt, Zada is still figuring out his process. Right now, he’s dabbling in being over-prepared. Before Sunrise, he filled up five journals with prep work. “I was a madman,” he says. He also tried method acting, which helped when working with industry veterans like Ralph Fiennes, Glenn Close, and Jesse Plemons. “In order to not get too freaked out, I spent most of my time in the character,” he says. “I didn’t want to be fangirling in the middle of a scene.”

His main model, of course, was Harrelson. Zada didn’t meet his predecessor until after filming wrapped, but he studied Harrelson’s many roles. “He gave me a performance to mirror,” Zada says. “I mean, my job for a while was to watch Woody Harrelson movies. That’s not a real job.”

Zada also looked to Mickey Rourke’s work, specifically in the 1987 neo-noir Angel Heart, for young Haymitch’s flirtatious streak. His heart belongs to Lenore Dove, but that streak comes out with Elle Fanning’s Effie Trinket. “There was a little bit of flirtatious energy with Elle,” Zada admits. “It makes their scene together come alive and adds a nice dynamic.”

His relationship with fellow District 12 tribute Maysilee (Mckenna Grace) runs deeper. What begins as an icy acquaintance melts into an attachment born from hardship. “It’s a lot like soldiers who return from war,” Zada says. “There’s a bond between Haymitch and Maysilee because of the traumatic events they’ve gone through.”

Off-screen, the two have become fast friends. They’re currently on a worldwide press tour together, Zada’s first. “Mckenna is one of my favorite people in the entire world,” Zada says of his costar. “I leaned on her so much during the shoot. She’s such a pro.” Grace has shared similarly flattering statements about Zada. She told Variety Australia that Zada is “about to become one of the biggest stars ever.” Harrelson echoed the opinion to Vanity Fair, saying, “he’s about to be a big star.”

“It’s nice to hear, but I don’t have a job right now,” Zada says, humbly countering with another Harrelson quote: “It’s all well and good until you start believing it.”

Still, Zada is optimistic others will share Grace and Harrelson’s view when Sunrise hits theaters. “My hope is that filmmakers and studios feel the same way,” he says, laughing. He also knows that stepping into a beloved franchise means plenty of opinions will follow. For now, Zada has vowed to stay off the Internet, especially after the release, in order to maintain some distance from the online discourse. “I’ve become too aware of what everyone is saying,” he says. “I just need to stay away and keep to myself.” Instead, he’ll occupy his time with the script he’s writing with his brother, a drama comedy about half-siblings.

“I only want to do what I want to do,” Zada says of future projects, finally revealing a bit of that rebellious spirit. “I’m not willing to be pushed into anything that I’m not wholeheartedly in love with, whether that means making money or not. I just want to explore and go way off the deep end.”

Zada wears Calvin Klein throughout; styled by Jason Bolden.

item.title: The Sorel x Aspen Collection Blends Alpine Performance With Après-Ski Style
item.description: Sorel returns for part two of its collaboration with Aspen Collection, the mountain’s performance and lifestyle apparel label.
item.dc:creator: Erin Cunningham
item.content:encoded:
In Aspen, the right footwear is a statement of intent. There are boots for the snow, boots for the slopes, and boots for the après. And each pair is both a style choice and a signal of how well you know the terrain.

Sorel, the cold-weather outfitter born in a 1962 snowstorm, has long been the go-to brand for locals and visitors alike. This season, the company returns for part two of its collaboration with Aspen Collection, the mountain’s performance and lifestyle apparel label, with an expanded range of shoes built to meet the elements.

The collection introduces four new styles: the fleece-lined Ona Ave Alpine Tall Lux with a shearling tongue (in an exclusive creamy colorway), the elevated Joan FRWD Cozy Lux, which combines leather and suede with custom D-ring hardware, and the relaxed Caribou Horizon GTX Lux — a mountain classic, but with a full-grain leather upgrade (and waterproof GORE-TEX protection). For something more rugged, the Daystorm Nomad HI GTX adds a stylish furry upper and bold colors to Vibram™ traction — complete with Aspen iconography.

It’s a fitting pair: Sorel has six decades of cold-weather credibility; Aspen has the reputation, the history, and the mountain itself. Together, they’ve created a lineup of boots for people who care about comfort, looks, and above all, tradition.

The collection is available at Aspen Collection’s flagship stores in Aspen Village and Snowmass, as well as at select retailers, Sorel.com, and AspenCollection.com.

item.title: Dior Enlists Rihanna and Robert Pattinson for a Hand-Drawn Holiday Fantasy
item.description: Plus more of the best campaigns of the holiday season.
item.dc:creator: W Staff
item.content:encoded:
It is never too early to get into the holiday spirit. Everyone knows the Christmas season can be stressful, but the more you prepare ahead of time, the more you can enjoy all the magic. So while it may seem too early to start considering your gifts, in reality, you’ll just be saving your future self a lot of stress. And luckily, the brands are, once again, ahead of schedule, already rolling out their holiday content for our benefit. Ferragamo, Dior, Chanel, and more have released their 2026 holiday campaigns, and the images are getting us in the yuletide mood. So while the leaves may just now be falling off the trees, soon they’ll be on the ground, covered in snow—and there’s no time like the present to dive into the 2026 holiday campaigns.

Dior

“It was a quiet night at the atelier at 30 Avenue Montaigne,” begins the animated short film, Christian Dior’s Night in Color. The seven-minute movie, directed by award-winning French filmmaker Sylvain Chomet and narrated by Robert Pattinson, tells a fictional story that weaves together key moments from the fashion house’s history.

Dior

Jonathan Anderson was inspired by the cinema’s transition from black-and-white to Technicolor for the Dior cruise 2027 collection. Christian Dior’s Night in Color once again explores that shift. The narrative follows Christian Dior as he rushes to make a dress for Marlene Dietrich and her Technicolor film.

Dior

The cast is filled with familiar voices: Louis Garrel as Dior, Josh O’Connor as a talking chair, LaKeith Stanfield as a director. Greta Lee pops up as a busy atelier bee, and Rihanna even makes an appearance as the star atop a Christmas tree. “Shine bright...like a Christmas tree,” she exclaims.

Dior

In the end, Dior is able to create a dress—the famed Junon style—and deliver it to Dietrich just in time. It’s a heartwarming story, filled with nostalgia, whimsy, and craft—all hallmarks of both Dior and the holiday season.

Celine

The Celine Les Fêtes campaign is all about the details. Shot by Christian Colomer, the camera is tight on the model, sometimes capturing a face, but more often stockinged legs that end in bold heels and ring-adorned fingers.

Celine

As the viewer, one can’t help but feel like they’re intruding. There is a party underway, and you just stumbled in, suddenly faced with the attendees’ bold knitwear and wrists stacked with bracelets.

Celine

A look from the Celine Les Fêtes campaign.

JW Anderson

Everyone is invited to Christmas at Strawberry Hill House, even the pigeons and squirrels. Creatures and human guests alike make themselves at home at the Gothic Revival villa in Twickenham, London, the setting of JW Anderson’s 2026 holiday campaign.

JW Anderson

The campaign is an intimate, domestic portrait of holiday bliss. Wreaths adorn the entrances and stockings are hung upon the fireplace. But the house isn’t alone in its decorations. The inhabitants get into the Christmas spirit as well, bedecked in knits from the JW Anderson x Pringle of Scotland collaboration and the brand’s wider ready-to-wear selection.

Louis Vuitton

Louis Vuitton’s 2026 holiday campaign is an ode to those who travel for their winter festivities. The Oliver Hadlee Pearch images take place in a train station, the setting of magical reunions and exciting departures.

Louis Vuitton

The campaign captures the last five minutes before a grand departure. Stories unfold on the platform and within the train cars. Friends reunite, children play, travelers rush around carrying their Louis Vuitton luggage. It’s a suspended moment that perfectly embodies Louis Vuitton’s Art of Travel.

Burberry

Burberry is opening the doors to a gorgeous English country home for its 2026 holiday campaign, inviting Pierce Brosnan, Dwyane Wade, Gabrielle Union, and more friends of the brand to gather for an afternoon of winter fun.

Burberry

“We wanted to celebrate 170 years of Burberry with a proper party,” said Daniel Lee, Burberry chief creative officer. “Family, friends, great gifts, and everyone dressed up.”

Burberry

Set at Longleat House in Wiltshire—a historic, stately home built in the 16th century—the images capture a festive celebration of party games, gift exchanges, and, of course, a whole lot of Burberry check.

Gucci

It’s time! The holiday season is officially upon us, which means Queen of Christmas Mariah Carey has taken the spotlight—and her rightful place on her holiday throne. Of course, preparations must be made, and the Gucci team is on it, making sure everything is ready for Carey to ring in all the merriment.

Gucci

The iconic singer stars in Gucci’s holiday campaign video, directed by Harmony Korine and set to Carey’s hit song, “All I Want for Christmas Is You.” Accompanying images star friends of the house as they wait in anticipation of Carey’s arrival.

Gucci

When Carey arrives at the party, she does so in Gucci’s new Butterfly special collection. Inspired by the insect, the collection embodies the iridescence of the butterfly, while paying homage to Carey’s signature motif and her 1997 album, Butterfly.

Chloé

Chloé’s latest campaign is festive, but not in an obvious way. Shot by David Sims and starring friend of the house, Claudia Schiffer, the images capture a nocturnal spirit through a cinematic, after-dark atmosphere.

Chloé

Schiffer’s enduring personal allure is reflected in the imagery, as her natural presence and distinctive character bring a singular perspective to the campaign.

Marc Jacobs

Fashion, humor, personality, and New York energy collide in Marc Jacobs’s winter 2026 campaign, Let It Joy. Actor Meg Stalter stars in the campaign video, holed up in her hotel room during a snowstorm. When Mel Ottenberg invites Stalter over for a party, there’s only one issue: She doesn’t know his room number.

Marc Jacobs

Chaos ensues as Stalter attempts to locate the party. Luckily, the comedienne does not give up and is able to follow the music. She eventually makes it to the holiday bash, ready to celebrate in her black Marc Jacobs shift dress alongside New York personalities and cultural figures like Knicks center Andre Drummond and model and actress Kai Schreiber.

Tory Burch

Tory Burch presents a guide to the holidays, along with tips to celebrate the upcoming season the Tory way: with optimism, joy, and presents piled high.

Tory Burch

Tory Burch’s holiday campaign comes with a list of rules to follow. Number two pertains to gifting (and receiving), suggesting we give generously and react dramatically. Number four urges us to embrace the festive spirit, while the last rule is a bit of a warning: Pace yourself; it’s a long holiday season ahead.

Tory Burch

Alongside the tips, you’ll find more holiday inspiration in the form of images from Anthony Seklaoui. The shots are full of beaded sparkle, cozy knits, and community—the perfect recipe for a joyous season.

David Yurman

Michael B. Jordan, Yerin Ha, and Inde Navarrette star in the David Yurman 2026 holiday campaign. The three actors gather in snow-covered Washington Square Park for shots that capture the joy of togetherness and the magic of the holiday season in New York City.

David Yurman

Jordan and Ha face off in a spirited card game, while Navarrette searches for the perfect holiday gift. Of course, all three are bedecked in David Yurman designs, including 18-karat gold cable bracelets and pieces from the brand’s Starburst and Armory collections.

Tiffany & Co.

Fresh off her buzzy turn in You Can See Everything, Amanda Seyfried has returned to New York from Texas, just in time for the holiday season. The actor is Tiffany & Co.’s newest House ambassador and the star of its holiday campaign, “Love Is a Gift.”

Tiffany & Co.

As part of the campaign, Seyfried acts in a short film, “You & Me,” which tells the story of two different Christmas celebrations: one taking place in the present day, and one in 1992. Between these two moments passes a Bird on a Rock ornament, originally gifted decades ago and still a prized possession all these years later. It’s a story of tradition, holiday memories, and the connection between generations.

Tiffany & Co.

“I’m thrilled to join the Tiffany & Co. family as their newest House ambassador and to be part of a campaign that celebrates love, family, and the traditions we carry with us through generations,” Seyfried said in a statement. “‘You & Me’ captures beautifully how a meaningful gift can hold memories and become part of a family’s story. It was incredibly special to bring that idea to life with Tiffany this holiday season.”

Skims

The holidays are all about family, so it makes sense that Kim Kardashian enlisted her very famous sisters to star in the Skims Holiday campaign. Shot by frequent Kardashian collaborator Nadia Lee Cohen, the campaign takes inspiration from nostalgic holiday portraits, placing Kim, Kourtney, Kylie, Khloe, and Kendall in scenes you may recall from your own home videos.

Skims

The sisters are styled in pieces from the Skims holiday shop, wearing outfits with varying degrees of coziness. Khloe and Kourtney are covered head-to-toe in their respective patterned onesie and red long johns. Kylie and Kendall, meanwhile, show off more skin in bras boasting classic holiday prints. All the girls don retro glam—bouffants and old-school glasses. The result is a vintage scene with no clear time stamp. But it doesn’t matter, because Santa still clearly approves.

Miu Miu

Gigi Hadid, Louisa Jacobson, and more gather in a grand townhouse to celebrate the holidays. The polished wood walls are covered in wreaths, the tree is bedecked with ornaments, and everyone is dressed in Miu Miu.

Miu Miu

The wardrobe highlights contrasts between lifestyle archetypes and seasonal themes. Silk dresses are paired with upcycled knits and sportswear-inspired zip-front blousons. Cropped sweaters reveal button-down shirts, and utilitarian cotton canvas separates are layered over sequined bralettes.

Miu Miu

But the models are not alone in this uptown space. They are joined by plush toy bears, rabbits, geese, and more. Treated like treasured guests, these additions provide whimsy to the scene, a composed portrait of bourgeois behavior subverted by humor and play.

Prada

Friendly furry creatures are not unique to the Miu Miu campaign this season—they pop up in the Prada world as well. This time, though, the woodland pals are hand-drawn by a team of artists led by cinematic animator John Pomeroy.

Prada

Sadie Sink gets down on the ground with a trio of mice to admire a patterned, calf-hair loafer. Maya Hawke faces off against a sly fox as she braves the elements of a frozen setting. There is a whimsy to these wintertime scenes, which emphasizes Prada’s humanity and a connection to craft that lies at the heart of the brand’s approach to creation.

Ferragamo

Kris Jenner is the matriarch of the Ferragamo family in the brand’s 2026 holiday campaign, The Joy of Loving. “Ferragamo is all about family,” says creative director Maximilian Davis. “And when I design, I am always thinking about that, too: how a collection can be worn by different generations, but also how pieces you love will be held onto and passed down through them.”

Ferragamo

The momager stars as the director of a fictional film, leading screen tests featuring the campaign’s various faces. There’s Paloma Elsesser and her brother, Sage; girl group The Womack Sisters; and Sofia Testino with her dog, Syko. Actress Joan Chen is joined by her daughter, Audrey Hui, while acting coach Nancy Banks poses with her son, actor Benny Buckley.

Ferragamo

The campaign connects back to the roots of Ferragamo, and founder Salvatore Ferragamo’s original desire to build a better life for his family through his love of invention and creativity. “One of the founding values of Ferragamo has always been of beauty that develops from craftsmanship, humanity, and joy,” says Salvatore’s son, Leonardo Ferragamo. “This campaign is telling that story.”

Loro Piana

Loro Piana invites you to a weekend at the cabin, where the elegantly falling snow outside matches the chic inhabitants’ wardrobes. Models are dressed in the brand’s holiday collection, an expression of style that plays out across textures, hand-finished prints, exclusive patterns, and elaborate stitches.

Loro Piana

Loro Piana’s usually muted color palette is realized once again, this time in the form of dark greens and earthy browns. They are highlighted with pops of winter-white and marigold.

Loro Piana

Warm jersey tops and trousers form the foundations of these après-ski looks. On top, classic Loro Piana outerwear like the Spagna jacket and Konny vest are crafted in wool and finely detailed with needlework; the wearer stays warm while also making an enviable sartorial impression. 

Chanel

Chanel is hitting the slopes for its 2026 Coco Neige collection. Bright-red knits and colorblocked puffers stand out against snow-capped mountains. The images have a retro flair, but the clothing is distinctly modern.

Chanel

A snowball fight adds even more joy to this already playful campaign, while penguin and polar bear-shaped purses and earrings provide the perfect amount of whimsy.

Chanel

Shearling caps keep ears warm, while winter whites are embraced with aplomb. It’s a reminder that dressing for warmth does not mean sacrificing style or charm.

Dior

Indulge in your sweet tooth with Dior’s 2026 holiday campaign, which sees the brand’s famous 30 Montaigne store reimagined as a sugar-dusted gingerbread house. Anya Taylor-Joy and Deva Cassel star in a joyous musical video. The house’s ambassadors prance around the store, snacking on Dior cookies, spritzing the brand’s famed fragrances, and trimming the icing-lined cookie Christmas tree.

item.description: Plus more of the season's latest openings, designer collaborations, and launches.

Moon Boot x Moncler Grenoble

The Moon Boot just got a major makeover courtesy of Moncler. Both of the brands’ signature characteristics combine for the Icon Rodeo, which debuted at Moncler Grenoble’s fall/winter 2026 runway presentation in Aspen earlier this year. The collaboration draws on the cowboy boot and features embroidery inspired by Aspen’s ranch heritage, soft suede finishes, and trademark lacing. Still, the technical functionality of Moon Boot remains. The boot is available in two brown-tone colorways called caribou and chestnut. This latest design builds on the existing partnership between Moon Boot and Moncler, which already includes the nylon Low Gator and suede Icon Low Biker. The product is available now in the U.S. and will launch globally at moonboot.com and moncler.com on November 26.

Loewe x Tim Burton’s The Nightmare Before Christmas

Loewe has partnered with Tim Burton’s The Nightmare Before Christmas to reimagine the beloved film’s characters and its visual language across bags, accessories, ready-to-wear, fragrance, and leather goods. Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez felt a deep connection to the film, which was created through the use of stop-motion, handmade articulated puppets, and hand-crafted miniature sets. The painstaking process of turning sketches into three-dimensional forms resonated with the designers. Loewe was given special access to the film’s archive and, in turn, the brand reimagined Nightmare’s world in leather marquetry, embroidery, print, enamel, and other signature house materials and techniques. Jack Skellington’s head pops up when an Amazona bag is unzipped. A sketched forest scene plays out across a silk shirt. A mini Flamenco bag boasts the stitches and colors of Sally’s skin. The pieces are colorful and whimsical, but tinged with darkness, embodying the energy that draws people to Nightmare. As a result, the collection acts as a celebration of Tim Burton’s The Nightmare Before Christmas and of the hands that shape imaginative worlds.
