Jimmy Choo’s Choo Stories

Jimmy Choo has introduced a new storytelling series celebrating life’s moments of transformation, and it’s kicking off this new endeavor, called Choo Stories, with the help of pop star Olivia Dean. Jimmy Choo has long been present for life’s milestones, big and small. Choo Stories expands on this with the belief that the joy of wearing something extraordinary is always worth celebrating. Through narration and a personal lens, each Choo Stories will place a protagonist at the heart of the story, exploring themes of transformation, confidence, self-expression, craftsmanship, and mastery.

This inaugural Choo Stories follows Dean through her sold-out world tour, The Art of Loving Live, for which the singer wore custom and ready-to-wear Jimmy Choo stompers. The images take the viewer both backstage at a Dean concert and behind the scenes of Jimmy Choo’s London design studio. There, one can see the relationship between maker and muse. This peek behind the curtain provides a new perspective on both Dean and Jimmy Choo, and allows the viewer to step into the shoes of their friends of the house.

John Hardy x Billie Eilish & Finneas

John Hardy is expanding on its relationship with Academy and Grammy Award-winning siblings Billie Eilish and Finneas. The musical duo was announced as John Hardy creative partners last year, but now they’ve surpassed the traditional role of brand ambassador by designing a jewelry collection in collaboration with the house. The Billie Eilish and Finneas collection was created with an emphasis on sustainability. It was designed using more responsible materials, including reclaimed metals, and made in production facilities powered entirely by renewable energy. As far as design, the collection represents a study in the contrast and complement of Eilish and Finneas’s personal styles. It is built around two personas: the understated wildflower and the bold and industrial screwball. The flower motif is represented throughout, rendered in sterling silver, lab-grown diamonds, and pearls. The screwball-inspired pieces, meanwhile, introduce a minimalist edge with sculptural chain links and spherical hardware evocative of piercings. While distinctive, the two styles are meant to be worn together in order to emphasize the tension between the delicate wallflower and the utilitarian screwball. The Billie Eilish and Finneas collection is available now at John Hardy stores, select retail partners, and johnhardy.com.

Banana Republic x Zankov

Henry Zankov is busy. Not only did the designer just present his debut collection for Diane Von Furstenberg alongside the latest for his eponymous brand at New York Fashion Week, but he also designed a collaboration with Banana Republic. Comprised of 27 pieces, the limited-edition, unisex capsule reflects both brands’ approach to craft and detail, offering unexpected pieces made from high-quality materials.

This is Zankov we’re talking about, so of course knits are the cornerstone of the collection. Brushed cashmere and wool yarns create sweaters of vivid stripes and Fair Isle patterns. Zankov looked to the Banana Republic archives when designing the capsule, and one leather and suede-paneled pencil skirt finds its origins in a 1986 style of similar construction. Leather pops up elsewhere in a burgundy bomber jacket and on the collar of a car coat. Accessories round it out with a selection of reversible hats, colorful socks, and scarves. The pieces are simple but exciting, bright and joyous, and inherently grounded in the languages of both Banana Republic and Zankov. The collection ranges in price from $90 to $600 and will be available to the public at select Banana Republic stores and online at bananarepublic.com starting October 20.

Patek Philippe Gondolo Ladies First

Patek Philippe has launched six new Gondolo Ladies First watches. Rendered in bright hues with sophisticated gem settings, the styles recall the original 2009 design while updating it for today. The collection redefines Patek Philippe's relationship with its female clients, offering an easy-to-wear jewelry watch that balances modern and vintage appeal. Set with hundreds of diamonds and offered in white and rose gold cases, the Gondolo watches are rich in detail but free of excess, the perfect accompaniment to a woman’s everyday wardrobe.

JW Anderson x Ugg

Thanks to Ugg and JW Anderson, you won’t have to choose between warmth and style this winter. The two brands have come together to present two of Ugg’s iconic styles—the Classic Boot and Tasman—with a JW Anderson loafer twist. The shoes were designed around JW Anderson’s signature shoe style, and the result toes the line between comfort and class. Motifs from both brands can be seen in the offerings, with JWA’s construction and Ugg’s signature materials both on display.

“Uggs are instantly recognizable, and I was interested in seeing something so familiar through the lens of JW Anderson,” Jonathan Anderson said. “For me, collaboration is about experimentation, bringing two distinct points of view together and seeing where that leads. We’ve explored the loafer extensively at JW Anderson, not only as footwear but also through its details applied to bags and ready-to-wear. I wanted to see how that language could translate into Ugg.”

The offerings are unisex and available in three colorways selected by Anderson: chestnut, khaki, and orange. They are available for purchase in stores and at jwanderson.com and ugg.com beginning October 15.

Christie’s and Boucheron’s Ode to Jewels

The storied jewelry brand Boucheron was founded nearly 100 years after Christie’s held its first auction in 1766. Despite the age gap, however, the two companies both hold rich histories and a sense of legacy within their respective industries. So it only makes sense for them to partner up on a new project—an exhibition created in collaboration between Boucheron and Christie’s called Boucheron: In Focus—A Monograph of a Visionary. On view in New York City from October 9 to 18, the show features over 80 creations drawn from the jewelry house’s heritage, past, and present. In Focus is divided into four sections that speak to Boucheron’s roots, codes, and inspiration: architecture, nature, couture, and innovation. Highlights include Human Being making its American debut, as well as the brand’s newest high jewelry Carte Blanche collection, which will be open to the public as well. “Our history with the United States goes back much further than our physical presence there,” Hélène Poulit-Duquesne, CEO of Maison Boucheron, said in a statement. “The first American clients appeared in Boucheron’s order books as early as 1865, and in 1903, Louis Boucheron opened an office in New York to maintain these close ties. And yet, it was only in 2024 that we opened our first American boutique, on Madison Avenue. This exhibition marks an important new milestone in our American journey.” For more information, click here.

Cartier’s Into the Wild Collection

Cartier is kicking off Tilda Swinton’s tenure as an ambassador for the high jewelry brand by making her the face of its newest collection. The Scottish actor models the over-the-top pieces of Cartier’s new Into the Wild offerings. Swinton shows off five creatures, whose stylized heads are rendered as extravagant rings, necklaces, bracelets, and earrings. A diamond-encrusted tiger gnaws at her finger, while an emerald-eye crocodile eats its tail as a bracelet clasp. The pieces toe the line between realism and abstraction. The animals’ likenesses are clear, but their bodies are distorted and graphic. The Cartier panther, for example, looks to have been stretched from its neck, elongated into a sleek bangle. Elsewhere, it perches on a clock face as the keeper of time. There is a whimsical beauty imbued in the collection, which is likely why Swinton, with her enigmatic grace, was chosen to represent it. She artfully crawls towards the camera like the crocodiles that adorn her neck and finger, embodying the strength of character and freedom of spirit exemplified by the jewels.

Moncler’s Re/Icons 2026 Collection

Moncler is revisiting four iconic styles from the brand’s past and reinterpreting them for a new era. Set around the theme of “Pioneers in Moncler with Extraordinary Dreams,” this year’s Re/Icons collection remains rooted in the mountains and Moncler’s pioneering foundation. Designs from as far back as the 1950s center the brand’s adventurous spirit and connection to iconism, cementing Moncler’s place in alpine history.

The collection features reimagined versions of the Karakorum, Verone, Himalaya, and Tibb. The Karakorum was originally designed in 1954 for Achille Compagnoni and Lino Lacedelli as part of the Italian expedition that achieved the first successful ascent of K2, the world’s second-highest mountain. Fast-forward a few decades for background on the Verone, which gained popularity in Italy in the ’80s when the puffer jacket became part of the metropolitan uniform. But this season, the Re/Icons collection expands beyond outerwear. For the first time, Moncler is also offering a collection of full looks, including windbreakers, T-shirts, pants, and skirts, as well as accessories. Cozy beanies and silk-twill foulards are available, as well as titanium and leather sunglasses inspired by vintage climbing goggles. Every individual piece is updated in a way that makes it feel relevant in the 21st century while maintaining its place in both mountaineering and fashion history.

Rob Roth’s Blondie T-Shirt

Artist and designer Rob Roth has launched a series of limited-edition, one-of-a-kind T-shirts at Dover Street Market New York. The first of the series features images of Debbie Harry, captured by Blondie cofounder Chris Stein. Roth reimagines the photographs through a collage-driven approach that blends art, photography, and fashion with a punk sensibility. The patch-working also acts as an homage to William S. Burroughs, a friend of both Stein’s and Harry’s. Burroughs was known for using “the cut-up method,” a technique in which he snipped and rearranged existing text to create unexpected combinations and meanings. In a similar vein, Roth has brought together two separate images to create a fresh composition: a reinterpretation of Stein’s photography through Roth’s distinct visual perspective. As Roth said in a statement, “Sometimes, you have to turn the frame upside-down.”

Roth sourced vintage T-shirts for the project, which he then sliced up and sewed together in new ways; this makes the garments another extension of the cut-up process. Each piece was finished with minimal embellishments and found objects. All of this means no two tops are alike. “This series of collectible, wearable art is a T-shirt lover’s dream,” said Harry. The shirts are available in limited quantities now at Dover Street Market New York. 

Banana Republic x La Ligne

Banana Republic and La Ligne have solved all your fall wardrobe worries. The two brands teamed on a 36-piece collection, which brings a fresh perspective to fall classics. The collaboration centers on functional pieces that can not only build upon each other, but also fit into an existing wardrobe. La Ligne’s three cofounders drew inspiration from the Banana Republic archives, reinterpreting many mainstay elements with contemporary proportions and a rich, fall-adjacent color palette. Of course, La Ligne’s signature stripes are present in an array of shirts, sweaters, and accessories. There is also an emphasis on outerwear, represented by a nubuck barn jacket, belted suede wrap coat, and cape trench. Finally, sweaters—a cornerstone of both brands—are plentiful, with offerings rendered in soft cashmere and chunky cotton. It’s all about the classics done right. The Banana Republic and La Ligne collection is available now at select Banana Republic stores and online at bananarepublic.com.

Givenchy By Sarah Burton’s Shark Pinch Boot

For fall/winter 2026, Sarah Burton reworked (and renamed) Givenchy’s iconic Shark Pinch Boot. The new design elongates the original, bringing it thigh-high, while added “pinch” hardware at the top hearkens back to accessories introduced in Burton’s first season with the brand. Still, the unmistakable boldness of the original shape remains at play. The boot simultaneously embraces the leg while creating a unique and sculptural silhouette. The style has already become a celeb favorite. Anya Taylor-Joy wore the footwear while promoting The Super Mario Galaxy Movie in March, and Ariana Grande donned a custom, embroidered pair on the opening night of her current tour. Finally, you can stick your feet in them, too. The Shark Pinch Boot in its many variations is available now in-store and online at givenchy.com.

Polo Ralph Lauren’s Polo Blaze Bag

Polo Ralph Lauren has launched a new bag just in time for fall. The Polo Blaze bag is named after the white marking on a horse’s face from the forehead to the nose. With sculptural lines and distinctive hardware, the piece represents a bold reimagining of equestrian spirit for the Polo Ralph Lauren woman. The bag is elevated yet effortless, crafted in moto-inspired leathers. The smaller top-handle option is prim and ladylike, while the wider, small-shoulder variety provides a bit of edge. The large shoulder version, finally, balances downtown edge with heritage elegance, providing a new, modern take on a work or travel tote. Omega Speedmaster 38mm Update

Omega is sharpening up its Speedmaster 38 mm with seven new references that bring the compact chronograph closer to the house’s iconic Moonwatch. The refresh swaps oval subdials for rounded ones, pares back the dial text, and adds a chunkier bezel and Moonwatch-style bracelet. The lineup ranges from classic black-on-steel to icy blue, mother-of-pearl, and two-tone gold versions, with two diamond-set options for a little extra flash. Consider it a cleaner, more polished take on one of watchmaking’s most recognizable silhouettes. For more info visit omegawatches.com.

Dilara Findikoglu’s Bridal Capsule

Alt brides, rejoice. Dilara Findikoglu has released her first-ever bridal capsule. The wedding-ready pieces fit seamlessly in Findikoglu’s Victorian-inspired oeuvre, with the lingerie-adjacent designs mirroring existing signatures from the designer’s collection. Never one to follow rules, Findikoglu said she wanted to take part in the ritual of weddings, but aimed to do so in her own way. The result is a collection comprised of just eight ruffle- and ribbon-covered pieces. There’s a lace-up mini dress, honeymoon-worthy bra-and-panties set, and a sophisticated, tailored look perfect for the courthouse bride. A pink mesh dress adds a girlish touch—ideal for those eschewing white—for the fashionable bridesmaid, while a classic corset can easily be recycled following the nuptials. The collection is available now on dilarafindikoglu.com.

Mikimoto x Chrome Hearts

Pearl jeweler Mikimoto and fashion label Chrome Hearts have reunited on another collaboration, two years after their first in 2024. Born from a shared appreciation for craftsmanship, individuality, and timeless design, the collection unites Mikimoto’s pearls with classic Chrome Hearts motifs and metalwork. The five pieces from the first collection, previously rendered in white gold, are now available in 22-karat gold hardware with Akoya pearls and natural diamonds. Two drop earrings, a bracelet, a safety-pin brooch, and a necklace offer traditional jewelry with an added edge, balancing refinement and rebellion in a collection that feels authentic to both brands. Mikimoto x Chrome Hearts is available exclusively at Chrome Hearts Aoyama; Mount Row in London; and the Mikimoto stores in Ginza, New York, and Hong Kong. Also, for a limited time, well-heeled shoppers can peruse the goods via private appointment at Chrome Hearts Cannes and St. Barths.

Hailey Bieber x Gap

Now you don’t have to dig through secondhand bins to mimic Hailey Bieber’s laid-back denim style. Any fan of the model knows she loves a vintage Gap jean, and she has officially teamed up with the clothing brand to make her favorite, effortless styles available to all. Introducing: The Hailey Jean, a limited-edition denim capsule that reimagines Gap’s designs through Bieber’s lens. The line is inspired by that effortless ’90s look, as well as the Gap silhouettes Bieber champions in her day-to-day life: the Extra Baggy and Low Rise Loose. Updated fit proportions usher the pieces into the 21st century, while six custom washes allow for an array of styling options. Bieber’s personalization of the jeans continues with the addition of a “1996” design detail referencing Bieber’s birth year, and the model’s signature printed inside the pocket lining. “Gap has been a part of my wardrobe since I was a kid, so this came together very organically,” the model said in a statement. “Nineteen-ninety-six was the year I was born and I get a lot of style inspiration from the ’90s because there was something so effortless about that era and the way people wore denim.” The Hailey Jean launches on July 16 online and in select Gap stores.

Gu Fall/Winter 2026

Former creative director of Marni, Francesco Risso, is going accessible. The designer just released the fall 2026 collection for Gu, his first as the creative director of the Uniqlo sister brand. The collection marks a turning point for the label, introducing a new design approach built around six lifestyle concepts. Together, these wardrobes—minimal, classic, playful, utility, sport, and cozy —represent the way people live today. Each one outfits a specific character, while encouraging combination in order to create the perfect personal style. The classic line features nostalgic, ’70s-inspired pieces, reinterpreted through a modern lens, while the playful offerings introduce colors and patterns that allow for radical expression. Among all of the pieces, there is truly something for everyone.

“What interests me most about clothing is its ability to accompany life,” Risso said in a statement. “The wardrobe of today needs to feel grounded and accessible, yet also leave space for imagination, individuality, and play. The six lifestyle concepts are an attempt to reflect that reality; everyday dressing can be both practical and expressive, familiar and surprising.” The collection has already started to roll out, and will be available in full in stores and on gu-global.com on July 24.

Pandora Wonders

Pandora is launching a new multiyear creative platform, Pandora Wonders, which will explore a distinct material annually. Up first, freshwater pearls, placed front and center in a whimsical collection co–created by British stylist Harry Lambert. The charms take on the shapes of ice cream cones, mushrooms, squids, and more, all rendered with one-of-a-kind freshwater baroque pearls. That makes each piece a collector’s item, as no two pearls are the exact same. They were chosen distinctly for their shape—because they resembled the body of a rocket ship or the head of a mouse—and are finished with 14-karat gold-plated details and crystals for added sparkle. “I’m such a fan of pearls, so I’m thrilled to bring a renewed sense of childlike delight and nostalgia to Pandora’s unique world of charms,” Lambert said in a statement. Per usual with Pandora, the charms can be worn in a multitude of ways: on necklaces, bracelets, hooked onto hoop earrings, and more. Pandora Wonders will be available in select stores and online at Pandora.net on July 9, 2026.

Birkenstock x Repetto

Balletcore and gorpcore unite in one of the most unexpected footwear collaborations of the summer. Beloved French shoe brand Repetto is transforming classic Birkenstock silhouettes that scream more girly girl than outdoorswoman. Think the classic Boston sandal with its rounded toe, but this time topped with a little bow and finished off with a satin ribbon to be tied up the ankle and calf. Moncler is sealing its latest collaboration with a kiss. Or rather, multiple kisses. The outerwear brand is celebrating its first collaboration with Rick Owens with a campaign shot by Juergen Teller. In the set of six images, Owens, Teller, and their respective wives and creative partners, Michèle Lamy and Dovile Drizyte, trade smooches while dressed head-to-toe in the collection.

While Moncler is known mostly for its winterwear, this collaboration offers more lightweight, warm-weather options. The looks are inspired by Berlin’s brutalist architecture, as well as the city’s natural spaces, where those hulking buildings meet bucolic greenery. (Owens calls it “brucolic.”) Each garment, therefore, can take the wearer from the city streets straight to the great outdoors. An adjustable jersey skirt and nappa leather bomber may lean more toward a more cosmopolitan air, while Trailgrip Megalace sneakers and a cropped, funnel-neck down jacket are begging to be taken on a hike. With a refined color palette of black, dark dust, vintage olive, and bold carnelian red, these pieces can be worn anywhere and feel completely at home. item.title: Anya Taylor-Joy's Best Red Carpet Moments Are Otherworldly
item.description: From A24 breakout star to Princess Peach, we're reminiscing on the actor's standout red carpet moments.
item.dc:creator: Maxine Wally
item.content:encoded:
The moment Anya Taylor-Joy stepped into the spotlight as the doe-eyed, porcelain star of The Witch, her unique look rendered her a standout beauty. And in addition to her one-of-a-kind facial features (which Taylor-Joy told W in a 2016 interview she “didn’t enjoy” and that she “stopped looking in mirrors for a very long time”), the Golden Globe-winning actress has a style that’s all her own.

Although she has her go-to codes (fluted sleeves, column gowns, sequins, and old Hollywood silhouettes), Taylor-Joy is a fashion dark horse—breaking out club-ready looks at Comic-Con one night, and a frilly frock the next. With every ensemble, the London native stays true to her whimsical, romantic inclinations. These days, when she’s not wearing Dior, she’s dipping into exclusive fashion archives from the likes of Pierre Cardin and Thierry Mugler. The actress loves dressing to the theme of her films almost as much as she loves a couture moment, and the result is almost a decade of red carpet showstoppers. Here, take a look back at some of Taylor-Joy’s best style moments from 2015 to now.

2026: LACMA Art + Film Gala

She looked like a sci-fi bride in a rippling ivory cape look from Pierre Cardin’s spring 1997 couture collection.

2026: Dior Show

Dior’s trailing sheer shawl and matching lace choker provided just the right amount of gothic romance.

2026: Lucky Los Angeles Premiere

For the premiere of her Apple TV show, she embraced champagne dressing in an asymmetrical ivory gown from Dior’s cruise 2027 collection.

2026: Dior Cruise Show

With a ruffle-adorned halter neck, a midriff cutout, and a frothy bubble skirt, this black Dior dress was moody and romantic all at once.

2026: Vanity Fair Oscar Party

The star dipped into John Galliano’s fall 1994 archives for a dancer-inspired take on no-pants dressing.

2026: The Super Mario Galaxy Movie Tokyo Premiere

Princess Peach got an upgrade, Jonathan Anderson style, in this mini dress from Dior’s spring 2026 couture collection.

2025: Marrakech International Film Festival

This gauzy slip, from Tom Ford by Haider Ackermann, upped the ante on sheer dressing.

2025: Governors Awards

Taylor-Joy looked like a moulded sculpture in a figure-hugging Maison Margiela gown and Tiffany & Co. jewels.

2025: TIFF

At the premiere of Sacrifice, Taylor-Joy reimagined the princess aesthetic in a folded Cinderella gown, courtesy of Jonathan Anderson’s Dior.

2025: Tiffany & Co. Blue Book Gala

Taylor-Joy delivered Old Hollywood glamour in a John Galliano-era Dior dress. She finished with brilliant Tiffany jewels, of course.

2025: The Gorge Premiere

The actor looked ready for take off at The Gorge premiere in a Dior mini dress fashioned with pleated wings.

2025: SNL50 Anniversary

Rare, archival pieces are a staple of Taylor-Joy’s red carpet style. The actor proved this at an SNL event in 2025 where she wore a fall 1995 Thierry Mugler look that was originally modeled by Kate Moss.

2025: Golden Globes

Pastel and sparkle were the prompts for Taylor-Joy at the 2025 Golden Globes. Her blush-pink slip dress and matching shawl came from the Christian Dior archives, while her jewels were from Tiffany & Co.

2024: Dior Cruise Show

Taylor-Joy is a patron saint of the no-pants trend, and here, she gave the look an equestrian twist in thigh-exposing stirrup-style tights.

2024: Cannes Film Festival

Forget themed dressing, Taylor-Joy was a true Dior princess at the 2024 Cannes premiere of her film, Furiosa.

2024: Furiosa Australia Premiere

The actor leaned into method dressing at the Furiosa premiere in Sydney. She wore a spiked mini dress and matching headpiece from Rabanne’s spring 1996 collection.

2024: CinemaCon

Tayloy-Joy offered her own interpretation of the LBD at CinemaCon, promoting her film, Furiosa, in a bondage-style dress from Ludovic de Saint Sernin’s fall 2024 collection, inspired by the late photographer Robert Mapplethorpe.

2024: Academy Awards

The Dior ambassador paid homage to the house’s iconic archives, attending the 2024 Oscars in a modern take on Christian Dior’s Venus dress from the designer’s fall 1949 collection. It was Maria Grazia Chiuri who designed this version, which featured a more streamlined skirt and a gray color scheme.

2024: Vanity Fair Oscar Party

Taylor-Joy later ditched the Venus redux for a more appropriate after-party option in the form of a Miss Sohee LBD, inspired by a look from the brand’s fall 2021 collection.

2024: Dune: Part 2 New York Premiere

The actress was one of the first to bring John Galliano’s celebrated spring 2024 couture collection for Maison Margiela to the red carpet.

2024: Dune: Part 2 World Premiere

Taylor-Joy shocked fans when she appeared at the Dune: Part 2 premiere in a dramatic white Dior gown, inspired by Marc Bohan’s work for the house’s spring 1961 couture collection. Up until that point, most didn’t know to expect the actress in the popular sci-fi sequel.

2023: Tiffany & Co.’s The Landmark Reopening

Though Taylor-Joy wasn’t attending a premiere or award show, she still pulled out all the stops for the opening of Tiffany & Co.’s flagship store, attending the event in a structured, red feather dress from Dilara Fındıkoğlu’s spring 2023 collection. Of course, Tiffany jewels completed the look.

2023: The Super Mario Bros. Movie Premiere

Taylor-Joy really embraced the theme of The Super Mario Bros. Movie by arriving at the premiere in a bubblegum pink racing jumpsuit by Dior.

2023: BAFTA Film Awards

Taking a break from her usual Dior, Taylor-Joy attended the BAFTA Film Awards in a Schiaparelli spring 2023 haute couture look featuring a structured gold velvet mini dress with a matching, oversized stole.

2023: Critics’ Choice Awards

Taylor-Joy wore a sheer, nude Dior haute couture dress to the Critics Choice Awards in 2023.

2023: Golden Globe Awards

Taylor-Joy showed up to the 2023 Golden Globes, where she was nominated for The Menu, in a yellow two-piece number from her trusted label, Dior. The elegant column skirt, bold color, and straight blonde hair seemed to take a number out of the red carpet playbook of her The Northman co-star Nicole Kidman.

2022: The Menu New York Premiere

For The Menu’s second premiere, Taylor-Joy embraced her inner porcelain doll in a Dior spring 2023 floral mini dress with leather cut-out gloves.

2022: The Menu UK Premiere

Taylor-Joy attended the premiere of The Menu in London wearing a cobalt blue leather dress from Alexander McQueen’s spring 2023 collection featuring a corset top, gloves, and a dramatically asymmetric hem.

2022: The Northman Premiere

Taylor-Joy looked like an ice queen in this sleek Dior fall 2022 dress at The Northman premiere in April 2022.

2021: CFDA Fashion Awards

The Face of the Year recipient accepted her award in this custom Oscar de la Renta look that Fran Fine would have undoubtedly loved.

2021: Last Night in Soho Premiere

Taylor-Joy embraced ‘70s glamour in this Dior gown for the Last Night in Soho premiere.

2021: Emmy Awards

For the 2021 Emmys, Taylor-Joy once again tapped Dior to create this buttery yellow confection.

2021: Venice International Film Festival

No, that’s not Barbie, that’s Taylor-Joy in a bright-pink Dior Haute Couture look at the Venice Film Festival.

2021: SAG Awards

Taylor-Joy wore Vera Wang and Tiffany & Co. for 2021’s SAG Awards.

2021: Critics’ Choice Awards

For the remote Critics Choice Awards, Taylor-Joy chose Dior Haute Couture.

2021: Golden Globe Awards

Law Roach chose this emerald green Dior look for the Golden Globes.

2020: Emma Premiere

For the Los Angeles premiere of Emma, the star wore a vintage Bob Mackie wedding dress.

2019: London Critics’ Circle Choice Awards

Taylor-Joy played up the romance in this beautifully drapped Vivienne Westwood couture dress.

2019: Glass New York Premiere

It’s rare to see Anya Taylor-Joy in suiting, but the actress put her own twist on this gold brocade Dolce & Gabbana jacket and slacks by pairing it with a dark lip and sideswept waves.

2019: Glass London Premiere

This little black dress from Saint Laurent is pretty simple for Taylor-Joy, but she added her own unique touch with the headband placed across her forehead.

2018: Comic-Con

The actress opted for a nighttime ensemble from Armani—and a superlong ponytail—to attend the Glass and Halloween panels during Comic-Con International in 2018.

2018: Serpentine Summer Party

Taylor-Joy looks absolutely adorable in this Chanel spring 2018 tweed dress.

2018: Royal Academy of Arts Summer Exhibition Preview Party

Floral, feathers, and sequins came together beautifully in this Huishan Zhang dress.

2018: Met Gala

The actress took the Costume Institute Gala’s 2018 theme, “Heavenly Bodies: Fashion & The Catholic Imagination” to the nth degree with this Dolce & Gabbana look.

2018: TV Empire Awards

Mint green and sequins meets a classic Hollywood silhouette with this Elie Saab spring 2018 gown.

2018: BAFTA Awards

Once again, Taylor-Joy tapped Dolce & Gabbana to dress her, wearing this lace and tulle gown to the BAFTAs in 2018.

2018: BAFTA Nominees Party

Taylor-Joy clearly has a thing for Dolce & Gabbana, and this corseted tulle dress is quintessentially Anya.

2017: BFI London Film Festival

One thing about Taylor-Joy: she can’t stay away from a sequin, so this Dolce & Gabbana dress was an obvious choice.

2017: Cannes Film Festival

The actress wore a bell-sleeved Burberry gown to a screening of The Meyerowitz Stories.

2017: BAFTA Awards

The actress’s inclination toward a bell-sleeve gown appeared once more when she wore this tiered Gucci dress to the BAFTAs.

2017: Split Premiere

The whimsical astrological print on this Schiaparelli couture fall 2016 wide-leg jumpsuit is what really makes it a standout.

2016: Gotham Independent Film Awards

Never one to shy away from a print, the 25-year-old wore this Gucci dress—replete with images of pumpkins and cranes—to the IFP Awards in New York.

2016: Toronto International Film Festival

The rosebud shoulder pads are the real winners of this Dolce & Gabbana dress.

2016: The Witch Premiere

Taylor-Joy opted for this sky blue sheer Gucci dress for The Witch’s premiere.

2015: BFI London Film Festival

The assignment: column gowns. And Taylor-Joy understood it with this Prada dress.

2015: Toronto International Film Festival

Baby-faced Taylor-Joy chose this burgundy Prada gown for her first-ever premiere.

item.title: Hunter Schafer’s Y2K Prada Coat Is A Clear 'Blade Runner' Callback
item.description: A rare moment that can bring fashion nerds and sci-fi geeks together.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Vintage Prada is not only timeless; it’s downright futuristic. Just ask Hunter Schafer, whose Y2K-era coat fits right into the Blade Runner 2099 universe.

At a London photocall for the Prime Video series today, the actor served sci-fi aesthetics in a PVC rain jacket from Miuccia Prada’s fall 2002 runway. The outfit underneath was decidedly more au courant, featuring a turquoise bra and a wrap skirt fresh from the spring 2027 runway. It’s the second time Schafer has worn a look from that collection on this press tour. But it is the first time the Prada It girl has dipped into the house’s archives for such a spot-on—or shall we say, clear—reference.

The see-through jacket has become a style signature of the 1982 sci-fi epic. In one now-iconic scene from Ridley Scott’s film, Joanna Cassidy’s character, a replicant named Zhora Salome who works as an exotic dancer, quickly flees a nightclub to escape being caught by a replicant-killing blade runner. She throws on a see-through raincoat over her underwear and runs through the pouring L.A. streets. It’s a fitting reference for Schafer, who plays an undercover human in the latest iteration, which finds replicants as the ruling class, and humans being hunted.

While this fashion callback is the most transparent, the 27-year-old star has been serving a steady stream of sci-fi method dressing in recent weeks. On Tuesday, she wore a futuristic wedding-gown-meets-tuxedo from Celine. Last week, she channeled Sean Young’s Rachael in a luxe brown Prada coat. The show premieres on November 25, so we can only hope the world-building references continue. Next up, might we suggest a recreation of this sheer Daryl Hannah bodysuit?

item.title: Alex Consani’s Couture Seatbelt Dress Is 'Grand Theft Auto' Appropriate
item.description: The supermodel wore an automobile-derived outfit to mark her next career move.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Alex Consani is buckling up for her next career move. The supermodel appears in Grand Theft Auto VI, and she has just the automobile-adjacent outfit to celebrate.

Styled by Jack Novotny, Consani strapped into a couture seatbelt dress for the video game’s launch party at Gekko restaurant in Miami. The design, from Paris-based label Sevali’s spring 2025 show, is made entirely of upcycled vehicle safety straps. Comprising various shades of charcoal, blue, and off-white, the pieced-together frock chaotically contours the body, with errant polyester straps hanging down and slices of skin on display. At the top, a bulky black buckle sits across the décolletage, giving the strapless silhouette a sturdy spin.

Sevali has become a go-to for subversive It-girl statements, from Charli xcx’s tattered sequin top on the Music, Fashion, Film tour to Kylie Jenner’s shimmering chainmail hood. For Consani, who recently made her acting debut in American Horror Story: 13, the archival pull is a highly respectable form of GTA method dressing.

Consani is an in-game radio host in the sixth iteration of the iconic franchise, joining a list of A-listers including Kyle MacLachlan, Blondie’s Debbie Harry, Samuel L. Jackson, and Karl Lagerfeld who have made GTA cameos over the years. Released on November 19, GTA VI marks the game’s first installment in 13 years. It’s once again jam-packed with celebrity DJs delivering song intros, quippy jokes, and on-the-go commentary as players cruise through the streets.

For her part, Consani hosts “Flash FM” alongside Robyn, a station that plays Charli xcx, MGTM, and Zara Larsson. Other radio hosts of GTA VI include Lana Del Rey, Burna Boy, Bad Bunny, and Miami native JT—who Consani sat with courtside at a Miami Heat game earlier in the day. Though that outfit was not safety-belt-derived, it was bra-forward and brimming with risqué skin-baring. Which is no surprise. Style-wise, Consani stays in the driver’s seat.

item.title: Simone Ashley's Y2K Galliano Dress Glows Like a Fashion Sunset
item.description: The 'Bridgerton' star stepped out in a slinky bias-cut slip from the legendary designer's namesake label.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
Simone Ashley is not just an actor. She’s also a singer, an environmental advocate, and a certified vintage fashion nerd. Naturally, a special trip to Mumbai, India, this week called for a dip into some highly exclusive runway archives.

Attending Vogue India’s Forces of Fashion awards yesterday, Ashley slipped into a silk dress from John Galliano’s spring 2001 collection. Sourced from Epoque Couture, the slinky number had a gradient sherbet palette, featuring diagonal panels of metallic pinks and yellows that wrapped around the body in Galliano’s signature bias-cut style. After first experimenting with the draping technique as a student at Central Saint Martins, the bias-cut became a staple of Galliano’s namesake collections in the 1990s and 2000s, and was incorporated into his work at Dior. Though this dress is from his 2001 archives, a pink version of it was first presented on his provocative spring 1995 runway. It was one of the most celebrated shows of his career, presented just a year before Ashley was born.

Its a fitting pick for the 31-year-old star, who accepted the Global Impact award at the Vogue event. She proved her love for vintage pieces on her press tour for The Devil Wears Prada 2 earlier this year, where she wore everything from Nicolas Ghesquière-era Balenciaga to flashy ’80s Mugler.

While she’s not currently on a press tour (Bridgerton season 5 comes out next year), the South Indian actor has certainly been on a fashion-filled jaunt while overseas. On Tuesday, she performed at Prince William’s environmental Earthshot Prize Awards in a showstopping custom design by Swadesh and Manish Malhotra. Performing a rendition of Nelly Furtado’s “I’m Like a Bird” on stage, Ashley glistened in the intricately beaded two-piece set. Before that, she coordinated with Kate Middleton in blue knit separates with crystal embellishments.

While her Galliano slip was free of sequins and shine, it still packed a sartorial punch. In the already-impressive Simone Ashley repertoire of vintage pulls, her latest Y2K dress makes for a decidedly special addition.

item.title: Morgan Maher Goes Hollywood With 'Everybody Loved Her, Everybody Wanted Her'
item.description: With a new book, the It-girl shooter trains her lens on Clairo, Rachel Sennott, Emily Ratajkowski—and the mythology of the movie star.
item.dc:creator: Claire Valentine
item.content:encoded:
There’s a reason why Morgan Maher has become the go-to photographer for It girls everywhere. Her 2023 debut book, Girls in Bed, took a tired trope and turned it into something new—through her lens, an intimate shoot with a subject in her most private space, her bed, becomes a setting for self-authorship and a playful exploration of femininity, rather than an exercise in exploitation or voyeurism.

For her second photo book, Everybody Loved Her, Everybody Wanted Her, a 350-page glossy tome in print by Friend Editions, the Maryland-born photographer shifts that setting to the rooms, pools, and sets of Hollywood. She keeps her subjects—the models include a cast of Maher’s friends and frequent collaborators, like Rachel Sennott, Emily Ratajkowski, JT, True Whitaker, and Clairo—but places them in the usually New York-based Maher’s new home of Los Angeles.

“I became fascinated with the concept of who the modern Hollywood woman is,” Maher, 31, told W ahead of her book’s publication. “How do you preserve the heart of girlhood within this mythology?”

Maher tried to answer that question, in part, by switching up her own process, working with a bigger crew than she was used to, using continuous film lighting, and using French Aaton motion picture cameras loaded with 16mm film for the first time. “It still felt like it was just me and her and my small camera,” she says. But the change in medium made the shoots feel more like film sets. “There’s a different way talent reacts to a flash or the sound of a shutter, versus the way they’re moving,” she added. “You can get those in-between moments.”

Movies are a relatively new fascination for Maher. “I was a fashion girlie before that,” she said. She worked at Marc Jacobs and spent about three years assisting the casting director, Anita Bitton, until her own photography took off. Recently, she fell for the screen tests for Paul Thomas Anderson’s Phantom Thread, which she found on YouTube. “In some of the camera tests, they’re not even in makeup or hair,” she said of her inspiration.

Most of the book’s subjects are longtime friends, and that ease and familiarity shows up in the photos. “I would never want a girl to do something that I wouldn’t do or that she doesn’t feel comfortable with,” Maher said. The photos capture a fantasy, from the lights to the hair and makeup; Maher wanted every model to feel like “an exciting version of themselves that they don’t get to be every day.” Subjects like Matilde Lucidi even invented character names for themselves for the shoots. “I always want to make a woman look beautiful,” Maher said. “I never want to make them in an uncomfortable position or an unflattering angle.” The result, she said, “feels a bit girl next door, but so heightened at the same time.”

The moving image may be where Maher is headed next. When she cut a short vignette for each woman from their shoot’s footage, nearly every one of them posted the video rather than the stills. Asked whether she’d like to make a film, Maher doesn’t hesitate. “Yes, I want to make a movie. I just need to write it all down.”

item.title: Kylie Jenner & Timothée Chalamet Are Back With Courtside Couple Style
item.description: The PDA-loving pair resumed their rightful place on the sidelines of a basketball game.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
The downside to the New York Knicks winning the NBA Finals in June is that we’ve had to endure a long, long summer not seeing Timothée Chalamet and Kylie Jenner sitting courtside. When might the PDA-loving, Chrome-Hearts-wearing couple resume their rightful place on the sidelines of a basketball game? Thankfully, last night, equilibrium was restored when the A-list pair enjoyed a romantic date night at a Los Angeles Lakers game.

Supporting Jenner’s home team against the Utah Jazz at Crypto.com Arena (yes), the couple was in their finest courtside form. As she is wont to do, Jenner slipped in some subtle promo for her brand Khy in a plunging leather jacket, which she paired with straight-leg jeans and shimmering strappy heels. Chalamet matched her palette in pooling leather slacks and a gorpy Adidas jacket. As they smooched, gossiped, and exchanged knowing glances, the pair solidified their place as the reigning sports-loving couple of 2026.

Though the pair is otherwise relatively press-shy (just ask Vanity Fair about that), they have no problem sitting front row together, serving major style moments with each appearance, from coordinating Chrome Hearts outfits to satisfying black-and-white contrast. Until last night, they had been on a months-long break from sports showmanship, instead enjoying high-profile date nights in Hollywood. Just last weekend, Jenner joined Chalamet at the 2026 Governors Awards, wearing a butter-yellow vintage Robert Cavalli gown. Though she skipped the red carpet, inside the event, the pair were seen canoodling over cocktails and canapés.

At this point, however, awards-season schmoozing is almost expected from the couple. A casual courtside date, on the other hand, offers a slice-of-life glimpse at their headline-worthy relationship. What lemony drink is Jenner enjoying? Who are they so cheekily whispering about? Did Chalamet take this video of his girlfriend with the Lakers cheerleaders? These are the details we need to know.

item.title: Kate Madden, Nicole Richie's Daughter, Enters the Spotlight With Balenciaga
item.description: The 18-year-old makes her modeling debut—and follows in her mom’s footsteps—in the Le City bag’s 25th anniversary campaign.
item.dc:creator: Carolyn Twersky Winkler
item.content:encoded:
Kate Madden, daughter of Y2K icons Nicole Richie and Joel Madden, is ready to introduce herself to the world. And what better way to do so than with a Balenciaga Le City Bag bag campaign? Twenty-five years ago, Richie helped turn the accessory into one of the era’s defining It bags. Now, mother and daughter have both been tapped to star in its anniversary campaign, making the moment less a passing of the torch than a shared family affair.

“I’ve wanted to model since I was young, but I felt like, now that I’m 18, and I have a very specific look, it’s the perfect time for me to start,” Madden told W ahead of the campaign launch. That look includes recently dyed black hair in place of her natural blonde, giving her style a darker, goth-inflected edge. Along with Madden’s large, captivating eyes—which have already drawn comparisons online to Tim Burton characters—the transformation is on full display in the campaign.

The Le City itself dates back to 2001, when Nicolas Ghesquière bucked the era’s prevailing logomania with a design inspired by the classic motorcycle jacket. Its supple lambskin body, metal buckles, and long leather laces quickly caught the eye of early-aughts style—and tabloid—fixtures, Richie among them.

For Madden, the bag has simply always been around. Growing up with a fashion-designer mother and a musician father has clearly shaped her aesthetic, which lands somewhere between the feminine eclecticism of Richie’s House of Harlow and the rock-forward attitude of Good Charlotte. Below, Madden talks about how her parents influence her style, raiding her mother’s closet, her makeup secrets, and career ambitions.

How would you describe your style?

I wear a lot of vintage stuff—a lot of black and pink. I love being girlie, but I also love to dress in darker pieces.

That really seems like an amalgamation of both your parents’ styles. Do they inspire you?

I would definitely say they influence my style. My dad basically only wears black, and I love to wear black. And then I take inspiration from my mom’s style when she was younger.

Do you shop your mom’s closet a lot?

Yeah, I’m always borrowing my mom’s stuff. It’s literally amazing. She’s so nice about letting me borrow whatever I want. Sometimes, she borrows things from me too.

What is the best style advice you’ve gotten from your parents?

They tell me to just be myself with my style. I love unique stuff, so they tell me to wear what I want. They’re always very supportive of whatever I want to wear.

Have you watched A Simple Life?

I haven’t. I guess I haven’t thought about watching it, but I see clips on TikTok. I don’t know, maybe I’ll watch it eventually.

Let’s discuss your makeup, because your big, bold eyes are so unique. I’ve seen people online say that you look like a Tim Burton character. What do you think about that comparison?

It’s the best thing ever. I love hearing that. I grew up as a dancer, so I learned how to do my makeup and my hair at a young age. I mostly focus on my eye makeup because I already have big eyes, so I try to accentuate them as much as possible.

How do you achieve the doe-eyed look? Do you use white eyeliner?

I don’t. My eyes just look like that. But I do wear fake eyelashes and dark eyeshadow.

Let’s talk about Balenciaga. How many Le City bags do you and your mom own? Do you have a favorite?

I have no clue how many my mom owns. I borrow hers a lot, but I have three of my own right now. I love my white one. It goes with everything and I basically wear it every day. It works when you’re trying to dress more fancy, but also when you’re trying to be casual.

What does it mean to be in this campaign with your mom, and to represent a bag she helped make famous?

It was so fun to do it with my mom. It was good for me to do my first campaign with her because I had someone who has more experience helping me through it.

What’s next for you?

I definitely want to keep modeling, and eventually I want to start acting.

Who do you look up to in those industries?

In the modeling industry, I definitely look up to Amelia Gray and Gabbriette.

item.title: Hailey Bieber Recreates One of Carolyn Bessette Kennedy's Best Looks
item.description: At the DealBook Summit in New York City, the Rhode founder evoked a modern-day CBK in a vintage Yohji Yamamoto blazer.
item.dc:creator: Natalie Michie
item.content:encoded:
There’s been no shortage of Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy references over the past year, but Hailey Bieber’s latest look might be the most impressive yet.

On Wednesday, the Rhode founder took the stage at the New York Times DealBook Summit in a vintage Yohji Yamamoto blazer that looked identical to the one owned by CBK. The tightly-buttoned black jacket, from the brand’s spring 1998 collection, features a mock-neck silhouette and a subtle peplum flare. Bessette first wore it to the Robin Hood Foundation Benefit with JFK Jr. in 1998. For her take, Bieber kept the white pencil skirt the same, but updated the vibe with glossy black pumps and a ’90s-style headband, though thinner than Bessette-Kennedy’s favored C.O. Bigelow accessory.

At the annual DealBook Summit, which gathers industry leaders in commerce, government, tech, and culture, Bieber sat down with journalist Andrew Ross Sorkin to talk mental health, social media, and selling Rhode to e.l.f. Beauty for $1 billion. The 29-year-old model was something of an outlier among the program’s guests, which also included Elon Musk, Zohran Mamdani, and Sam Altman. After all, she’s certainly the only one who can pull off a niche ’90s It girl reference and talk billion-dollar acquisitions. Along with getting some backstage support from her husband Justin, having the perfect power dressing ensemble was key to success, and for Bieber, that of course meant a spot-on CBK recreation.

It’s been a fashion-filled, Rhode-focused few days for the star, who, just yesterday, accepted the Brand of the Year award at WWD’s Beauty Inc Awards. For that appearance, she did not go archival, but instead wore a fresh-off-the-runway slip from Calvin Klein—which is, famously, Bessette’s former place of work. Looking back, perhaps it was a chic little hint at the iconic recreation look to come.
